The Machinery Regulation lists safety components with fully or partly self-evolving behavior using machine learning to perform safety functions in Annex I Part A, and its recitals say a third party should assess them. Judge support in the policy's input representation and in physical operating variables, where a camera or control-rate change can outweigh the task label. ## Four ways to remain close to evidence

Offline-RL methods differ in how they keep improvement away from unsupported values, and Park and colleagues find the policy-extraction step often matters more than the value objective <Cite id="park-bottleneck-2024" />.

### Conservative value estimation

Conservative Q-Learning penalizes high values on actions outside the dataset while preserving observed ones <Cite id="cql-2020" />. RankQ's authors argue that such pessimism anchors policies to suboptimal data, and their action ranking raised a VLA's real cube-stacking success from 43.1% to 88.9% <Cite id="rankq-2026" />.

### Avoiding unseen-action queries

Implicit Q-Learning fits a state value by expectile regression over dataset actions and extracts a policy by advantage weighting, so value fitting never queries a new action <Cite id="iql-2022" />. For action-chunking VLAs, CO-RFT extends temporal-difference learning to chunks after an imitation-learning initialization <Cite id="co-rft-2025" />.

### Regularizing the policy toward behavior

TD3+BC adds a cloning term and state normalization to an off-policy actor-critic and matches more elaborate algorithms <Cite id="td3-bc-2021" />. Flow Q-Learning trains a one-step actor alongside an expressive flow policy, avoiding iterative action generation during deployment <Cite id="flow-q-learning-2025" />.

### Discretizing and scaling the value function

QT-Opt trained a Q-function on over 580,000 real grasp attempts and reached 96% success on unseen objects <Cite id="qt-opt-2018" />. Q-Transformer discretizes each action dimension and represents its Q-value as a separate token for autoregressive offline value learning <Cite id="q-transformer-2023" />. With datasets up to 1000 times the usual size, many offline RL algorithms still saturate well short of maximum performance, and long horizons form a fundamental barrier <Cite id="horizon-reduction-2025" />.

## When behavior cloning is the better tool

Behavior cloning is the default for clean expert demonstrations: it fits the action labels and has no bootstrapped critic. Robomimic found recurrent cloning a strong baseline on human demonstrations, where batch-RL methods struggled <Cite id="robomimic-2021" />, and Kumar and colleagues favor offline RL for sparse rewards, suboptimal or noisy data, and long horizons with composable trajectories <Cite id="offline-rl-vs-bc-2022" />.

## A six-step evaluation protocol

Do not choose checkpoints by the Q-values they maximize. Paine and colleagues found offline RL algorithms not robust to hyperparameters, yet able to rank policies reliably once the algorithm and Q-estimation method are controlled <Cite id="paine-hparam-2020" />.

### 1. Lock the data split by deployment factor

Hold out environments, objects, operators or periods to match the intended generalization; random transition splits leak adjacent frames. Kumar and colleagues adapt cross-validation to tune offline RL without online evaluation <Cite id="offline-rl-workflow-2021" />.

### 2. Establish three baselines

Use cloning, a recurrent cloner when history matters, and the simplest regularized offline-RL method. RvS's conditioned two-layer MLP competes with TD and transformer methods but is weak on random data <Cite id="rvs-2021" />.

### 3. Report support-aware diagnostics

Report action distance from the data, critic disagreement, saturation rate and per-source performance; EDAC, for one, penalizes out-of-distribution actions through Q-ensemble uncertainty <Cite id="edac-2021" />.

### 4. Use simulation only where it is predictive

Simulation ranks close checkpoints only where its link to hardware is measured, as SIMPLER did with paired real evaluations <Cite id="simpler-2024" />. SCORE limits simulated RL to the support of a real-data policy, raising eight real dexterous tasks from 37.8% to 89.9% average success, against 59.5% for the best baseline <Cite id="score-2026" />.

<Image id="simpler-visual-matching-2024" />

### 5. Run blinded physical trials

Fix the protocol before policy identities are known, randomize conditions, and count interventions, collisions and resets, as TRI did <Cite id="tri-lbm-2025" />.

### 6. Keep a fixed canary set

Run one repeatable physical suite for every candidate and keep the episode IDs; the TriFinger benchmark offers a reproducible real-hardware setup <Cite id="trifinger-offline-2023" />.

## From a fixed dataset to controlled online improvement

RLPD mixes offline data into off-policy online learning without separate conservative pretraining <Cite id="rlpd-2023" />. Conservative critics fine-tune poorly, so Cal-QL calibrates CQL with a one-line change and leads on 9 of 11 benchmarks <Cite id="cal-ql-2023" />. Retaining offline data in replay is a safe default, though WSRL shows it is unnecessary with a well-designed online method <Cite id="wsrl-2024" />. A separate study finds naive Q-function pretraining often offers little benefit over random initialization when fine-tuning a pretrained policy <Cite id="dong-q-pretrain-2026" />.

Ishir Garg, Benjamin Eysenbach, Sergey Levine and colleagues at UC Berkeley and Princeton (October 2026) use prior data to decide where to explore: they estimate empowerment, a measure of how many future states an agent can reach from a state, from unlabeled offline trajectories without any environment interaction <Cite id="offline-empowerment-2026" />. Used as an exploration bonus for online goal-conditioned contrastive RL, it sped up learning and raised success on five of the OGBench task and dataset pairs and matched the baseline on the rest, over 5 seeds; every test ran in simulation <Cite id="offline-empowerment-2026" />.

Keep action bounds and command validation outside the learned policy, define interventions and resets, and compare each promotion with the frozen offline checkpoint. PA-RL fine-tuned the 7B OpenVLA with Cal-QL from 40% to 70% real-world success in 40 minutes <Cite id="pa-rl-2024" />. Q2RL uses a few interactions to extract values from a behavior-cloned policy, then gates between cloning and RL actions <Cite id="q2rl-2026" />.

LWD applies offline-to-online RL to a pretrained VLA across a fleet of 16 dual-arm robots and reports 95% average success over eight tasks <Cite id="lwd-2026" />. BORA keeps its VLA base frozen and updates a lightweight residual actor from online rollouts, corrections and offline data <Cite id="bora-2026" />. The [RL fine-tuning guide](/manipulation/rl-finetuning) covers this phase.

<RealRobotRlGains className="my-6" />

## A compact go/no-go checklist

Run an offline-RL experiment only when actions, rewards, terminations and timing are trustworthy, the data holds behavior that cloning should not imitate uniformly, and deployment lies inside the data's support, since generalization to out-of-support states is often a big barrier <Cite id="park-bottleneck-2024" />.

edits.before: ## The 2021 break: physics moved onto the GPU Isaac Gym kept physics and policy training on one GPU, passing PhysX buffers straight to PyTorch tensors without CPU round trips. Its authors report 2 to 3 orders of magnitude improvement over a CPU simulator feeding a GPU network . Rudin and colleagues scaled from 128 robots, typical of CPU implementations, to 16,384 on one workstation GPU. Flat terrain took under four minutes and uneven terrain twenty. Their deployment policy used 4,096 robots, 98,304-transition batches (24 steps per robot) and 1,500 updates in under 20 minutes on an i9-11900k CPU and RTX A6000 GPU . Zoom out in the figure below to see thousands of copies of one robot practise at once, then shuffle their worlds. Their game-inspired curriculum promotes robots that cross their tile, demotes those covering under half the commanded distance, and loops hardest-level solvers back to a random level, and in this massively parallel regime their PPO bootstraps the critic at time-outs . MuJoCo XLA (MJX) moved MuJoCo onto the GPU, and MuJoCo Playground (2025) built on it an open framework for quadrupeds, humanoids, hands and arms, aimed at sim-to-real transfer . edits.before: ## What the environment count actually buys The opening scene is an illustrative calculation: a fixed 220-million-transition budget, an assumed CPU-cost curve that raises per-iteration costs, and a calibrated near-four-minute time at 4,096 environments. Only Rudin's separate deployment run ties 4,096 robots to a reported bound . The curve reflects a bottleneck the Isaac Lab paper reports: on a state-based Franka drawer task, an RTX 5090 workstation nearly matches a server with two RTX PRO 6000 GPUs and two 64-core EPYC 9554 CPUs, a task-dependent result the authors put down to CPU bottlenecks and the workstation's fast single core . Environment count also changes learning: at fixed batch size, more robots cut Rudin's training time but hurt the policy past a point . SAPG reports PPO saturating beyond a certain count , while Beukman and colleagues avoid plateaus with over 1M environments, improving monotonically to one trillion transitions . FastTD3 combines parallel simulation with large batches and a distributional critic to accelerate off-policy humanoid learning . ## Isaac Lab and the framework era Isaac Lab grew out of Orbit , a 2023 framework on Isaac Sim . Headless state-based training on RTX PRO 6000 GPUs scales "almost perfectly linearly". With eight GPUs and 16,384 environments, the DextrAH teacher grasp-and-lift task exceeds 900,000 FPS and Franka cabinet 1.6 million, counting environment steps over simulation plus learning time . NVIDIA's 2026 overview says Isaac Lab 3.0 splits backend code from the core API, so users choose Isaac Sim's PhysX and RTX for sensor-rich work or headless Newton for throughput . Isaac Lab 3.0 entered early access on 16 September 2026 . ## Newton: physics as a multi-solver library Newton, an open-source GPU physics engine co-developed by Disney Research, Google DeepMind and NVIDIA, joined the Linux Foundation on 29 September 2025 . It generalizes the deprecated `warp.sim` module of NVIDIA Warp and uses MuJoCo Warp as its primary backend . NVIDIA's 16 March 2026 post announced general availability of Newton 1.0 and called Isaac Sim 6.0 and Isaac Lab 3.0 early access releases ; Isaac Sim 6.1.0 and Newton v1.6.0 followed on 10 September 2026. Behind one API, NVIDIA's overview lists MuJoCo and Featherstone solvers in generalized coordinates, and SemiImplicit, XPBD and Kamino in maximal coordinates, while VBD (vertex block descent ) handles cloth and soft bodies and implicit MPM handles continuum materials . The post describes SDF collision from CAD meshes and Drake-inspired hydroelastic contact over finite-area patches, and its assembly example sets a plus or minus 10 mm sparse-SDF band . Isaac Sim 6.1 added hydroelastic contact, a pressure-field model , to its experimental Newton integration . NVIDIA reports that Skild AI trains GPU-rack-assembly RL policies, including connector insertion, with Isaac Lab's Newton backend, SDF and hydroelastic contact, and that Samsung "will use Newton" for synthetic VLA training data; its refrigerator example couples MuJoCo Warp two-way with a VBD cable solver for RB-Y1 cable insertion . It also reports MuJoCo 3.5 (MJWarp) speedups over MJX of 252x for locomotion and 475x for manipulation on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs, without stating task variants, environment counts, precision or timing definition . edits.before: ## The quadruped lineage Hwangbo and colleagues replaced simulated actuation with a learned network for ANYmal's series-elastic actuators, which predicts joint torque from current and past joint-position errors and velocities; policies trained with ideal or analytical actuator models failed to take a single step without falling. A separate recovery policy flipped ANYmal upright from nine tested configurations, after the authors relaxed joint-velocity constraints following the first hardware attempt . Lee and colleagues trained a privileged RL teacher to supervise the actions and latent features of a temporal convolutional student, which reads two seconds of proprioceptive history, plus the command and current state, with no terrain map. Trained on rigid procedural terrain, ANYmal-B and ANYmal-C controllers crossed mud, snow, rubble and vegetation without environment-specific tuning, though a robot commanded off a cliff will walk off it . RMA, a base policy plus an adaptation module, deployed on the A1 robot without any fine-tuning ; the [sim-to-real module](/rl-sim2real/sim2real-transfer) covers the distillation mechanics. Miki and colleagues fed elevation-map height samples and proprioception to a GRU belief encoder whose learned attention gate controls how much exteroception enters; the student imitates a privileged teacher and falls back on proprioception when sensors mislead. The Etzel hike covered 2.2 km and 120 m of climb in 78 minutes against a planner's 76, with no falls but stops to reattach a shoe and swap batteries, and the authors list possible falls at occluded cliffs or stepping stones . Agarwal and colleagues use a front-facing depth camera and policy memory to infer terrain beneath the hind feet . Rudin and colleagues trained flat-terrain walking in under four minutes on one workstation GPU. Their deployment policy used 4,096 ANYmal robots, batches of 98,304 transitions (24 steps per robot) and 1,500 updates in under twenty minutes, with a game-inspired terrain curriculum that promotes robots that cross a tile, demotes those that fall short and loops hardest-level solvers back to a random level . The released `legged_gym` repository (October 2021) is the Isaac Gym environment used to train ANYmal on rough terrain . ANYmal Parkour's high-level policy selects walking, jumping, climbing and crouching skills, crossing obstacles at up to two meters per second . With a cheap granular-media model in the training loop, Choi and colleagues' Raibo ran on beach sand at 3.03 m/s with feet fully buried . ## A gait is a timing pattern A gait is a footfall-timing pattern: each leg's phase offset in the stride and its duty factor $\beta$, the fraction of the cycle on the ground. Walk These Ways commands a gait as three timing offsets between foot pairs plus a stepping frequency: (0.5, 0, 0) trots, (0, 0.5, 0) bounds and (0, 0, 0) pronks . Push the dog and the humanoid in the figure below to see why fewer feet on the ground make balance harder. In the MIT Cheetah 2 design, Park, Wensing and Kim plan stance time from stride length and speed, $T_{st} = L/v_d$, keep swing duration fixed, and modulate duty cycle by vertical impulse scaling. Stride length grows with speed only up to 3 m/s, so this is one controller's schedule. Roll instability ended the 6.4 m/s top-speed treadmill run, and at the highest speeds the robot partly leaned on the side wall. The minimum cost of transport, 0.47, came at 4 m/s . Margolis and colleagues report record agility for the MIT Mini Cheetah with a learned controller, sustaining speeds up to 3.9 m/s , and periodic reward composition yields standing, walking, hopping, running and skipping on Cassie . ## From quadrupeds to humanoids On Unitree's H1, H2O turns RGB-camera human pose estimates into real-time whole-body teleoperation: it fits and retargets AMASS motions, filters those a privileged imitator cannot track, and trains a tracking policy with domain randomization that outputs 19 joint-position targets to a PD controller. The robot side also uses motion capture for linear velocity . On the G1 with fixed wrists, ASAP trains an ankle delta-action model from real rollouts, freezes it in simulation for fine-tuning, and deploys the policy without it. Its quantitative hardware comparison against Vanilla covers only kicking and LeBron's "Silencer" . A causal transformer over proprioceptive history gave humanoids a fully learned controller that deployed zero-shot . Cassie's dual-history controller ran a 400-meter dash , a miniature soccer humanoid walked 181% faster and turned 302% faster than a scripted baseline , and Hiking in the Wild maps raw depth and proprioception to joint actions without external state estimation, at up to 2.5 m/s . Humanoid Parkour learns vision-based whole-body control without motion priors and selects obstacle-crossing skills autonomously under joystick steering . Joshua Aurand, Marco Hutter and colleagues at Disney Research Zurich and ETH Zurich (October 2026) built Walk Like This, which sets walking style from a reference clip and speed from a joystick: a diffusion model generates the styled motion and an RL policy tracks it . In simulation, a tracker trained on generated motion fell 0.001 times per minute while following the diffusion output, against 1.104 for one trained on the original motion capture, at the cost of larger tracking errors . On a Unitree G1 the authors report about 4 hours of zero-shot deployment across styles without a failure .

Boston Dynamics benchmarks policies in simulation, then on an internal Spot robustness fleet running 24/7 for over 2,000 cumulative hours a week; falls reproducible in simulation are recreated for training or evaluation <Cite id="bd-spot-rl-2024" />.

On 19 March 2025 the RAI Institute described an Atlas policy that tracks retargeted human motion, each maneuver built from about 150 million simulator runs and transferred zero-shot <Cite id="rai-atlas-rl-2025" />. Boston Dynamics later said Atlas practiced "for millions of hours in simulations in parallel", with only rotary actuators that are easier to represent in simulation <Cite id="bd-atlas-hard-work-2026" />.

In August 2025, Boston Dynamics and Toyota Research Institute reported Large Behavior Models on Atlas: a 450M-parameter diffusion transformer trained with <Term id="flow-matching">flow matching</Term> on curated teleoperated demonstrations from hardware and simulation. It controls the full robot at 30 Hz, predicting 48 actions (1.6 seconds) per inference and most often executing 24 (0.8 seconds at 1x speed), and the neural policies share its control interface with an MPC-based teleoperation system <Cite id="bd-atlas-lbm-2025" />. Boston Dynamics unveiled the product version of Atlas at CES on 5 January 2026 and committed its 2026 fleets to Hyundai and Google DeepMind <Cite id="bd-atlas-ces-2026" />.

Agility reports that Digit's whole-body control model, an LSTM with fewer than one million parameters, trains in Isaac Sim for decades of simulated time over three or four days and transfers zero-shot <Cite id="agility-wbc-2025" />. Figure reports that its S0 whole-body policy, now conditioned on camera perception, traverses real-world stairs <Cite id="figure-s0-2026" />.

<span id="what-the-lineage-does-not-solve" />
## Limits of the lineage

Contact-rich manipulation is harder to simulate: Acosta and colleagues call dynamic contact the computational bottleneck for most simulations <Cite id="acosta-2021" />, and the [locomotion-manipulation comparison](/rl-sim2real/why-rl-locomotion) explains why. Eureka's LLM-written rewards beat human experts on 83% of 29 environments <Cite id="eureka-2024" />, and DrEureka writes both reward functions and domain-randomization distributions, getting a quadruped to walk atop a yoga ball <Cite id="dreureka-2024" />.

Lukas Amiet, Marco Hutter, Cesar Cadena and colleagues at ETH Zurich (October 2026) had an ANYmal D quadruped solve a Rubik's Cube with its feet; the cube is 0.4 m on a side and weighs 4.6 kg, and the robot flips it or pins it with one foot while the other pushes a layer round <Cite id="rubiks-quadruped-2026" />. Skills trained with privileged RL and distilled into policies that read onboard depth and proprioception completed all three attempted hardware solves without intervention, each about 30 steps over 8 to 9 minutes <Cite id="rubiks-quadruped-2026" />. In separate skill trials both flips succeeded 15 of 15 times, while the counterclockwise layer turn succeeded 13 of 15 times and the clockwise turn 10 of 15 <Cite id="rubiks-quadruped-2026" />.

edits.before:
<MotionPantograph className="my-6" />

A da Vinci surgeon sits at a console away from the table and moves hand controllers, while patient-side arms carry wristed instruments and an endoscope. The robot adds motion scaling, tremor filtering and wrists that articulate inside the body. Yang and colleagues place such a system at Level 0, no autonomy, because even with motion scaling its output represents the surgeon's desired motion <Cite id="yang-autonomy-2017" />. At level 1 a robot gives cognitive and physical assistance, and at level 2 it performs a surgical task autonomously <Cite id="attanasio-autonomy-2021" />.

<Image id="da-vinci-xi-surgeon-console-vesoul-2023" />

The field began with positioning. In 1988 Kwoh and colleagues reported a robot with improved absolute positioning accuracy for CT-guided stereotactic brain surgery <Cite id="kwoh-ct-robot-1988" />. Marescaux and colleagues reported transatlantic robot-assisted telesurgery in 2001 <Cite id="marescaux-telesurgery-2001" />. Intuitive says cardiac surgery was the first specialty cleared on the original da Vinci, in 2002 <Cite id="davinci5-cardiac-2026" />.

Da Vinci 5, cleared in March 2024, has more than 150 enhancements over Xi and more than 10,000 times its computing power <Cite id="davinci5-clearance-2024" />. Its optional Force Feedback instruments let the surgeon feel forces at the instrument tips, and Intuitive reported up to 43 percent less force on tissue in preclinical trials <Cite id="davinci5-clearance-2024" />. In a preclinical study by 28 surgeons, the feature at its high setting cut maximal force by 36, 41 and 55 percent in retraction, dissection and suturing <Cite id="awad-force-feedback-2024" />.

Logs from 444 thoracic procedures by 73 surgeons show median tip force falling from 1.79 N with feedback off to 1.32 N at the high setting <Cite id="kneuertz-dv5-force-2025" />. A pilot study of 68 colorectal operations found less applied force without a significant change in bowel function or length of stay <Cite id="chang-dv5-colorectal-2025" />. In January 2026 the FDA cleared da Vinci 5 for selected cardiac procedures using instruments without force feedback <Cite id="davinci5-cardiac-2026" />.

Intuitive reports that its installed base grew 12 percent in 2025 to 11,106 systems, and that da Vinci procedures grew roughly 18 percent worldwide in 2025 <Cite id="intuitive-q4-2025" />. Of 532 fourth-quarter placements, 303 were da Vinci 5s <Cite id="intuitive-q4-2025" />. In the second quarter of 2026, procedures grew about 15 percent and 246 of 468 placements were da Vinci 5s <Cite id="intuitive-q2-2026" />.

<SurgicalSystemsTable className="my-6 wide-measure" />

Every system in the table is Level 0 or Level 1 on the Yang scale <Cite id="yang-autonomy-2017" />.

## The challengers and what they compete on

CMR Surgical's Versius is a modular multiport system whose arms are separate bedside units that can move between operating rooms, driven from an open console <Cite id="cmr-versius-authorization-2024" />. In October 2024 the FDA authorized it through De Novo for adult cholecystectomy, the first multiport soft-tissue general surgical system authorized that way <Cite id="cmr-versius-authorization-2024" />. CMR put robot-assisted surgery at about 2.5 percent of nearly 10 million annual US major operating-room procedures <Cite id="cmr-versius-authorization-2024" />. Versius Plus was cleared in December 2025, and by March 2026 CMR reported more than 45,000 Versius patients in more than 30 countries <Cite id="versius-plus-510k-2025" /><Cite id="cmr-45000-patients-2026" />.

Medtronic's Hugo was cleared on December 3, 2025 for urologic procedures including prostatectomy, nephrectomy and cystectomy <Cite id="medtronic-hugo-clearance-2025" />. Medtronic says it had already been used in more than 30 countries <Cite id="medtronic-hugo-clearance-2025" />. Its first US case followed at Cleveland Clinic in February 2026 <Cite id="medtronic-hugo-first-us-2026" />.

Medtronic says about 80 percent of US abdominal urologic surgery is already robot-assisted <Cite id="medtronic-hugo-first-us-2026" />. In June 2026 it filed 510(k)s for general and gynecologic surgery <Cite id="medtronic-hugo-510k-2026" />.

Johnson & Johnson's OTTAVA, a table-integrated soft-tissue robot, received De Novo authorization in July 2026 for general-surgery procedures including gastric bypass, cholecystectomy and hiatal hernia repair <Cite id="jnj-ottava-2026" />. J&J says it occupies 30 to 50 percent less space than boom- and cart-mounted systems <Cite id="jnj-ottava-2026" />. In a Michigan registry of 169,404 patients, robotic use in common general-surgery procedures rose from 1.8 percent in 2012 to 15.1 percent in 2018 <Cite id="sheetz-adoption-2020" />.

Moon Surgical's Maestro is a two-armed assistant that holds and positions the laparoscopic camera and instruments, using the cameras and graspers a hospital already owns. Its first 510(k), in December 2022, rested on substantial equivalence to a 1990s endoscope positioner <Cite id="maestro-tavac-2023" />. A single surgeon used it without an assistant in a 30-patient series <Cite id="maestro-tavac-2023" />.

The commercial system was cleared in June 2024 <Cite id="maestro-commercial-510k-2024" />. ScoPilot, cleared in March 2025, runs on NVIDIA Holoscan on the robot and lets the laparoscope follow the instrument tip on demand <Cite id="scopilot-clearance-2025" />, Level 1 assistance on the Yang scale <Cite id="yang-autonomy-2017" />.

<ScopeFollow className="my-6" />

## The precision and reliability bar

A policy that succeeds 95 percent of the time per step compounds to 21.5 percent over 30 steps, the arithmetic of the [reliability gap](/frontier/reliability-gap/). FDA reports on robotic surgery from 2000 to 2013 included 144 deaths (1.4 percent of 10,624 reports), 1,391 patient injuries and 8,061 device malfunctions <Cite id="alemzadeh-adverse-events-2016" />. At clearance, Intuitive said da Vinci 5 would first go to a small number of US customers to gather data on real use <Cite id="davinci5-clearance-2024" />. In the ROLARR trial of 471 rectal-cancer patients, robotic assistance did not significantly reduce conversion to open surgery: 8.1 percent against 12.2 percent for conventional laparoscopy (P = .16) <Cite id="rolarr-2017" />.

In 2016 STAR, the Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot, performed supervised autonomous soft-tissue anastomosis in vivo in pigs <Cite id="star-suturing-2016" />. Its suture spacing and leak pressure matched or exceeded both expert surgeons and robot-assisted technique <Cite id="star-suturing-2016" />. In 2022 a robot performed laparoscopic small-bowel anastomosis in pigs over a one-week survival period, with the operator choosing among autonomously generated plans <Cite id="saeidi-laparoscopic-2022" />. It outperformed expert manual and robot-assisted technique on consistency and accuracy <Cite id="saeidi-laparoscopic-2022" />.

In 2025 SRT-H, whose high-level language policy guides a low-level policy through long-horizon steps and helps it recover from errors, ran ex vivo cholecystectomy experiments <Cite id="srt-h-2025" />. It succeeded on all eight gallbladders tested without human intervention <Cite id="srt-h-2025" />. [Hierarchical policies](/manipulation/hierarchical/) covers that design.

<SurgicalAutonomyLadder className="my-6" />

A device is authorized for an indication, a named procedure in a named population, and expansion needs a new clearance. Yang and colleagues argue that a highly autonomous robot starts practicing medicine, which in the US falls to medical societies <Cite id="yang-autonomy-2017" />. They propose licensing robotic surgeons through the medical establishment, as is done for human surgeons <Cite id="yang-autonomy-2017" />.

Yang and colleagues put the gap between the 510(k) and premarket-approval pathways at tens of millions of dollars and years of review, and add that risk tolerance to autonomous robots is expected to change as autonomous machines such as self-driving cars become commonplace <Cite id="yang-autonomy-2017" />. Haidegger names the lack of autonomy benchmarks and standards as a major barrier to commercialising autonomous surgical robots <Cite id="haidegger-autonomy-2019" />, and [safety and assurance](/frontier/safety-and-assurance/) covers the general case.

## What robot learning takes from it

The da Vinci Research Kit exposes all control layers through open electronics and software built around retired first-generation da Vinci mechanics <Cite id="dvrk-research-kit-2014" />.

Clinical recordings could become training data. SRT showed that imitation learning works on the da Vinci despite its approximate kinematics, using a relative action formulation, so the large repository of clinical data may be used for robot learning without further corrections <Cite id="srt-2024" />. edits.before: NVIDIA's Cosmos 3 report calls a home robot built from a separate VLM planner, VLA or WAM, and forward-dynamics model "fragmented" and "computationally wasteful" . Cosmos 3, launched at GTC Taipei on 31 May 2026, unifies those capabilities in one omni-model . Its predecessor Predict2.5 had already combined text-, image- and video-conditioned generation in one flow-based model . Its Mixture-of-Transformers backbone routes language and ViT-encoded vision to a causal autoregressive reasoner and VAE-encoded vision, audio and actions to a diffusion generator; diffusion tokens attend to both streams, while reasoner tokens never read diffusion tokens . It supports VLM understanding, video generation and three action modes: forward dynamics (video from clean actions), inverse dynamics (actions from clean video) and policy (both). Specialized results come from separate post-training, such as a DROID policy started from mid-trained Cosmos3-Nano with fresh action modules. Nano has 16B parameters on a dense 8B transformer and Super 64B on a dense 32B one . ## Genie 3 renders worlds at 24 fps that hold for a few minutes The original Genie learned latent actions and generated 2D worlds at about one frame per second . Genie 2 (December 2024) moved to 3D, with consistent worlds for up to a minute and most examples lasting 10 to 20 seconds . In its August 5, 2025 announcement, DeepMind describes Genie 3 as a limited research preview: text-prompted worlds navigable in real time at 24 fps and 720p, largely consistent for a few minutes. A SIMA agent sent navigation actions to Genie 3, and the world model simulated the future without knowing the agent's goal; the test involved no robot manipulation. It lists five limits: a constrained direct action space, multi-agent interaction, geographic accuracy, legible text only when supplied, and a few minutes of continuous interaction . Project Genie, released in January 2026 for AI Ultra subscribers, caps sessions at 60 seconds per world .

<span id="world-action-models-as-policies" />
## World-action models now run as closed-loop robot policies

A world-action model (WAM) predicts future video and actions together. NVIDIA reports that DreamZero runs a 14B autoregressive video-diffusion model as a 7 Hz closed-loop policy and more than doubles the generalization of state-of-the-art [VLAs](/manipulation/vla-models/) on real robots <Cite id="dreamzero-2026" />. Cosmos Policy post-trains Cosmos-Predict2 with no architectural modifications and reaches 98.5% on LIBERO and 67.1% on RoboCasa <Cite id="cosmos-policy-2026" />. LingBot-VA learns frame prediction and policy execution together, feeding real observations back into its rollouts and overlapping prediction with motor execution <Cite id="lingbot-va-2026" />.

Under perturbation, Cosmos-Policy reached 82.2% on LIBERO-Plus and LingBot-VA 74.2% on RoboTwin 2.0-Plus, while VLAs such as π0.5 matched them on some tasks only with extensive, diverse training <Cite id="wam-robustness-2026" />. Fast-WAM stays competitive without test-time video generation, while removing video co-training costs far more <Cite id="fast-wam-2026" />.

OpenWAM (October 2026), from Heng Yu, Li Fei-Fei, Jiajun Wu, Ehsan Adeli and colleagues at Stanford, pretrains the Wan2.2-5B video model causally on more than 10,000 hours of robot video. That training raised video-then-action success on LIBERO-Long from 68.4% to 97.8% over the original Wan2.2-5B. Its action expert can generate jointly, video first, action first or decoupled <Cite id="openwam-2026" />.

Long-WAM (October 2026), from Wei Huang, Linxi Fan, Song Han, Yukang Chen and colleagues at NVIDIA, MIT and HKU, found that longer visual history pays off when the video model was pretrained autoregressively. On RoboCasa GR-1, extending context from 0 to 19.2 seconds raised success from 63.3% to 78.7%, while a bidirectionally pretrained start showed no net gain. On real robots it stacked moving cups in 95% of trials, a task where π0.5 and Fast-WAM succeeded in none of 20 <Cite id="long-wam-2026" />.

DreamCan (October 2026), from Chongkai Gao, Jiajun Wu, Li Fei-Fei and colleagues at Stanford, NUS, Harvard and Northwestern, plans with a few generated subgoal images instead of dense video. Its training subgoals are chosen to balance whether a low-level policy can reach each one against how far each moves the task. With a 0.1-billion-parameter policy that was not pretrained, it reached 91.2% on LIBERO-Long against 82.4% for evenly spaced subgoals. π0.5 and Lingbot-VA, whose scores the authors took from the original papers, reached 92.4% and 98.5% <Cite id="dreamcan-2026" />.

<span id="1x-and-odyssey-the-commercial-edges" />
## 1X still fails dexterous tasks, while Odyssey streams worlds live

1X reports that its NEO policy builds on a 14B video model, mid-trained on 900 hours of egocentric human video and fine-tuned on 70 hours of robot data, with an inverse-dynamics model (IDM) extracting actions. Over 30 runs per task it scored 0% on drawing a smiley and pouring cereal. The backbone takes 11 seconds per 5 seconds of video, plus 1 second for the IDM <Cite id="1x-world-model-2026" />. In June 2026, 1X launched a World Model Lab led by Sam Sinha, previously a founding research scientist at Luma AI <Cite id="1x-world-model-lab-2026" />.

Odyssey-2 (October 2025) generates each frame causally from prior frames and user input, streaming a new frame every 50 ms (about 20 fps), steerable by text <Cite id="odyssey-2-2025" />.

edits.before: ## In IWS tests, generated demonstrations rivalled real ones for two policies The Interactive World Simulator is built on an action-conditioned latent dynamics model. It reports more than 10 minutes of stable generated-video interaction at up to 15 FPS on a single RTX 4090, at a default 128×128 resolution; quantitative video comparisons use 192 steps (19.2 seconds) . In 100-episode mixtures, generated-only versus real-only policy data scored 87.9% versus 90.3% for DP and 76.2% versus 73.6% for ACT. With more real data, π0.5 rose from 73.1% to 88.8%. Points used 100 MuJoCo or 10 physical evaluations, and the simulator was trained on interaction data including real play. A four-task test from 20 initial configurations gave positively biased simulator scores except for T pushing . ## Some video simulators rank policies in real-world order, others do not RoboWorld pairs an autoregressive video world model with a GPT-4o scorer that rates task progress from 0 to 5 from fixed external views. In its fourth revision, 4,186 generated 30-second rollouts gave eight policy-level scores matching the 26 February 2026 RoboArena leaderboard at Pearson r = 0.989 and Spearman rho = 0.970 (p < 0.001); the eight aggregates are the correlation points. The paper reports contact-induced object artifacts and VLM scores about one point above human scores over roughly 100 rollouts . DeepMind reports its Veo-based simulator predicted relative policy performance in nominal and out-of-distribution conditions, checked against more than 1,600 real evaluations. Its episodes last 8 seconds, and its authors call contact-rich, small-object interaction an open challenge . PolaRiS found that the open Ctrl-World hallucinated during object interaction in diverse scenes and mis-ranked policies at MMRV 0.22 . In February 2026 Runway reported a similar ranking test for its GWM-Robotics world model. Across eight vision-language-action policies from RoboArena, with 1,450 simulated rollouts scored by human graders, the policies' simulated and real progress scores had a Pearson correlation of 0.95 . Runway says the study tests policy ranking only and does not predict absolute success rates . In September 2026 it announced Praxis-1, a world action model it is testing with partners before an open-weight release . ## Generated experience trains real policies, but contact-rich tasks stay open RISE ran RL inside a compositional world model and gained 35 to 45 absolute points on three real tasks, including dynamic brick sorting . GRAIL used 3D assets and video-model priors to generate over 20,000 humanoid sequences. Visual policies trained only on them reached 84% success on object pick-up and 90% on stair-climbing on a real Unitree G1 . Yinlong Dai, Homanga Bharadhwaj and Dylan P. Losey at Virginia Tech and Johns Hopkins (October 2026) seed CASTER with generated videos of a person doing the task, then optimize a feasible robot motion in a digital twin . DeepMind reports its Veo-based simulator predicted relative policy performance in nominal and out-of-distribution conditions, checked against more than 1,600 real evaluations. PolaRiS found the open Ctrl-World hallucinated during object interaction in diverse scenes and mis-ranked policies at MMRV 0.22 . In February 2026 Runway reported a similar GWM-Robotics world-model ranking test. Across eight vision-language-action policies from RoboArena, with 1,450 simulated rollouts scored by human graders, the policies' simulated and real progress scores had Pearson correlation 0.95 . Visual policies trained only on them reached 84% success on object pick-up and 90% on stair-climbing on a real Unitree G1 . Yinlong Dai, Homanga Bharadhwaj and Dylan P. Losey at Virginia Tech and Johns Hopkins (October 2026) seed CASTER with generated videos of a person doing the task, then optimize a feasible robot motion in a digital twin . The central failure is action indifference: smooth, photorealistic futures that ignore the robot's action. A 2026 survey of robot world models rates controllability above visual plausibility <Cite id="world-model-survey-2026" />, and the closed-loop World-in-World benchmark found it mattered more than visual quality for task success <Cite id="world-in-world-2025" />.

<span id="start-with-the-intended-use" />
## Perception scores miss function, so each use needs its own test

WorldArena scores 14 models separately as data engines, policy evaluators and action planners, and reports a "significant perception-functionality gap" <Cite id="worldarena-2026" />. NVIDIA reports its DreamGen Bench video scores tracking downstream policy success <Cite id="dreamgen-2025" />. 1X saw unchanged policy weights degrade within days after subtle lighting or background changes <Cite id="1x-world-model-2024" />.

<span id="level-1-one-step-action-sensitivity" />
## Level 1: open models often fail to follow a changed action

Build matched counterfactuals: fix the observation, noise, prompt and history, and change one action dimension. WorldEval found raw action inputs often yield videos that ignore the action <Cite id="worldeval-2025" />, and IRASim and Ctrl-World add frame-level action conditioning <Cite id="irasim-2024" /> <Cite id="ctrl-world-2025" />. Across six open action-conditioned world models and more than 18,000 test instances, WorldSimProbe found systematic degradation in how actions are realized <Cite id="worldsimprobe-2026" />.

<span id="level-2-temporal-and-physical-consistency" />
## Level 2: pooled video metrics hide physical errors

Roll out autoregressively, score task events such as grasp, slip and release, and report error per horizon. Fréchet Video Distance "increases only slightly with large temporal corruption" <Cite id="fvd-content-bias-2024" />. WorldModelBench uses 67K human labels to catch violations such as objects changing size <Cite id="worldmodelbench-2025" />, and video models trained on simple physics failed out of distribution, copying the closest training example <Cite id="video-physical-law-2024" />.

<Image id="roboworld-bair-forcing-2026" />

<span id="level-3-task-progress-scoring" />
## Level 3: the progress scorer needs its own test

Many evaluators pair a video generator with a vision-language scorer, as WorldGym does, so each half needs its own test <Cite id="worldgym-2025" />. GVL fixes poor naive VLM value prediction by ordering shuffled frames, scoring more than 300 real tasks <Cite id="gvl-2024" />. Runway and DreamDojo used human graders instead, Runway collecting over 16,000 ratings <Cite id="runway-gwm-robotics-eval-2026" /> <Cite id="dreamdojo-2026" />.

<span id="level-4-policy-ranking" />
## Level 4: the best simulators order policies as real trials do

A policy evaluator must reproduce reality's ordering, measured as Pearson correlation and Mean Maximum Rank Violation (MMRV) <Cite id="runway-gwm-robotics-eval-2026" />. Real comparisons often rest on 10 to 50 trials, and adding trials after peeking risks p-hacking; the STEP sequential test cuts trials by up to 32% <Cite id="optimal-stopping-2025" />.

<Image id="roboarena-evaluation-2025" />

Google DeepMind reports its Veo simulator ranked eight Gemini Robotics checkpoints against more than 1,600 real evaluations at MMRV 0.03, though its absolute success predictions ran low <Cite id="veo-world-simulator-2025" />. WorldGym reached r = 0.78 <Cite id="worldgym-2025" />, and NVIDIA reports r = 0.995 for DreamDojo <Cite id="dreamdojo-2026" />. Runway reports Pearson 0.95 and MMRV 0.033 over eight RoboArena policies, testing ranking only <Cite id="runway-gwm-robotics-eval-2026" />. PolaRiS found that Ctrl-World "produces heavy hallucinations during object interaction", mis-ranking policies at MMRV 0.22 <Cite id="polaris-2025" />.

Physics simulation sets the bar. In June 2026, Yuke Zhu and colleagues reported that SimFoundry, which rebuilds a real scene in simulation from video, predicted real results across 7 tasks and 5 policy architectures at mean Pearson 0.911 and MMRV 0.018 <Cite id="simfoundry-2026" />. PolaRiS reports r = 0.9 against real trials <Cite id="polaris-2025" />, and X2Real 0.84 <Cite id="x2real-2026" />.

<span id="level-5-closed-loop-usefulness" />
## Level 5: planning and fine-tuning in a world model improved outcomes

IRASim planning raised Push-T IoU from 0.637 to 0.961 <Cite id="irasim-2024" />, and fine-tuning on Ctrl-World's imagined successes raised policy success by 44.7% <Cite id="ctrl-world-2025" />. Post-training on action-observation data helped more than a stronger pretrained video generator <Cite id="world-in-world-2025" />.

For value-learning uses, Palenicek and colleagues compare learned dynamics with the simulator's true dynamics inside the RL loop, separating dynamics-model error from the other limitations of value expansion <Cite id="revisiting-model-value-expansion-2022" />.

SIMPLER's test, whether simulated and real policy performance correlate under matched visual and physical conditions, applies to learned simulators too <Cite id="simpler-2024" />. RoboArena widens real evaluation beyond one laboratory <Cite id="roboarena-2025" />.

<span id="control-the-evaluation-shifts" />
## Saturated benchmarks hide robustness gaps

Use a factorial matrix to expose shifts one "unseen" split could conceal. RoboLab-120 sorts 120 tasks into visual, procedural and relational axes and measures sensitivity to controlled perturbations <Cite id="robolab-2026" />:

<EvalShiftTable className="my-6" />

edits.before: ## The tracking lineage DeepMimic adapted standard RL to imitate motion clips, including retargeted ones, for animated characters and an Atlas robot model . PHC tracks motion and recovers from falls for simulated avatars, with no physical robot: its controller imitates 98.9% of 11,313 filtered AMASS training clips, and PMCP trains new primitives on progressively harder failed clips . On the Unitree H1, H2O's privileged motion-filtering imitator is "similar to PHC" and follows PULSE . A second policy learns whole-body tracking from the cleaned retargeted set with domain randomization and follows human keypoints estimated from an RGB camera, but the deployed teleoperation system, a joint-target policy over a PD controller, also uses robot-side motion capture for linear velocity . OmniH2O's student, distilled from a privileged RL teacher, tracks head-and-hand goals from proprioceptive history with no explicit global-linear-velocity input, though root odometry still maps goals into the robot frame . A visual policy trained on teleoperated demonstrations can drive the tracker, evaluated on four of six recorded tasks at ten runs each, and the authors report no safety guarantees for extreme disturbances or out-of-distribution goals . HumanPlus estimates the operator's body and hand poses with one RGB camera, and its Humanoid Shadowing Transformer, trained with PPO on retargeted motion in simulation, runs zero-shot on a customized H1 from IMU and joint encoders. Two head-mounted cameras record the robot's view during shadowing, and supervised behavior cloning then trains a Humanoid Imitation Transformer from binocular images and proprioception; occlusion, fixed retargeting and limited locomotion remain constraints . ExBody separates upper-body motion imitation from robust leg velocity tracking . ExBody2 tracks local keypoints with separate velocity tracking, because drifting global keypoint targets can accumulate tracking errors. It filters references by an initial policy's lower-body tracking error and distills a privileged PPO teacher into a history-based student that walks, squats and dances on Unitree G1, though transitions between specialists remain unresolved . ASAP, the delta-action method in the [sim-to-real module](/rl-sim2real/sim2real-transfer), fine-tunes against a simulator corrected from real G1 rollouts for jumps and sports-style motions . KungfuBot trains one policy per processed reference motion and tightens the tracking reward's error tolerance as training proceeds, never loosening it; its quantitative hardware test is ten Tai Chi trials with the G1 root fixed for evaluation . GMT instead trains a single tracking controller, distilled from a soft mixture-of-experts teacher whose gating network combines expert actions; its baselines and ablations run in simulation, and it neither gets up after falls nor targets slopes and stairs . Learned get-up policies lift a real G1 from lying face up or face down . KungfuBot2 combines local and global tracking, segment rewards and a mixture-of-experts controller for many motions . BeyondMimic learns cartwheels, spin-kicks, flip-kicks and sprinting with one setup and shared hyperparameters and transfers zero-shot to hardware . ZEST trains motion-imitation policies with RL from motion capture, monocular video and animation, and deploys them zero-shot on Atlas, the Unitree G1 and Spot . ## Three decompositions ship in 2026 HOVER distills full-body kinematic motion imitation across control modes into one policy . ResGAC combines geometric admittance feedback with residual RL for precise end-effector tracking during whole-body motion . Figure, NVIDIA and Google DeepMind each shipped whole-body control in 2026 with the learning boundary in a different place. ### A unified motion-tracking policy: Figure Helix 02 S0 Figure announced Helix 02 on 27 January 2026. It keeps the tracking decomposition: S2 reasons over scenes and language and emits latent goals; S1, a 200 Hz visuomotor transformer, maps head and palm cameras, fingertip tactile sensors and full-body proprioception to whole-body joint targets; and S0, a 10M-parameter controller at 1 kHz, turns joint state and base motion into actuator commands. S0 trained on over 1,000 hours of joint-level retargeted human motion and sim-to-real RL across more than 200,000 parallel environments, and the headline demo is a 4-minute dishwasher unload and reload . Figure says it later conditioned S0 on camera perception , and reports that Helix 2.5, pretrained from random initialization on its Index human-behavior dataset, succeeded on 56% of blind zero-shot trials in 30 unseen homes, against 9% when trained from scratch . ### A VLA above a learned controller: GR00T + GEAR-SONIC NVIDIA keeps the VLA and whole-body controller as separate learned systems, and released GR00T N1.7 as early access on 18 April 2026 . GR00T N1.7 is a 3B-parameter VLA with a Cosmos-Reason2-2B backbone and a flow-matching action head; with the `UNITREE_G1_SONIC` embodiment it predicts latent action tokens that the GEAR-SONIC controller, running at 50 Hz, decodes into joint commands for legs, arms and hands . SONIC (Science Robotics) scales tracking from 1.2M to 42M parameters on 700 hours of motion capture, with one token space serving VR teleoperation and VLAs . Code is under Apache 2.0 and weights under the NVIDIA Open Model License, and every checkpoint loads the gated Cosmos-Reason2-2B backbone . Qiayuan Liao, Pieter Abbeel, Koushil Sreenath and colleagues at UC Berkeley (October 2026) train a tracker with analytic gradients through short rollouts of a differentiable world model fit to logged simulator transitions . Their SuperMimic passed the return of the released SONIC checkpoint after 3 hours on one H100 GPU, where SONIC trained for 7 days on 128 L40 GPUs, and failed on 25 of its 129,514 training motions against 179 for SONIC . The authors note that the GPU models differ and that SuperMimic trained on the public part of SONIC's data, about 2.3 times less motion . ### One VLA, feet to fingertips: Gemini Robotics 2 Google DeepMind puts everything in one model: its 30 July 2026 announcement reports that Gemini Robotics 2 controls full humanoids "from feet to fingertips", fetching and shelving a watering can on Apptronik's Apollo 2. One checkpoint runs Apollo 2 with SharpaWave hands, Apollo 2 with Inspire hands and the Franka Duo with Robotiq grippers, and DeepMind reports adapting to new bi-arm robots in a few hours, with fewer than 200 examples in most cases . Tap a body region in the figure below to see how a humanoid's motors are shared between legs, arms and hands.

## What tracking does not solve

A tracker does not choose its own motion. Workhorse trains a visual planner and whole-body tracker separately on the same human poses, augmenting each for the other's deployment errors <Cite id="workhorse-2026" />. HDMI extracts human and object trajectories from monocular video, then trains policies to track both <Cite id="hdmi-2025" />.

Zhang and colleagues pair a terrain-aware diffusion motion generator with a tracker fine-tuned on its imperfect references, crossing boxes, hurdles and stairs on a G1 <Cite id="wbc-motion-gen-2026" />. VIRAL's simulation-trained RGB policy ran continuous loco-manipulation for up to 54 cycles on a G1 <Cite id="viral-2025" />, and Boston Dynamics reports that a policy trained for 50 to 70 pound loads moved a fridge of over 100 pounds <Cite id="bd-atlas-hard-work-2026" />.

Yutang Lin, Guanya Shi and C. Karen Liu at Amazon FAR, Carnegie Mellon and Stanford (October 2026) plan in the latent command space of a frozen behavior foundation model, which closes the balance loop at 50 Hz while their FIBER planner replans at 5 Hz <Cite id="fiber-2026" />. FIBER projects separately trained policies for box pickup, door opening and grasping into that space and trains one perceptive planner on their rollouts; across 128 simulated variations per task it succeeded 42.0% of the time, against 11.6% for replaying the projected latents, 3.5% for a kinematic planner and 95.4% for the task experts <Cite id="fiber-2026" />. Trained only in simulation, FIBER succeeded in 6, 4 and 2 of 10 real G1 trials on the three tasks <Cite id="fiber-2026" />.

Zeji Yi, Guanya Shi and colleagues at Carnegie Mellon and Amazon FAR (October 2026) split collision avoidance between a perception-conditioned diffusion policy that proposes whole-body motions and an RL controller that tracks them and keeps balance <Cite id="swap-2026" />. Their SWAP labels training data in hindsight, placing obstacles only where an executed motion did not sweep <Cite id="swap-2026" />. Across five simulated tasks it averaged 88.3% success with test-time steering, 72.4% without it and 17.4% when the diffusion output drove the joints directly <Cite id="swap-2026" />. On a real G1, with motion capture for localization and the moving obstacles, it succeeded in 18 of 25 trials; the authors trace the failures to LiDAR occlusion and tracking mismatch <Cite id="swap-2026" />.

HITTER pairs a planner that predicts the ball and picks the strike with an RL whole-body controller, and reached up to 106 consecutive table-tennis shots against a human <Cite id="hitter-2025" />. LATENT builds humanoid tennis skills by correcting and composing incomplete human motion fragments <Cite id="latent-tennis-2026" />. Chris Paxton of Agility Robotics wrote in October 2026 that many such systems still see the ball through external motion trackers, which leaves onboard perception as the limit <Cite id="paxton-robot-sports-2026" />.

Retargeting is lossy: artifacts such as foot sliding and self-penetration significantly reduce tracking-policy robustness, particularly for dynamic or long sequences <Cite id="gmr-retargeting-2025" />, and noisy, inconsistent transferred references motivated a 2026 robustness method with a fall-recovery curriculum <Cite id="robust-tracking-2026" />.

Nicholas Ioannidis, Xue Bin Peng and colleagues at Simon Fraser University, FieldAI and NVIDIA (October 2026) replace the weighted objectives of retargeting with a priority order: foot placement first, then contacts with objects or other characters, then the remaining pose objectives <Cite id="primoretarget-2026" />. On two-person interactions from Inter-X their PriMoRetarget kept 78.8% of source hand contacts, and PPO policies trained on its output tracked the motions on a simulated Unitree G1 93.6% of the time <Cite id="primoretarget-2026" />. The strongest of three baselines, PHC, reached 35.2% and 72.8%; GMR and OmniRetarget scored lower <Cite id="primoretarget-2026" />. Collaborative manipulation by several robots stayed harder, at 62.6% tracking success <Cite id="primoretarget-2026" />.

Chaitanya Chawla, Kartik Sharma, Guanya Shi and colleagues at Carnegie Mellon (October 2026) check reachability during generation: their EmbodyHOI steers a frozen generator of human hand-object motion with a differentiable inverse-kinematics cost for the target robot while it samples <Cite id="embodyhoi-2026" />. On the Unitree G1 this cut the wrist error left after retargeting from 8.9 cm to 0.6 cm, and simulated policies trained on the guided references succeeded on 79% of 50 randomly drawn tasks, against 68% for unguided references <Cite id="embodyhoi-2026" />. Fixing the arms with inverse kinematics after generation dropped success on a four-task suite to 32.8%, against 79.7% with guidance, which costs 32 times an unguided sample <Cite id="embodyhoi-2026" />.

<RetargetingGap className="my-6" />

## V-JEPA 2 adds robot control with under 62 hours of robot video

edits.before: Control is energy minimization in latent space. The Cross-Entropy Method searches 800 candidates over ten iterations at horizon one for actions whose predicted feature map is closest in L1 to the goal's, executes the first action and replans. This goal distance has no demonstrated calibration to a value function, and the pixel decoder trained for visualization plays no part in control . A separate JEPA study trains embedding distances to approximate negative goal-conditioned value, improving planning on simple control tasks . Meta reports a 1.2B-parameter model with 65% to 80% pick-and-place success on new objects in unseen environments, given visual subgoals . V-JEPA 2.1 adds dense predictive losses and reports "a 20-point improvement in real-robot grasping success rate over V-JEPA-2 AC" . A Meta FAIR design study produced a JEPA world model that beats DINO-WM and V-JEPA-2-AC in navigation and manipulation . ## LeCun's AMI Labs raised over a billion dollars for world models LeCun left Meta and co-founded AMI Labs (Advanced Machine Intelligence), which raised \$1.03 billion at a \$3.5 billion pre-money valuation in March 2026 to build world models . LeCun is executive chairman and Alex LeBrun is CEO . LeBrun told TechCrunch that "'world models' will be the next buzzword": "In six months, every company will call itself a world model to raise funding." . ## JEPA has no steerable simulator, and its latents are hard to validate 1. Every currently usable interactive simulator is generative. Genie 3, Cosmos 3, Odyssey-2 and the Interactive World Simulator render pixels a user can inspect and steer . No interactive, action-controllable JEPA environment has shipped. 2. Latent-only objectives are hard to validate: without a decoder, a reader cannot see what the model believes. V-JEPA prevents collapse with an exponential-moving-average target encoder and stop-gradient, a design inherited from BYOL , and its authors state their adaptation of BYOL's justification as a hypothesis . LeJEPA removes those heuristics with "no stop-gradient, no teacher-student" ; LeVJEPA applies its collapse-free objective to video with a single encoder and projector , and Klindt and colleagues prove that it linearly recovers a world's latent variables under stated assumptions . In complex scenes, most models still score at chance on IntPhys 2 while humans are near perfect . ## Robot results do not yet separate the two camps 3. V-JEPA 2-AC's reported robot tests are bounded tabletop skills. Reaching, grasping, reach-with-object and pick-and-place with supplied goals and subgoals do not establish contact-rich assembly, deformable manipulation or whole-body control . SkyJEPA, a June 2026 preprint from Pratyaksh Rao, Yann LeCun, Giuseppe Loianno and colleagues, runs a JEPA-style latent dynamics model with sampling-based optimal control on a quadrotor's embedded hardware. It reports outdoor closed-loop flight with zero-shot sim-to-real transfer . 4. The camps post similar numbers. On LIBERO, latent world-model VLAs (VLA-JEPA 97.2, JEPA-VLA 96.4) sit beside video-based ones (Cosmos Policy and LingBot-VA 98.5, Say-Dream-ACT 98.1) . VLA-JEPA argues that pixel-anchored latent actions learn nuisance motion , and JEPA-VLA that V-JEPA 2 embeddings discard unpredictable factors . On the harder LIBERO-Plus, Cosmos-Policy reaches 82.2% and JEPA-WAM 79.2% without large-scale robot pretraining, or 86.3% as a π0.5 instantiation . 5. Fast-WAM separates video co-training from test-time generation. It keeps a future-video training objective but at inference only encodes the current frame and runs action denoising on a chunk. On LIBERO and RoboTwin 2.0, removing video co-training hurt success more than removing explicit future generation. That leaves a general JEPA advantage unproven. ## An interactive JEPA world or a contact-rich win would settle it Either of two results would break the stalemate: a JEPA environment a user can steer the way Genie 3 is steered today , or a JEPA advantage on contact-rich tasks, where both camps' evidence runs out. Until then the JEPA line has the cheapest demonstrated path from observation to zero-shot planning , and the [generative video](/world-models/generative-video/) line has the only usable simulators. In September 2026, Haoran Zhu, Wancong Zhang, Yann LeCun and Anna Choromanska tested JEPA world models as driving planners with no driving policy trained, using ground-truth future observations as goals. They report that earlier JEPA models were either accurate but slow or fast but too weak to plan. Their AD-E2E-JEPA projector gives a 100-fold inference speedup while keeping planning performance, rolling out 256 candidate trajectories over 8 frames in 0.8 seconds . H-JEPA, from Yann LeCun (AMI Labs and NYU) and colleagues (October 2026), stacks action-conditioned JEPAs that each predict farther ahead and hand subgoals to the level below. On Visual AntMaze a three-level hierarchy raised success from 18% to 73% with less planner compute . Leonardo Toso, Yann LeCun, James Anderson and Oumayma Bounou of Columbia, NYU and AMI Labs showed in October 2026 that next-step prediction with anti-collapse regularization can reach its minimum loss while discarding a system's controllable unstable modes. The learned state is then impossible to stabilize. They add an inverse-dynamics loss that reconstructs actions and prove, for linear systems, that exact reconstruction keeps every state direction reachable within the horizon. Experiments on CartPole, Walker2D and PointMaze from pixels extend the finding to nonlinear tasks .

<span id="a-deployment-rule-for-representation-prediction" />
## Use JEPA when reconstructing pixels adds no evidence

Use a JEPA-style model when the decision depends on task-relevant change and reconstructing pixels adds no evidence, as in goal-conditioned planning. Decoder-free latent planning already scales, with one 317M-parameter TD-MPC2 agent performing 80 tasks <Cite id="tdmpc2-2023" />. Synthetic video, visual debugging and simulator replacement fit poorly, because the decoder-free state hides what it omitted. Test whether nearby embeddings mean equivalent outcomes and whether action rankings match hardware, and add out-of-distribution detectors or planner fallbacks, since embedding distance is uncalibrated confidence (see the [model-based](/world-models/model-based-robot-learning/) and [evaluation](/world-models/evaluation/) guides).

## The asymmetry is in the MDP

Legged RL left simulation in 2019, when Hwangbo and colleagues transferred trained policies to ANYmal <Cite id="hwangbo-2019" />. Lee and colleagues' proprioceptive controller then held up in natural environments <Cite id="lee-2020" />, RMA ran on an A1 without fine-tuning <Cite id="rma-2021" />, and an off-policy recipe now trains humanoid locomotion in 15 minutes on one RTX 4090 <Cite id="seo-2025" />.

Boston Dynamics says RL helps where conditions are easy to simulate but good strategies are hard to describe <Cite id="bd-spot-rl-2024" />. Rudin and colleagues' policy observes <Term id="proprioception">proprioception</Term> and 108 terrain-height samples, and a learned network models ANYmal's series-elastic actuators, which are hard to simulate <Cite id="rudin-2021" />. Contact-rich manipulation is harder: the 2026 reality-gap survey notes that most simulators assume rigid bodies while real objects deform, that perfect fidelity is computationally infeasible, and that simplified contact models are particularly problematic in contact-rich tasks <Cite id="reality-gap-survey-2026" />. Tang and colleagues blame the cost of physical interaction for RL's difficulty in [robotics](/rl-sim2real/rl-for-robotics) <Cite id="tang-drl-survey-2025" />.

Locomotion papers combine <Term id="ppo">PPO</Term>, <Term id="domain-randomization">domain randomization</Term> and a <Term id="curriculum-learning">curriculum</Term>. Manipulation papers more often learn from real demonstrations, which need no contact model: Diffusion Policy beat prior methods by 46.9% on average across 12 tasks <Cite id="diffusion-policy-2023" />, and ACT learned to slot a battery at 80 to 90% success from 10 minutes of [demonstrations](/manipulation/bc-foundations) <Cite id="act-aloha-2023" />.

## Contact geometry is where the gap lives

A gait recovers from a wrong contact force on the next step; a jammed peg cannot. Acosta and colleagues call dynamic contact the computational bottleneck for most simulations, and three simulators they tested missed elastic impacts <Cite id="acosta-2021" />. Rigid-body contact models have a task-specific accuracy ceiling <Cite id="fazeli-2017" />, and Factory, which simulates 1000 nut-and-bolt interactions at once, still calls assembly contact a longstanding challenge <Cite id="factory-2022" />.

<Image id="shadow-hand-lightbulb-2007" />

<span id="it-is-a-tendency-not-a-law" />
## Exceptions in manipulation

OpenAI's in-hand policy learned finger gaiting without human demonstrations <Cite id="openai-dactyl-2018" />. Its Rubik's-cube successor, trained with automatic domain randomization, solved one fixed 43-subgoal scramble in two of ten trials with a sensor cube and zero of ten with vision for face angles, on customized hardware with tuned torque limits and a calibrated hand simulation <Cite id="openai-rubiks-cube-2019" />. Visual Dexterity reorients novel shapes in a median of about seven seconds on hardware under \$5,000 <Cite id="visual-dexterity-2022" />, and DextrAH-RGB [transfers](/rl-sim2real/sim2real-transfer/) an end-to-end RGB grasping policy <Cite id="dextrah-rgb-2024" />, distilled from a privileged teacher into a stereo-RGB student for a KUKA arm and Allegro hand <Cite id="isaac-lab-2025" />.

<CubeTrials className="my-6" />

In assembly, AutoMate's generalist solves 20 assemblies zero-shot <Cite id="automate-2024" />, Play2Perfect reaches 60% on 0.5 mm-clearance insertions <Cite id="play2perfect-2026" />, and InsertAnything, trained only on a simulated hexagonal insertion, succeeded on 95.0% of trials across eight unseen real insertion tasks <Cite id="insertanything-2026" />. SPARR's real-world residual adds 38.4% success over zero-shot transfer <Cite id="sparr-2026" />.

<span id="the-skeptic-record" />
## Brooks calls the dexterity forecasts fantasy, and Morgan Stanley asks for ROI

Evidence: Rodney Brooks, co-founder of iRobot and Rethink Robotics, calls the belief that current methods will yield practical humanoid dexterity within decades "pure fantasy thinking", since vision-only training gives no force channel ([dexterity](/frontier/dexterity/)) <Cite id="brooks-dexterity-2025" />. His January 2026 scorecard predicts deployable dexterity "will remain pathetic compared to human hands" beyond 2036, and walking humanoids too unsafe near people without new mechanical systems <Cite id="brooks-scorecard-2026" />. Rethink raised \$150 million and shut down in 2018 when sales fell short <Cite id="rethink-shutdown-2018" />.

<Image id="roomba-870-2014" />

Evidence: Morgan Stanley's July 2026 note says humanoids have a "PR problem": they are framed as substitutes for workers instead of tools for hazardous or labor-constrained tasks. It adds that "the industry's social license to deploy may matter just as much as technical performance". Investors "are increasingly looking for tangible evidence of real-world return on investment". The note says the US ban on Chinese humanoid imports risks raising R&D costs, and keeps a 50,000-unit China shipment estimate for 2026 <Cite id="morgan-stanley-pr-problem-2026" />.

<span id="unit-economics" />
## Unitree's Q1 2026 adjusted profit fell 52.55% year over year

Evidence: Unitree's Q1 2026 adjusted net profit fell 52.55% year over year, according to the STAR Market prospectus it filed in May 2026 <Cite id="unitree-prospectus-2026" />.

Evidence: Bessemer expects industry data costs to exceed \$3B over the next two years and calls capital the moat <Cite id="bessemer-robotics-2026" /> ([industrial deployment](/data-hardware/industrial-deployment/)).

Evidence: at Computex 2026, a Qualcomm-powered humanoid collapsed face-first during the live keynote, in a failure attributed to a communication glitch <Cite id="computex-collapse-2026" />.

<span id="the-demo-to-deployment-gap" />
## Vendor hours and shipment counts do not document productive work

The bear case is that closing the [reliability gap](/frontier/reliability-gap/) between demo and product outlasts the capital. Lisa Yan, quoted in Bessemer's own analysis, describes the climb from 99% to 99.9% as steep <Cite id="bessemer-robotics-2026" />.

Agility reports 65,000 hours of Digit production experience on an undated homepage <Cite id="agility-digit-production" />, and Figure reports 1,250+ hours at BMW Spartanburg by November 2025 <Cite id="figure-bmw-production-2025" />; neither counts autonomous units or supervised time ([evaluation crisis](/data-hardware/evaluation-crisis/)). Omdia counted about 13,000 humanoids shipped in 2025 <Cite id="agibot-omdia-ranking-2026" /> <Cite id="agibot-omdia-2026" /> and SAG 19.1K in the first half of 2026 <Cite id="sag-humanoid-shipments-2026" />. The IFR counted about 7,000 full-size humanoids, those above 140 cm, sold in 2025 <Cite id="ifr-service-robots-2026" />. Tesla's Q2 2026 update says it is still installing its first Optimus lines, whose initial builds go to an "Optimus Academy for training data collection" <Cite id="tesla-q2-2026-update" />.

<span id="the-capital-cycle" />
## Robotics funding passed 23 billion dollars by June 2026, and China repriced first

Evidence: beyond Crunchbase's narrower venture count <Cite id="crunchbase-robotics-funding-2026" />, a newsletter writeup put the total above \$23B by early June 2026 by PitchBook's tally <Cite id="robotics-funding-23b-2026" />. Bessemer Venture Partners argues there is "no robotics bubble" and that the sector is "structurally underinvested", but concedes that "some valuations are stretched" <Cite id="bessemer-robotics-2026" />. The skeptic side rests on Brooks's timeline predictions and Morgan Stanley's demand for ROI evidence: Brooks calls some humanoid hype "downright delusional" <Cite id="brooks-scorecard-2026" />, while Morgan Stanley makes no bubble call <Cite id="morgan-stanley-pr-problem-2026" /> ([competing theses](/frontier/competing-theses/)).

<FundingHumanoidCounts className="my-6" />

Evidence: on September 21, 2026, Reuters reported that regulators were slowing humanoid listings after Unitree's shares rose more than fivefold on debut, then fell 55% from their peak, and quoted a venture capitalist saying some private-market projects had taken valuation cuts of 30% to 50% <Cite id="reuters-china-humanoid-ipo-2026" />.

<span id="how-a-winter-would-happen" />
## Three hypothetical failures could start a winter

The three mechanisms below are hypothetical scenarios. Their precedent is the 1973 Lighthill report, which found progress in robot-building "even more disappointing" than in the rest of AI <Cite id="lighthill-1973" />.

**Speculation:** the reliability gap outlasts investor patience. If 99.9% takes five more years of per-task engineering, the 2026 fund vintage marks to market against pilots. Bessemer says the last stretch "takes longer than most timelines assume" <Cite id="bessemer-robotics-2026" />.

**Speculation:** the data thesis plateaus. If 10x more data stops buying <Term id="success-rate">success-rate</Term> gains, the fix is new science such as tactile integration, contact-faithful simulation or world models ([data bottleneck](/data-hardware/data-bottleneck/)). Ken Goldberg's 100,000-year data gap is the timing version: he accepts that data-driven methods "will eventually produce general purpose robots", and asks when <Cite id="goldberg-data-gap-2025" />.

**Speculation:** the form factor is wrong. If task-specific systems keep winning cost per task, the humanoid thesis most of the capital is priced on collapses, as Brooks's "pure fantasy thinking" line predicts <Cite id="brooks-dexterity-2025" />.

<span id="the-watchlist" />
## As of September 2026, none of the eight milestones is met

The board reads three not met, five partial, zero met. In unseen homes, π0.5 cleaned kitchens and bedrooms <Cite id="pi05-2025" />, and in September 2026 Figure reported 56% zero-shot success in 30 unseen homes, against 9% without Index pretraining <Cite id="helix-2-5-2026" />. Generalist reports 99% average success where earlier models reached 64%, though "not all tasks" reach those rates <Cite id="generalist-gen1-2026" />. RoboArena, RoboChallenge and ManipulationNet are building shared evaluation infrastructure <Cite id="roboarena-2025" /> <Cite id="robochallenge-2025" /> <Cite id="manipulationnet-2026" />.

Figure's Helix 02 takes fingertip tactile input <Cite id="helix-02-2026" />, and T-Rex beats its strongest baseline by over 30%, though most <Term id="vision-language-action-model">VLA</Term> models still "overlook the tactile modality" <Cite id="t-rex-2026" />. Sparsh-X and TouchWorld are tactile foundation models <Cite id="sparsh-x-2025" /> <Cite id="touchworld-2026" />. Surveys name [contact modeling](/rl-sim2real/sim2real-transfer/) a key contributor to the <Term id="sim-to-real-gap">sim-to-real</Term> gap, "particularly problematic in contact-rich tasks like robotic manipulation" <Cite id="reality-gap-survey-2026" />.

<span id="what-would-prove-the-bears-wrong" />
## Four measurable results would falsify the bear case

<BearCaseLock className="my-6" />

A verified deployment of 10,000 humanoids doing documented work breaks the commercial-viability premise, which vendor records so far measure in hours <Cite id="agility-digit-production" /> <Cite id="figure-bmw-production-2025" />, and one policy above 90% across more than ten unseen homes breaks the generalization premise <Cite id="helix-2-5-2026" /> ([generalization](/frontier/generalization/)). Cost-per-task parity breaks the form-factor premise <Cite id="brooks-dexterity-2025" />.

A real-world success-rate scaling law across tasks breaks the plateau premise: EgoScale's <Term id="scaling-law">scaling law</Term> is fit to validation loss <Cite id="egoscale-2026" />, and Lin et al. find a "roughly power-law relationship" for single-task generalization <Cite id="lin-data-scaling-laws-2024" />. Until then, more than \$23B had been raised by early June against that scoreboard.

A node is one participant, such as a camera driver, policy server or controller bridge. ## Time and synchronization

Camera, depth, joint and force streams arrive at different rates, so inputs need acquisition and arrival timestamps. MCAP records a publish time and a log time for every message <Cite id="mcap-spec-2026" />.

Logging source, receipt and inference-completion times splits latency into sensing, transport, model execution and command delivery; ros2_tracing does it at an average overhead of 0.0033 ms per message <Cite id="ros2-tracing-2022" />. With `use_sim_time` set, ROS time follows the latest `/clock` message <Cite id="ros2-clock-design" />, so nodes that mix it with wall time see spurious timeouts. The [calibration guide](/classical/calibration) covers spatial and temporal alignment.

## tf2: the coordinate-frame graph

tf2 keeps a time-buffered tree of coordinate frames and transforms data between any two frames at any time <Cite id="tf2-docs-2026" />. A lookup at an image timestamp can wait for the transform; the tf2 tutorial raises an exception only if it is still missing after a 50 ms timeout <Cite id="tf2-time-tutorial-2026" />. Foote's original tf library makes this a distributed bookkeeping problem, tracking frame relationships through both space and time across a robot system <Cite id="tf-library-2013" />.

REP 105 defines `odom` as a drifting short-term reference and `map` as a frame whose poses can jump <Cite id="rep-105-2010" />, and camera optical frames take an `_optical` suffix and a different axis convention <Cite id="rep-103-2010" />. A policy trained on base-frame <Term id="end-effector">end-effector</Term> deltas cannot be sent tool-frame deltas in the same layout; *Modern Robotics* covers the geometry <Cite id="modern-robotics-2017" />.

A learned-policy graph can separate drivers, state assembly, a policy server, a command gate, a controller bridge and a supervisor. The supervisor can drive ROS 2 managed nodes, which leave a primary state only on an external request or an error <Cite id="ros2-lifecycle-design-2015" />. ## RT-2: actions become text

RT-2 (2023) writes each action dimension's 256 bin indices as strings in a <Term id="vision-language-model">vision-language model</Term>'s token stream: PaLI-X already has a token for every integer up to 1000, while PaLM-E overwrites its 256 least frequently used tokens. The backbone, up to 55B parameters, is co-fine-tuned on robot trajectories and the original web vision-language data, which the authors report generalizes better than robot data alone <Cite id="rt2-2023" />. PaLM-E's inputs interleave visual, continuous state-estimation and text embeddings, grounding its language model in sensor observations <Cite id="palm-e-2023" />.

That web knowledge shows up as emergent object choice, such as picking the smallest object, and multi-stage reasoning, such as using a rock as an improvised hammer <Cite id="rt2-2023" />. Gemini Robotics 1.5 interleaves actions with natural-language reasoning <Cite id="gemini-robotics-15-2025" />. VLA-0 revisits plain-text action representations, avoiding added action heads or a modified vocabulary <Cite id="vla-0-2025" />.

In a May 2025 research note, Danny Driess and colleagues at Physical Intelligence call this tokenization "not suitable for high-frequency, precise, or fluent motions," likening it to "controlling your arm by verbally saying which muscles should contract" <Cite id="knowledge-insulation-2025" />.
