In February 2026, Toyota Research Institute researchers compared 89 co-trained policies over 58,000 simulated and 2,835 real rollouts. Vision-language and cross-embodiment co-training substantially improved generalization, while discrete action-token variants brought no significant benefit <Cite id="lbm-cotraining-2026" />. Xiaomi-Robotics-1 (July 2026) pretrains on over 100,000 hours of UMI handheld-gripper and egocentric trajectories and reports 57.4% on RoboCasa365 against a previous best of 46.6%; its authors say code and checkpoints will be released <Cite id="xiaomi-robotics-1-2026" />.

Moritz Reuss's October 2025 post, which he presents as his personal selection and opinion, says "OXE is mostly low-quality data" and "we still lack good methods to quantify data quality in imitation learning" <Cite id="oxe-quality-critique-2026" />.

## Octo and OpenVLA: the open models

Two 2024 releases made the recipe reproducible outside Google. Octo ships 27M- and 93M-parameter checkpoints trained on 800k Open X-Embodiment trajectories; learned readout tokens in a block-wise-masked transformer feed a lightweight diffusion head that outputs action chunks, and fine-tuning can add a new sensor or output while retaining the transformer weights <Cite id="octo-2024" />. In zero-shot WidowX evaluation, Octo reports a "25% higher success rate" with goal images than with language, and the authors suggest goal images carry more task information; only 56% of its pretraining data has language annotations <Cite id="octo-2024" />.

<Image id="octo-evaluation-setups-2024" />

OpenVLA builds on the Prismatic VLM <Cite id="prismatic-vlm-2024" />, with a Llama 2 7B backbone <Cite id="llama-2-2023" /> and fused DINOv2 <Cite id="dinov2-2023" /> and SigLIP <Cite id="siglip-2023" /> features. Trained on 970k robot demonstrations, it predicts seven coordinates for position, orientation and gripper, each split into 256 uniform bins between the training data's 1st and 99th quantiles instead of its minimum and maximum; bin indices replace the 256 least-used Llama tokens and are predicted autoregressively <Cite id="openvla-2024" /> <Cite id="openvla-oft-2025" />.

Its headline result is 16.5 points higher absolute task success than RT-2-X (55B) with "7x fewer parameters", over 29 tasks on two embodiments: 17 WidowX tasks with ten trials each and 12 Google-robot tasks with five, from matched initial robot and object states, with partial credit on some tasks <Cite id="openvla-2024" />. Among later open models, SmolVLA trains on one GPU, deploys on consumer GPUs or CPUs and decouples action prediction from execution with asynchronous inference <Cite id="smolvla-2025" />. CogACT conditions a dedicated diffusion action transformer on the VLM's output <Cite id="cogact-2024" />.

## The discrete-token throughput problem

OpenVLA's original formulation decodes seven action tokens sequentially per timestep <Cite id="openvla-oft-2025" />. RT-2 runs at 1 to 3 Hz for the 55B PaLI-X variant and about 5 Hz for the 5B variant, queried over the network from a multi-TPU cloud service <Cite id="rt2-2023" />. OpenVLA runs at about 6 Hz on one RTX 4090 in bfloat16, without compilation or speculative decoding, and its quantization analysis notes that slower inference changes the controller dynamics <Cite id="openvla-2024" />.

π0 instead adds a flow-matching expert that outputs action chunks at up to 50 Hz <Cite id="pi0-2024" />, and PD-VLA decodes in parallel by fixed-point iteration with no retraining, reaching 2.52 times the execution frequency <Cite id="pd-vla-2025" />. OpenVLA-OFT (2025) combines bidirectional parallel decoding, <Term id="action-chunking">action chunking</Term>, continuous actions and an L1-trained MLP head; its ALOHA variant, OFT+, adds FiLM for language grounding <Cite id="openvla-oft-2025" />.

On LIBERO <Cite id="libero-2023" />, OFT raises average success over four ten-task suites from 76.5% to 97.1% with an added wrist image and proprioceptive state, fine-tuned per suite and scored over 500 episodes each. On an A100, averaged over 100 one-image queries, L1 OFT generates 109.7 actions per second against OpenVLA's 4.2, and 71.4 with the added inputs <Cite id="openvla-oft-2025" />. LIBERO-Plus finds that such models drop from 95% to below 30% under modest perturbations and tend to ignore language instructions completely <Cite id="libero-plus-2025" />.

Real ALOHA runs use three images, robot state and absolute joint targets at 25 Hz, down from the platform's 50 Hz, and OFT+ executes all 25 actions before replanning, against eight on LIBERO. ALOHA tasks such as folding clothes are scored for partial completion, LIBERO for binary success <Cite id="openvla-oft-2025" />.

## A 2026 selection rule

Choosing a VLA means choosing a prior (the visual, language and robot experience in the backbone) and a control interface (the action, horizon, frame and measured rate). OFT changed both throughput and success without replacing OpenVLA <Cite id="openvla-oft-2025" />. Write down the required semantic novelty, embodiment data, action contract and latency budget, pick the prior with the [foundation-model guide](/manipulation/foundation-models/) and the output with the [action-space guide](/manipulation/action-spaces/), then compare only models whose contracts match; [generalist policies](/manipulation/generalist-policies/) and [RL fine-tuning](/manipulation/rl-finetuning/) cover the rest.

GR00T N1 separates the two, with a vision-language System 2 over a diffusion-transformer System 1 <Cite id="gr00t-n1-2025" />. π0.7 conditions on language plus strategy metadata and subgoal images, and Physical Intelligence reports zero-shot cross-embodiment laundry folding <Cite id="pi07-2026" />. Google DeepMind's Gemini Robotics 2 controls full humanoids, including a 22-degree-of-freedom hand, and is available only to early-access partners <Cite id="gemini-robotics-2-2026" />.

## The flow-matching log-likelihood problem

<Term id="ppo">PPO</Term> runs several epochs of minibatch updates on a clipped surrogate objective <Cite id="ppo-2017" />, which needs the likelihood of each action taken. <Term id="flow-matching">Flow matching</Term> trains by regressing vector fields along fixed conditional probability paths <Cite id="lipman-flow-matching-2022" />, so the executed action's log-likelihood is intractable <Cite id="pi-rl-2026" />. Online RL applied directly to large VLAs is also unstable and needs compute beyond most local machines <Cite id="ire-vla-2025" />.

DPPO (Ren et al., 2024) follows DDPO, which posed diffusion denoising as a multi-step decision problem <Cite id="ddpo-2023" />. DPPO embeds denoising inside the environment MDP: each denoising transition has an analytic Gaussian likelihood, and the environment advances and pays reward only after the final step. Only the last selected denoising steps are fine-tuned, with a frozen copy of the network for earlier ones <Cite id="dppo-2024" />.

DPPO is the strongest of the compared diffusion-based RL methods on state-input Robomimic tasks, though off-policy methods are more sample-efficient on HalfCheetah and a Gaussian policy slightly beats it on the low-randomness Lamp task. A simulation-trained One-leg assembly policy transferred zero-shot to a Franka Emika Panda and succeeded in 16 of 20 trials at 10 Hz <Cite id="dppo-2024" />.

ReinFlow injects learnable noise into a flow policy's path for exact per-step likelihoods, saving 82.63% of wall time against DPPO on legged locomotion <Cite id="reinflow-2025" />, and FPO instead builds a PPO-clip ratio from the conditional flow-matching loss <Cite id="fpo-2025" />. QF3 (UC Berkeley and Amazon FAR, October 2026), an off-policy method that adds the critic's action gradient to the flow-matching loss, is reported as the first off-policy flow RL method to train humanoid locomotion from scratch and transfer it zero-shot to hardware, with a 10× wall-clock speedup over the on-policy FPO++ <Cite id="qf3-2026" />.

ConRFT (Chen et al., 2025) fine-tunes a consistency-policy action head, a sampler distilled from a diffusion policy <Cite id="consistency-policy-2024" />, while freezing the visual encoders and transformer backbone of Octo-small on a 7-DoF Franka. Offline Cal-ConRFT pairs a consistency-based <Term id="behavior-cloning">behavior cloning</Term> loss with a Cal-QL critic, from 20 to 30 demonstrations per task, and online HIL-ConRFT adds human takeovers to the demonstration buffer <Cite id="conrft-2025" />.

ConRFT reports 96.3% mean <Term id="success-rate">success rate</Term> across eight tasks, 20 trials each, after 15 to 90 minutes of listed online training. ConRFT's headline 144% is a rounded relative gain over offline Cal-ConRFT's 39.4% mean, which the SFT baseline also scores. Online learning curves can include successes produced by human takeovers, and the paper warns of reward-classifier hacking and limited generalization <Cite id="conrft-2025" />. ConRFT says every compared method used interventions, but PA-RL reports fine-tuning OpenVLA autonomously with Cal-QL, from 40% to 70% in 40 real-world minutes <Cite id="pa-rl-2024" />.

pi_RL (Chen et al., 2026) fine-tunes flow-based policies with online PPO. Flow-Noise learns Gaussian noise for denoising transitions jointly with the velocity network and uses the joint likelihood of the denoising path in place of the executed action's marginal likelihood. Flow-SDE uses Gaussian transition likelihoods in a two-layer denoising and environment MDP, with one randomly chosen denoising step stochastic and the rest deterministic <Cite id="pi-rl-2026" />.

Main experiments fine-tune π0 and π0.5 in simulation on LIBERO, ManiSkill, MetaWorld and CALVIN, and gains under distribution shift do not consistently reach the five unseen MetaWorld ML45 tasks. A Real2Sim2Real case transfers zero-shot to a Franka Panda, reporting 40% success without a trial count <Cite id="pi-rl-2026" />.

## HIL-SERL: a human in the loop, RL on the robot

HIL-SERL (Luo et al., Science Robotics 2025) follows SERL, which learned PCB assembly, cable routing and object relocation in 25 to 50 minutes per policy <Cite id="serl-2024" />, and uses RLPD, off-policy RL with offline data mixed in <Cite id="rlpd-2023" />. Intervention transitions enter both the demonstration and RL buffers, autonomous ones only the RL buffer, and training typically starts from 20 to 30 demonstrations; Jenga whipping starts from 30 with no real-time takeovers <Cite id="hil-serl-2024" />.

HIL-SERL completes 100% of observed evaluation trials, 100 per task, except IKEA whole assembly with 10 trials and at most two attempts per sub-policy. Training takes 1 to 2.5 hours for nearly all tasks and 6 for timing-belt assembly, including scripted motion, rollouts, intended stops and computation. Against HG-DAgger with matched episodes and interventions, average success is 49.7% versus 100% and cycle time 9.6 versus 5.4 seconds <Cite id="hil-serl-2024" />.

Online learning curves can include human-assisted successes, the paper reports DP's dashboard-assembly success as both 18% and 28%, and Luo and colleagues did not test unstructured environments or extensive randomization <Cite id="hil-serl-2024" />. The [RL for Robotics module](/rl-sim2real/rl-for-robotics/) covers the off-policy context, and [parallel simulation RL](/rl-sim2real/parallel-sim-rl/) the simulation route.

Mulligan (Stanford, October 2026) starts each round of supervised collection at the initial states where the policy failed or has not been tried; with value-based action selection, it raised final-round success on three real tasks by 10 to 34 percentage points over HG-DAgger, scored on 2,550 held-out, blinded episodes <Cite id="mulligan-2026" />.

## Residual RL and distillation back into the generalist

Residual RL adds a learned correction to a fixed controller <Cite id="residual-rl-2018" />. PLD (Probe, Learn, Distill; Xiao et al., 2025) freezes a VLA, trains task-specific residual actors with off-policy RL, lets them recover from the states the base policy reaches, and distills the trajectories back into the generalist through SFT. Residual exploration carries no safety guarantee <Cite id="pld-2026" />.

<Image id="pld-gpu-insertion-2025" />

On LIBERO, averages are 99.2% for the model labelled OpenVLA against 91.8% for its baseline, and 97.2% against 93.4% for π0. On a four-task SimplerEnv suite, Octo-SFT rises from 71.8% to 96.6% and the WidowX carrot task from 43.3% to 93.9%; the printed average delta is +24.9, though the means differ by 24.8 <Cite id="pld-2026" />.

On a Franka, PLD records 30/30 randomized trials for cube pick-up and peg insertion, but 28/30 for a blue cube and 20/30 for a red one under changed clutter. On YAM, four GPU insertion and removal stages distill into one BC policy that runs at least an hour continuously with recovery, though per-stage one-shot success stays below 100% <Cite id="pld-2026" />.

RLDG (Xu et al., 2024) uses HIL-SERL specialists to generate data for fine-tuning OpenVLA and Octo, so the generalist never receives RL updates. In FMB single-object assembly, RL supplies insertion data while humans supply grasping and transport, and OpenVLA succeeds in 20/20 trials against 12/20 with human demonstrations <Cite id="rldg-2024" />. Relabeling suggests action quality, more than state distribution, drives the benefit; the method needs task rewards, speed-optimized RL data can cause premature object drops, and OpenVLA commands actions at 4 Hz while RL runs at 10 Hz <Cite id="rldg-2024" />.

## EXPO-FT: value-guided edits on a frontier VLA

EXPO (Perry Dong, Qiyang Li, Dorsa Sadigh and Chelsea Finn; ICLR 2026) trains a large flow or diffusion base policy with a stable imitation objective plus a lightweight Gaussian edit policy that nudges sampled actions toward higher value, avoiding gradients through the denoising chain, and reports up to 2 to 3× better sample efficiency on average <Cite id="expo-2025" />.

EXPO-FT, from Dong, Kuo-Han Hung, Tian Gao, Sadigh and Finn, extends EXPO to VLA action chunks and human teleoperation corrections on π0.5. Tasks the base cannot do zero-shot get imitation fine-tuning to around 40% success or above before online RL, and sparse binary rewards come from rule-based detectors over 95% accurate. It reports 30/30 on every evaluated task within an average of 19.1 minutes of online robot data across eight task variants <Cite id="expo-ft-2026" />.

<ExpoFtResults className="my-6" />

The paper calls HIL-SERL highly reliable in its original evaluations; this suite randomizes a much larger initial-state space, and the standard budget was too small for learning to start on Cube Pick and Pool Shot. With extra samples, HIL-SERL reaches 27/30 and 13/30 there <Cite id="expo-ft-2026" /> <Cite id="hil-serl-2024" />.

DSRL keeps the base policy frozen and runs RL over its latent-noise space <Cite id="dsrl-2025" />. Dong and Finn argue it has a ceiling: "If the skill a robot needs isn't already somewhere in what the base model learned during pretraining, no amount of noise-searching will produce the action ...". DSRL averages 19/30 in their comparison <Cite id="perry-dong-post-training-2026" /> <Cite id="expo-ft-2026" />. PrefPI repeatedly fits preference-conditioned policies on self-generated trajectories, then amplifies the preference signal through classifier-free guidance <Cite id="prefpi-2026" />.

<NoiseOrEdit className="my-6" />

Dong and Finn's September 2026 blog post says: "RL shows incredible promise in training frontier robotics models, but it is not yet a recipe. It's a craft." EXPO-FT still needs a human to define success, reset the scene and intervene, longer horizons strain the value function, and "Nineteen minutes of robot interaction is not nineteen minutes of post-training," because gradient updates dominate wall-clock time <Cite id="perry-dong-post-training-2026" />. Real-Time EXPO-FT lets a lightweight edit policy react to the latest observation while a slow VLA proposes chunks, and on four dynamic real tasks average performance rises from 42% to 97% <Cite id="realtime-expo-ft-2026" />; [real-time execution](/manipulation/realtime-execution/) covers the latency budgets.

A review of robotic deep RL case studies lists real-world challenges that research on games and simulated control seldom addresses <Cite id="ibarz-2021" />, and a 2025 survey of real-world successes calls stable, sample-efficient real-world RL a priority <Cite id="tang-drl-survey-2025" />.

## Two ways to spend a transition

An <Term id="on-policy">on-policy</Term> method can only update on data the current policy generated, so each batch is collected, consumed and discarded; PPO allows several minibatch epochs per batch, where plain policy gradient takes one step <Cite id="ppo-2017" />. An <Term id="off-policy">off-policy</Term> method improves one policy from data another produced, so experience accumulates in a <Term id="replay-buffer">replay buffer</Term>. Underneath is <Term id="q-learning">Q-learning</Term>: fit the value of a state-action pair and bootstrap from the best next action, even one never taken <Cite id="sutton-barto-2018" />.

<ReplayReuse className="my-6" />

TD3 reduced DDPG's overestimation bias with clipped double critics, delayed policy updates and target policy smoothing <Cite id="td3-2018" />. DDPG itself is a model-free actor-critic built around deterministic policy gradients for continuous actions <Cite id="ddpg-2016" />. Soft actor-critic added a maximum-entropy objective aimed at sample complexity and brittle convergence <Cite id="sac-2018" />.

### Why robotics defaulted to PPO anyway

With thousands of GPU environments, steps are nearly free and training stability is the scarce resource. SAC's authors credit on-policy training with stability at the price of "poor sample complexity", and call off-policy learning with neural function approximation "a major challenge for stability and convergence" <Cite id="sac-2018" />.

<Image id="isaac-gym-allegro-envs-2021" />

Rudin and colleagues trained ANYmal with 4,096 parallel robots, 98,304 steps per update and 1,500 updates in under twenty minutes on one workstation GPU, more than 122,880 environment steps per second <Cite id="rudin-2021" />. Minitaur's 160,000 control steps over about two hours average about 22 per second, below its 50 Hz rollout rate because resets and overhead count <Cite id="haarnoja-walk-2019" />. [Parallel simulation](/rl-sim2real/parallel-sim-rl) covers the first regime.

edits.before: Sample efficiency is how much experience a method needs to learn. Haarnoja and colleagues learned Minitaur locomotion from 160,000 control steps in about two hours of real-world time that includes resets and the operator . DayDreamer trained a Unitree A1 to roll over, stand and walk in one hour without a simulator, and ten more minutes of online learning taught it to withstand pushes; the authors intervened manually at the edge of the training area . A Walk in the Park demonstrates model-free quadruped learning directly on indoor and outdoor terrain with a carefully tuned controller . QT-Opt collected over 580,000 grasp attempts across seven robots in about 800 robot hours . The 2016 hand-eye preprint, which trained a supervised grasp-success predictor, reports about 800,000 grasp attempts over two months with 6 to 14 robots at a time . ## Offline reinforcement learning Offline reinforcement learning learns a policy from a fixed dataset of transitions without further environment interaction during training, then deploys it . It can reuse corpora like those in the [datasets module](/data-hardware/datasets), but a learned policy can choose actions outside the behavior distribution, Bellman targets then use erroneously high Q-values for them, and later backups propagate the errors without fresh feedback . BCQ showed that this extrapolation error leaves standard off-policy algorithms unable to learn from fixed batches , and CQL answers it by learning a lower bound on policy value, penalizing Q-values on out-of-distribution actions . ### Does any of this beat behavior cloning on robot data? Mandlekar and colleagues found batch RL weak on human demonstrations: neither BCQ nor CQL did well on human datasets, while history-dependent BC-RNN was a strong baseline . Kumar, Hong, Singh and Levine give sufficient conditions under which offline RL beats BC, assuming coverage of the optimal policy; with noisy data that improves coverage, conservative offline RL has a better bound than BC on equal expert data, while on expert data similar performance is a worst-case result. Their drawer-manipulation comparison, in simulation, pits BC on expert successes against CQL on noisy scripted data. Naive CQL can perform no better than BC . For teleoperation data, a supervised [behavior-cloning baseline](/manipulation/bc-foundations) is the simpler starting point, though newer real-robot results favor RL. Hindsight experience replay targets sparse binary rewards directly, storing transitions under their original goal and alternative goals and recomputing the reward for each, for example with goals achieved later in the same episode .

## The reset problem

A simulated episode restarts from a fresh state automatically, at only computational cost <Cite id="autonomous-rl-2022" />; a physical one ends wherever the robot is, and a person or a learned behavior has to put it back <Cite id="leave-no-trace-2017" />.

Zhu and colleagues name learning from raw sensory inputs, assigning rewards without hand-designed instrumentation, and learning without human episode resets as the requirements for real-world RL; their D'Claw hand trained unattended, but evaluation included manual resets for bead manipulation <Cite id="real-world-rl-ingredients-2020" />. Leave No Trace learns a reset policy alongside the forward policy and aborts before non-reversible states <Cite id="leave-no-trace-2017" />. VaPRL learns to reach curriculum-selected starting states, reducing manual resets in simulated robotics tasks <Cite id="vaprl-2021" />. Sharma and colleagues' EARL benchmark sums gaps to optimal deployment return over training and treats interventions as constrained costs, though its experiments still schedule resets during training <Cite id="autonomous-rl-2022" />.

<Term id="reset-free-learning">Reset-free learning</Term> replaces manual resets with learned recovery behaviors. Gupta and colleagues' MTRF sequences task-specific policies with a designer-provided task graph, and a D'Hand on a Sawyer arm learned valve reorientation and pipe insertion without manual episode resets. The setup still used supplied rewards, motion capture for the in-hand object, scripted arm motion for pickup and a user who positioned the objects, pipe insertion used frozen fingers, and the method assumes that successful upstream tasks leave valid starting states for downstream ones <Cite id="reset-free-rl-2021" />. Without such a task graph a person handles the reset, a cost the human-in-the-loop line pays deliberately <Cite id="hil-serl-2024" />.

## Where this goes from here

[Parallel simulation](/rl-sim2real/parallel-sim-rl) explains the sampler behind on-policy training, [why RL won locomotion](/rl-sim2real/why-rl-locomotion) which problems simulation represents faithfully, and [sim-to-real transfer](/rl-sim2real/sim2real-transfer) deployment. [RL fine-tuning](/manipulation/rl-finetuning) covers RL on pretrained vision-language-action policies: pi_RL applies online PPO to flow-based pi0 and pi0.5 policies, replacing flow-matching regression with a policy-gradient update <Cite id="pi-rl-2026" />, and PLD fine-tunes a generalist on hybrid recovery data from residual specialists <Cite id="pld-2026" />.

HIL-SERL reports 100% success in 100 evaluation trials per task, except IKEA whole assembly at 10 of 10. Nearly all tasks took one to two and a half hours of real-world training and timing-belt assembly six, counting scripted motion, rollouts and intended stops <Cite id="hil-serl-2024" />. ReF-HIL also uses successful human experience to shape critic values while constraining updates outside learned human-action neighborhoods <Cite id="ref-hil-2026" />. DROID <Cite id="droid-2024" /> and Open X-Embodiment <Cite id="open-x-embodiment-2023" /> supply large real-robot demonstration corpora, but both papers evaluate imitation policies, so offline RL on them needs reward labels the datasets do not define.

## Camera intrinsics

Intrinsics map pixels to rays through focal lengths, principal point and lens distortion. Zhang's method recovers them from a planar pattern at a few unknown orientations <Cite id="zhang-2000-calibration" />, and Kannala and Brandt's generic model covers wide-angle and fisheye lenses <Cite id="kannala-brandt-2006" />. Refit after any focus, resolution or crop change. AnyCalib estimates pixel rays from one image and fits several camera models to them, including pinhole and fisheye models; its formulation also handles cropped or stretched images <Cite id="anycalib-2025" />.

## Depth is a measurement model

Stereo depth error scales with the square of distance, and repetitive structures make matches ambiguous <Cite id="realsense-tuning-2026" />; the D400 datasheet adds saturation from specular reflections <Cite id="realsense-d400-datasheet-2026" />. Kinect random error grows from a few millimeters to about 4 cm at maximum range <Cite id="khoshelham-kinect-2012" />, and a joint depth-color calibration with a depth-distortion model beat the manufacturer's <Cite id="herrera-depth-color-2012" />.

Camera Depth Models uses RGB and raw sensor depth to predict corrected metric depth, with synthetic sensor noise used during training <Cite id="camera-depth-models-2025" />.

## Hand-eye calibration

Hand-eye calibration finds the gripper-to-camera transform for a wrist camera, or base-to-camera for a fixed one. Shiu and Ahmad cast it as $AX = XB$ <Cite id="shiu-ahmad-1989" />, Tsai and Lenz solved it in about ${}100 + 64N$ arithmetic operations for $N$ robot stations <Cite id="tsai-lenz-1989" />, and Park and Martin derived closed-form exact and least-squares solutions <Cite id="park-martin-1994" />. Daniilidis represents the motions with dual quaternions and solves rotation and translation together using singular value decomposition <Cite id="daniilidis-1999" />.

<Image id="baxter-gripper-wrist-camera" />

## π0: the action expert

π0 grafts a second transformer, the action expert of about 300M parameters, onto a pretrained <Term id="vision-language-model">vision-language model</Term> initialized from PaliGemma; the backbone handles image and text tokens, and the expert's 50 action tokens attend into it at every layer through shared self-attention. Inputs are 2 or 3 RGB images, language and proprioceptive state, and the model predicts H = 50 actions, executing 16 per inference at 20 Hz on UR5e and Franka or 25 at 50 Hz on the other robots <Cite id="pi0-2024" />. PaliGemma itself couples a SigLIP vision encoder to a Gemma language model for transfer across vision-language tasks <Cite id="paligemma-2024" />.

Where [Diffusion Policy](/manipulation/diffusion-policy/) denoises with a DDPM, π0 trains the expert with conditional flow matching on a straight path. Training samples noise $\varepsilon \sim \mathcal{N}(0, I)$, forms $A_t^\tau = \tau A_t + (1 - \tau)\varepsilon$, and regresses $v_\theta$ onto $u = A_t - \varepsilon$. Inference integrates from $\tau = 0$ to $\tau = 1$ in 10 forward-Euler steps, with the image-text-state prefix KV-cached once so each step recomputes only the action suffix <Cite id="pi0-2024" />. Lipman et al. found optimal-transport paths more efficient than diffusion paths for training and sampling <Cite id="lipman-flow-matching-2022" />.

edits.before: Cross-embodiment pre-training combines single-arm, dual-arm and mobile manipulators across 7 robot configurations. The base model reaches what the authors call "rudimentary proficiency", and complex tasks such as laundry folding use curated post-training data . PI says π0, π0-FAST and π0.5 executed chunks synchronously, waiting for inference after each one , which the RTC paper later compared with asynchronous execution on π0.5 . ## Why ten steps is enough A DDPM path curves through noise space, while rectified flow straightens paths so that coarse time steps simulate them accurately . Each Euler step costs a forward pass through the expert: π0 uses 10 steps , π0.6 uses five , and π0.7 also uses five . Consistency and one-step distillation, covered in [Diffusion Policy](/manipulation/diffusion-policy/), pursue the same saving. ## π0-FAST: compressed action tokens FAST traces the failure of per-dimension, per-timestep binning to highly correlated tokens, which make next-token prediction trivial; policies with this naive tokenization make no progress on table bussing at 20 Hz or T-shirt folding at 50 Hz . FAST instead applies a discrete cosine transform along time, rounds the coefficients and byte-pair-encodes the result, and its universal FAST+ tokenizer is trained on about one million one-second action chunks across embodiments , or "1M real robot action sequences" in PI's post . Trained on a 10k-hour cross-embodied mixture, π0-FAST matches π0's generalist performance with up to five times fewer GPU hours. Inference costs more: about 750 ms per one-second chunk on an NVIDIA 4090, against within 100 ms for diffusion π0, since decoding needs 30 to 60 tokens instead of ten steps . The Knowledge Insulation note reports that π0-FAST took twice as long to finish single-embodiment table bussing . ## π0.5 and Knowledge Insulation π0.5 targets open-world generalization . It keeps the π0 skeleton, adds training examples that interleave images, language commands, object detections, subtask predictions and low-level actions, and at inference first predicts a language subtask ("pick up the plate"), then conditions the action expert on it. In long-horizon mobile manipulation in new homes, removing either cross-embodiment data source significantly hurts home-task scores, while removing web data leaves those scores nearly unchanged but strongly hurts language following and subtask inference . The Knowledge Insulation paper turns the two-stage π0.5 approach into one stage: the expert trains with flow matching for continuous inference, and the backbone trains on discrete FAST tokens, vision-language data and planning data, with expert gradients stopped at the backbone keys and values . With a frozen backbone, shirt folding drops to 0%; on generalist table bussing, π0 needs 7.5 times as many training steps to match; and vision-language co-training also gives the joint-training baseline good language following without stop-gradient . The openpi π0.5 checkpoints were trained with KI, but the repository supports only the flow-matching head , so outside groups reimplement the FAST loss and KI . ## π0.6 and π*0.6: scaling and experience The π0.6 model card, dated November 17, 2025, initializes the backbone from Gemma3 4B, gives the action expert about 860M parameters and keeps expert gradients out of the backbone. Without task-specific fine-tuning, π0.6 folds laundry reliably and fully assembles the box 20% of the time, tasks that previously needed fine-tuning to succeed at all . In PI's Robot Olympics, fine-tuned π0.6 averaged 52% success and 72% task progress, while a fine-tuned standard VLM without π0.6's robot pre-training had no successes and 9% progress . π*0.6 uses Recap to learn from demonstrations, expert teleoperation corrections and autonomous experience, with a language-conditioned value function whose advantage, against a task-dependent threshold, gives each action a binary improvement indicator; human corrections are forced positive, and evaluation samples with the positive indicator . The report places this formulation closest to CFGRL , while outside groups find RL on flow-based π0 and π0.5 hard because flow matching makes action log-likelihoods intractable . The companion blog's example is a bad portafilter grasp that causes a later insertion failure . On a rig with two 6-DoF arms and 50 Hz joint-position control, on-robot experience more than doubles successful completions per hour for double-shot espresso and diverse laundry, tested on a button-up shirt, against offline RL plus demonstration fine-tuning. Failures fall by "about a factor of two" ("more than 2×" in the figure), the "90%+" summary excludes diverse laundry, and the box task reports stages separately, with remaining failures mostly in final placement . In PI's February 2026 partner report, Weave describes π0.6 folding laundry at a customer laundromat, while Ultra describes live order packing with a human intervention system that also collects training data . PI published MEM on March 3, 2026 . π0.6-MEM pairs a video encoder with a high-level policy that predicts updated natural-language summaries of earlier events, and handles tasks needing up to fifteen minutes of memory, such as recipe setup and kitchen cleanup. Its adaptation experiments train memory and memoryless policies on the same corrections, such as which way to open a refrigerator . ## RL tokens On March 19, 2026, PI described RL tokens: small actor and critic networks train online on a compressed, frozen token from π0.6, speeding up the most precise stages of four tasks by up to 3×; Ethernet insertion took two hours of training with 15 minutes of robot data . [RL fine-tuning](/manipulation/rl-finetuning/) covers the wider method family. ## π0.7: generalization as a prompting problem π0.7 treats underspecified prompts as the [generalization](/frontier/generalization/) bottleneck. It is π0.6 plus MEM at about 5B parameters, and training simulates real-time chunking delays of 0 to 12 timesteps, up to 240 ms on a 50 Hz robot , the training-time RTC method that on π0.6 matched inference-time RTC at lower compute . The context holds task and subtask language, with the subtask from a learned high-level policy or a human, and episode metadata on quality, speed and mistakes; training uses different subsets of this context but always keeps the joint or end-effector control-mode label. Space robotics is the design and operation of robots beyond Earth, from planetary rovers to station arms and satellite servicers. A signal needs 4 to 20 minutes to reach Mars <Cite id="jpl-ipn-pnt-2024" />, so rovers drive mostly on their own <Cite id="enav-perseverance-2026" />, and commercial servicers have docked with satellites in orbit since 2020 <Cite id="mev1-servicing-2025" />.

<Image id="perseverance-selfie-rochette-2021" />

## Autonomy paced by the speed of light

NASA and JPL rovers have used onboard autonomy since 2004 <Cite id="mer-mobility-software-2006" />. Sheridan's 1993 review found that space teleoperation had tended to avoid time delay by not teleoperating from the ground <Cite id="sheridan-time-delay-1993" />. The Mars Exploration Rovers layered goal-based driving over reactive and predictive safety checks, and drove over 11,000 m combined by October 2005 <Cite id="mer-mobility-software-2006" />. They were the first robots to use visual odometry on another world, and within two years it grew from an "extra credit" capability into a critical vehicle safety system <Cite id="mer-visual-odometry-2007" />.

In Perseverance's first Mars year, AutoNav evaluated 88 percent of the 17.7 km driven, against Opportunity's previous record of 2.4 km over fourteen years <Cite id="perseverance-autonomy-2023" />. It drove 699.9 m without humans reviewing the imagery and 347.7 m in one sol, both planetary rover records <Cite id="perseverance-autonomy-2023" />. Its Enhanced Autonomous Navigation runs on a single-core CPU and raised average daily driving distance by an order of magnitude <Cite id="enav-perseverance-2026" />. By October 28, 2024, it had evaluated the terrain for about 90 percent of 32.1 km <Cite id="enav-perseverance-2026" />.

Research addresses terrain risk at two stages. Endo and colleagues fuse terrain classifications and slip predictions into a distribution for risk-aware path planning, evaluated in simulation <Cite id="traversability-slip-2023" />. Kilic and colleagues detect slip from an IMU and wheel encoders, with field tests in a planetary analogue environment <Cite id="proprioceptive-slip-2022" />.

Since February 2026 Perseverance can [fix its own position](/classical/state-estimation/) by matching navcam panoramas to orbital imagery, to within 25 cm in about two minutes <Cite id="mars-global-localization-2026" />. In December 2025 JPL used [vision-language models](/manipulation/vla-models/) on the ground to generate Perseverance waypoints from HiRISE orbital imagery and terrain-slope data <Cite id="perseverance-ai-drive-2026" />. After a digital twin verified over 500,000 telemetry variables, the rover drove 210 m on December 8 and 246 m two days later <Cite id="perseverance-ai-drive-2026" />.

Onboard software also picks science targets. On Curiosity since 2016, AEGIS has increased science data return by selecting targets for the ChemCam laser spectrometer <Cite id="aegis-curiosity-2017" />. On Perseverance it picks SuperCam targets from wide-angle images during or right after long drives, without waiting for a ground cycle <Cite id="perseverance-autonomy-2023" />. In 2024 NASA described PIXL's "adaptive sampling" as the first use of AI on Mars to make autonomous decisions from real-time rock composition analysis <Cite id="pixl-adaptive-sampling-2024" />.

On April 19, 2021, Ingenuity made the first powered, controlled flight on another planet, in an atmosphere with about one percent of Earth's surface pressure <Cite id="ingenuity-first-flight-2021" />. Designed for five flights over thirty days, it flew 72 times in almost three years before NASA ended the mission in January 2024 <Cite id="ingenuity-mission-end-2024" />. NASA's accident investigation named the most likely cause: a lack of surface texture gave the navigation system too little information <Cite id="ingenuity-investigation-2024" />.

<Image id="ingenuity-mastcam-z-closeup-2021" />

## Living off the land: ISRU

MOXIE, on Perseverance, was the first demonstration of <Term id="in-situ-resource-utilization">in-situ resource utilization</Term> (ISRU) on another planet, making oxygen by solid-oxide electrolysis of atmospheric carbon dioxide <Cite id="moxie-sciadv-2022" />. A scaled-up version would make the tens of tons of oxygen an ascent rocket needs on Mars, instead of launching hundreds of tons from Earth <Cite id="moxie-sciadv-2022" />. Across sixteen runs MOXIE produced 122 grams of oxygen, peaking at 12 grams per hour at 98 percent purity or better, about twice NASA's original goals <Cite id="moxie-completion-2023" />. It concluded operations in September 2023 <Cite id="moxie-completion-2023" />.

<Image id="moxie-installation-perseverance-2020" />

Scaled ISRU means drilling and moving abrasive regolith in vacuum and cold. NASA's PRIME-1 suite reached the lunar south pole on Intuitive Machines' IM-2 lander in March 2025, where the lander, Athena, came to rest on its side in a crater <Cite id="prime-1-lunar-2025" />.

NASA put it about 400 m from its target and the mission at about ten hours of the ten days planned; the PRIME-1 team's 2026 paper gives about 500 m and 12 hours <Cite id="prime-1-lunar-2025" /><Cite id="hancock-prime1-2026" />. TRIDENT, Honeybee Robotics' one-metre rotary-percussive drill, executed its commanded motions, but with the lander on its side it could not reach the surface to excavate <Cite id="prime-1-lunar-2025" /><Cite id="hancock-prime1-2026" />. Initial data suggested the MSOLO mass spectrometer detected only gases of human origin, such as propellant and traces of Earth water <Cite id="prime-1-lunar-2025" />. In [evaluation](/data-hardware/evaluation-crisis/) terms PRIME-1 was one trial: the instruments worked while the landing cost the science <Cite id="prime-1-lunar-2025" />.

Firefly's Blue Ghost landed on March 2, 2025, four days before Athena, and all its NASA payloads operated <Cite id="blue-ghost-lister-2025" />. Its LISTER probe dug with gas to 1 m, the deepest robotic planetary subsurface thermal probe yet <Cite id="blue-ghost-lister-2025" />.

Learned locomotion meets the same regolith in analogue tests on the ground. In October 2026, Adrian Fuhrer, Marco Hutter and colleagues at ETH Zurich reported on a 2025 campaign in the ESA/DLR LUNA lunar analogue facility in Cologne, where the quadrupeds ANYmal-D and Magnecko walked loose regolith simulant and crater-like terrain. The robots could cross the simulant, but sinkage and slip, dust kicked up by foot contacts, and perception failures from overexposure, shadows and low-texture ground all degraded performance <Cite id="luna-legged-2026" />.

Cave exploration adds route uncertainty. PLGRIM connects local risk-aware planning to global exploration goals and was tested on robots in Martian-analogue lava tubes <Cite id="plgrim-2021" />. Other work remains at the mission-concept stage: Olsen and Alexis propose jumping legged robots for lava tubes <Cite id="mars-jumping-2023" />, while ReachBot's MELT study proposes locomotion through extendable and retractable limbs <Cite id="reachbot-melt-2024" />.

## Orbital robotics: servicing and removal

<Term id="on-orbit-servicing">On-orbit servicing</Term> covers satellite repair, refuelling, upgrades and debris removal <Cite id="space-manipulator-review-2025" />. It means matching a target's orbit, then docking with it or grasping it. An arm and its base satellite move each other, and in 1989 Umetani and Yoshida derived a generalized Jacobian from momentum conservation to control such arms <Cite id="umetani-yoshida-1989" />. A 2025 review organises capture control around free-floating and free-flying modes, from vision-based estimation to post-capture stabilisation <Cite id="space-manipulator-review-2025" />.

Relative navigation needs labelled spacecraft images. SPEED combines synthetic and real imagery for monocular pose estimation <Cite id="speed-challenge-2019" />; SPEED+ adds hardware-in-the-loop images with controlled poses and space-like illumination <Cite id="speedplus-2021" />. SPARK instead supplies simulated RGB and depth images labelled by spacecraft or debris class <Cite id="spark-2021" />.

The renderer has to reproduce the sensing problem. URSO uses Unreal Engine 4 to generate labelled views of spacecraft orbiting Earth <Cite id="urso-2019" />. SurRender's CPU ray tracer uses double precision to handle the scale difference between celestial distances and local target detail <Cite id="surrender-2021" />.

<OrbitalServicingTable className="my-6 wide-measure" />

ROTEX flew on Space Shuttle Columbia in early 1993, worked autonomously, under astronaut teleoperation and under ground control, and grasped free-floating objects <Cite id="rotex-1993" />. Japan's ETS-VII demonstrated autonomous rendezvous and docking between two satellites in 1998, with flight experiments for a 2 m, six-degree-of-freedom arm <Cite id="ets-vii-ard-2001" /><Cite id="ets-vii-robot-2001" />. In DARPA's 2007 Orbital Express, the ASTRO servicer autonomously captured NextSat and transferred propellant and a battery to it over four months <Cite id="orbital-express-2008" /><Cite id="boeing-orbital-express-2007" />.

On the International Space Station, Canadarm2, a 17 m arm, assembled the station and still grapples and berths arriving cargo vehicles <Cite id="canadarm2-csa-2024" />. Dextre, a two-armed robot that rides it, replaces exterior equipment including 100 kg batteries by <Term id="teleoperation">teleoperation</Term> from the ground <Cite id="dextre-csa-2024" />.

<Image id="dextre-canadarm2-iss-2017" />

In 2020 Northrop Grumman's MEV-1 made the first docking of two commercial spacecraft in orbit, capturing Intelsat 901 in the graveyard orbit above geosynchronous altitude and returning it to service <Cite id="mev1-servicing-2025" />. After five years it undocked, the first such undocking in that orbit, and moved to its next mission <Cite id="mev1-servicing-2025" />. On July 21, 2026, Northrop Grumman's Mission Robotic Vehicle launched with the DARPA-funded RSGS payload, twin robotic arms built by the U.S. Naval Research Laboratory <Cite id="rsgs-mrv-launch-2026" />. It will install small propulsion modules called mission extension pods to extend satellites' lives <Cite id="rsgs-mrv-launch-2026" />.

Debris is the uncooperative case, and ESA's 2026 report states that active debris removal is required to stop collisions multiplying debris <Cite id="esa-space-environment-2026" />. In 2024 Astroscale's ADRAS-J, flying for JAXA, inspected a discarded rocket upper stage in three fly-arounds and closed to about 15 m <Cite id="adras-j-15m-2024" />. No commercial spacecraft had come closer to debris, and the onboard collision-avoidance system aborted autonomously after an unexpected relative attitude anomaly <Cite id="adras-j-15m-2024" />.

By March 25, 2026, ADRAS-J had begun a controlled deorbit after 293 days in orbit <Cite id="adras-j-deorbit-2026" />. ADRAS-J2 targets launch in Japan's fiscal year 2027 to capture and remove an upper stage weighing about 3 t <Cite id="adras-j2-isar-2026" />.

NASA discontinued OSAM-1, a mission to refuel an unprepared satellite, in March 2024 after an independent review <Cite id="osam1-discontinued-2024" />. It cited technical, cost and schedule challenges and what it called a broader community evolution away from refuelling unprepared spacecraft, which left no committed partner <Cite id="osam1-discontinued-2024" />. In August 2026 NASA and Katalyst called off the LINK servicer's planned capture and boost of Swift, launched in 2004, over an attitude-control issue on the commercial spacecraft <Cite id="swift-boost-update-2026" />. NASA expected Swift to re-enter later in 2026 <Cite id="swift-boost-update-2026" />.

## What robot learning takes from it

In DARPA's 2007 Orbital Express, the ASTRO servicer autonomously captured NextSat and transferred propellant and a battery to it over four months <Cite id="orbital-express-2008" /><Cite id="boeing-orbital-express-2007" />.

On the International Space Station, Canadarm2, a 17 m arm, assembled the station and still grapples and berths arriving cargo vehicles <Cite id="canadarm2-csa-2024" />. Dextre, a two-armed robot riding it, replaces exterior equipment including 100 kg batteries by <Term id="teleoperation">teleoperation</Term> from the ground <Cite id="dextre-csa-2024" />.

<Image id="dextre-canadarm2-iss-2017" />

In 2020 Northrop Grumman's MEV-1 made the first docking of two commercial spacecraft in orbit, capturing Intelsat 901 in the graveyard orbit above geosynchronous altitude and returning it to service <Cite id="mev1-servicing-2025" />. After five years it undocked, the first such undocking in that orbit, and moved to its next mission <Cite id="mev1-servicing-2025" />. On July 21, 2026, Northrop Grumman's Mission Robotic Vehicle launched with the DARPA-funded RSGS payload, twin robotic arms built by the U.S. Naval Research Laboratory <Cite id="rsgs-mrv-launch-2026" />. It will install small propulsion modules called mission extension pods to extend satellites' lives <Cite id="rsgs-mrv-launch-2026" />.

Debris is the uncooperative case, and ESA's 2026 report states active debris removal is required to stop collisions multiplying debris <Cite id="esa-space-environment-2026" />. In 2024 Astroscale's ADRAS-J, flying for JAXA, inspected a discarded rocket upper stage in three fly-arounds and closed to about 15 m <Cite id="adras-j-15m-2024" />. No commercial spacecraft had come closer to debris; the onboard collision-avoidance system aborted autonomously after an unexpected relative attitude anomaly <Cite id="adras-j-15m-2024" />.

By March 25, 2026, ADRAS-J had begun a controlled deorbit after 293 days in orbit <Cite id="adras-j-deorbit-2026" />. ADRAS-J2 targets launch in Japan's fiscal year 2027 to capture and remove an upper stage weighing about 3 t <Cite id="adras-j2-isar-2026" />.

NASA discontinued OSAM-1, a mission to refuel an unprepared satellite, in March 2024 after an independent review <Cite id="osam1-discontinued-2024" />. It cited technical, cost and schedule challenges and what it called a broader community evolution away from refuelling unprepared spacecraft, which left no committed partner <Cite id="osam1-discontinued-2024" />. In August 2026 NASA and Katalyst cancelled the LINK servicer's planned capture and boost of Swift, launched in 2004, over an attitude-control issue on the commercial spacecraft <Cite id="swift-boost-update-2026" />. NASA expected Swift to re-enter later in 2026 <Cite id="swift-boost-update-2026" />.

## What robot learning takes from it

Learned control has flown on NASA's Astrobee free-flyers aboard the ISS. In 2025 Banerjee and colleagues reported the first in-space test of learned warm starts for trajectory optimization, while a convex solver still enforced safety <Cite id="banerjee-warm-starts-2025" />. The network cut solver iterations by 60 percent with rotational dynamics and 50 percent with in-distribution obstacles <Cite id="banerjee-warm-starts-2025" />. On May 27, 2025, the Naval Research Laboratory's APIARY team ran what it calls the first reinforcement-learning control of a free-flyer in space, with a policy trained in randomized simulation <Cite id="apiary-astrobee-2025" />.

The Space Robotics Bench authors say costly technology demonstrations and limited data severely hinder robot learning in space <Cite id="space-robotics-bench-2025" />. A September 2026 review adds space-specific dynamics and sensing, limited onboard resources and stringent safety requirements <Cite id="ai-space-robot-ops-review-2026" />. AI4MARS offers 326,000 crowdsourced terrain labels on 35,000 rover images, and a model trained on it exceeded 96 percent accuracy <Cite id="ai4mars-2021" />.

Space shares its [reliability](/frontier/reliability-gap/) bar with [surgical robotics](/adjacent/surgical/). Ingenuity flew more than fourteen times its five planned flights <Cite id="ingenuity-mission-end-2024" />, while OSAM-1 was cancelled before flight <Cite id="osam1-discontinued-2024" />. AEGIS and the digital-twin check on AI-planned drives both add autonomy in bounded, verified steps <Cite id="aegis-curiosity-2017" /><Cite id="perseverance-ai-drive-2026" />.

## Deformables and the long tail

A wooden block rests on one of six sides. A towel can be bunched up in more ways than any state estimator will ever enumerate, and some tasks add water, grease, or peanut butter <Cite id="holson-olympics-2025" />. Cloth, liquids, and compliant packaging fill Holson's task list: hang a dress shirt that starts with one sleeve inside out, clean peanut butter off your own manipulator.

Cloth manipulation depends on how the robot reduces the starting disorder. FlingBot learns a pick, stretch and fling primitive from visual observations <Cite id="flingbot-2021" />. SpeedFolding predicts paired gripper poses for bimanual actions, first smoothing the garment and then folding it along user-specified lines <Cite id="speedfolding-2022" />. Cloth Funnels chooses between flings and pick-and-place actions to bring garments into a canonical shape and aligned pose for later skills <Cite id="cloth-funnels-2022" />.

## Naive joint training

Fine-tuning a pretrained network through a random head distorts its features and raises out-of-distribution error <Cite id="kumar-finetuning-distorts-2022" />. The KI paper finds the same in VLAs: gradients from a new action expert degrade the backbone, slowing training and weakening language following, so that π0, told to bus a spoon into the bin, grasps trash <Cite id="knowledge-insulation-paper-2025" />.

ChatVLA calls this spurious forgetting, robot training overwriting visual-text alignments <Cite id="chatvla-2025" />. Between robot tasks, though, pretrained VLAs resist forgetting, and simple experience replay sometimes removes it <Cite id="vla-continual-forgetting-2026" />.

edits.before:
## Limits and alternatives

Stopping expert gradients does not adapt the backbone: with the backbone frozen, the paper's shirt-folding policy scores 0%. FAST supervision supplies that signal, and vision-language co-training can give plain joint training good language following without stop-gradient <Cite id="knowledge-insulation-paper-2025" />.

GR00T N1 freezes the language part of its VLM <Cite id="gr00t-n1-2025" />. NVIDIA reports that N1.5, which froze the whole VLM among other changes, raised real GR-1 language following from 46.6% to 93.3% <Cite id="gr00t-n1-5-2025" />, and N1.6 unfreezes the top 4 layers <Cite id="gr00t-n1-6-2025" />.

BLIP-2 bridges frozen image encoders and language models <Cite id="blip2-2023" />; VLM2VLA writes actions as language and trains only LoRA adapters <Cite id="vlm2vla-2025" />, and UAM keeps over 95% of its VLM's multimodal capability with no freezing, gradient stopping or co-training <Cite id="uam-forgetting-2026" />. Figure's Helix instead backpropagates from its fast policy into the VLM through their shared latent vector <Cite id="helix-2025" />, and HybridVLA trains discrete and diffusion action prediction together <Cite id="hybridvla-2025" />. InstructVLA jointly trains reasoning and action generation on vision-language and robot instruction data using mixture-of-experts adaptation <Cite id="instructvla-2025" />.

## Results

A many-embodiment π0 generalist needs 7.5 times the training steps of π0.5 + KI to reach similar table-bussing performance, and single-embodiment π0-FAST specialists need twice the wall-clock time from slow inference. Table bussing is scored at ten episodes per task and policy. When a mobile robot moves unseen objects into an open drawer, web-data co-training boosts generalization most, and language following improves but stays imperfect <Cite id="knowledge-insulation-paper-2025" /> <Cite id="knowledge-insulation-2025" />.

In third-party fine-tuning, π0.5 with KI stays near zero on out-of-distribution task perturbations, so KI alone does not fix out-of-distribution language generalization <Cite id="apt-action-expert-pretraining-2026" />. A reimplemented co-training plus KI baseline trailed standard behavior cloning on mean LIBERO-PRO and LIBERO-Plus success <Cite id="anchor-align-2026" />, though the dual FAST and flow objective mitigates forgetting more than flow alone <Cite id="garg-self-demonstrated-control-2026" />. Across seven VLAs, VQA co-training goes with better knowledge retention <Cite id="act2answer-2026" />, and in Toyota Research Institute's 89-policy study, training only on robot data cost the VLM backbone its ability to generate language <Cite id="lbm-cotraining-2026" />.

## Stage 3: imitation baseline

[Behavior cloning](/manipulation/bc-foundations/) trains on expert states and then visits its own; DAgger formalized why errors compound and why corrective labels on learner-induced states change the problem <Cite id="dagger-2011" />. Start with the smallest closed-loop baseline, such as an image encoder and MLP on one camera, task and action convention, and debug alignment, normalization and reset diversity before adding scale. robomimic found results sensitive to design choices, demonstration quality and stopping criteria <Cite id="robomimic-2021" />.

Then add temporal structure: ACT predicts action chunks <Cite id="act-aloha-2023" />, and Diffusion Policy models a multimodal distribution over action sequences <Cite id="diffusion-policy-2023" />.

## Stage 4: action contract

Among [action spaces](/manipulation/action-spaces/), joint positions are mechanism-specific, while end-effector deltas share a task-space convention across compatible controllers. ## The hardware wall

<Image id="jetson-agx-orin-auledas-2024" />

Its baseline π0 has 2.7B parameters and models three 224×224 cameras, 32 language tokens, 14 action dimensions, chunk size 50, 10 denoising steps, batch size one, and BF16 or FP16. Excluding network, sensor and execution latency, it predicts 162.5 inferences per second on H100 and 19.0 on Jetson Thor. A hypothetical 9.1B π0-L reaches 3.9 on Thor, all three π0 components are memory-bound there, and on B100 raising denoising steps from 10 to 50 multiplies total latency by 2.15 <Cite id="vla-perf-2026" />.

VLA-Perf calls 10 Hz inference "acceptable" and 100 Hz "high-performance" relative to common camera rates. Thor's predicted 19 Hz clears the first; the authors propose smaller models, fewer denoising steps or lower-precision quantization for the second <Cite id="vla-perf-2026" />. NVIDIA's Jetson AI Lab measured a different setup, π0.5 with action horizon 10 on Jetson AGX Thor, at about 132 ms in PyTorch BF16 and 49 ms with FP8 plus NVFP4 <Cite id="jetson-ai-lab-openpi-thor" />.

RT-2's 55B model ran at 1 to 3 Hz <Cite id="rt2-2023" />, and the 7B OpenVLA runs at about 6 Hz on an RTX 4090 but 1.2 Hz on its evaluation A5000 <Cite id="openvla-2024" />. OpenVLA-OFT's parallel decoding of chunked continuous actions raised throughput 26x and average success from 76.5% to 97.1% <Cite id="openvla-oft-2025" />. Dexmal and StepFun ran π0 with two camera views in 27.3 ms on one RTX 4090 <Cite id="realtime-vla-2025" />, and Fast-in-Slow, which embeds a fast action module in its VLM, reaches 117.7 Hz control with eight-action chunks <Cite id="fast-in-slow-2025" />.

In VLA-Perf, server placement depends on the network: synchronous π0 on an RTX 4090 takes 38.7 ms over WiFi 6 against Thor's 52.6 ms, but 55.7 ms over 5G, and B100 over 4G with a slow cloud link takes 273.4 ms <Cite id="vla-perf-2026" />.

## Three ways to hand off a chunk

<Term id="action-chunking">Chunking</Term> captures temporal dependencies in demonstrations at the cost of reactivity to unexpected states <Cite id="bidirectional-decoding-2024" />. Let inference take $d$ milliseconds during the current chunk.

Synchronous execution runs part of a chunk, pauses for inference, then resumes, the default in many prior works <Cite id="real-time-chunking-2025" />. π0 executes 16 of its 50 actions on its 20 Hz UR5e and Franka setups and 25 on the other 50 Hz robots <Cite id="pi0-2024" />, and Physical Intelligence ran π0, π0-FAST and π0.5 synchronously before RTC <Cite id="pi-real-time-chunking-blog-2025" />. The RTC paper links stop-start motion to distribution shift <Cite id="real-time-chunking-2025" />.

Naive switching jumps to the new chunk on arrival. That removes dead time but adds a discontinuity: the new chunk comes from an observation $d$ milliseconds old, and the command steps by the two chunks' disagreement in one tick <Cite id="real-time-chunking-2025" />.

<Term id="temporal-ensembling">Temporal ensembling</Term>, ACT's 2023 method, averages each timestep's predictions with weights that favour older ones <Cite id="act-aloha-2023" />, but averaging predictions from different modes need not give a valid action. In RTC's π0.5 real-robot comparison, both ensembling variants triggered the robot's protective stop at +100 and +200 ms of injected latency <Cite id="real-time-chunking-2025" />.

Real-Time Chunking inpaints the next chunk while the current one executes, fully weighting the first $d$ actions, which execute during inference, and works on diffusion and flow policies without retraining <Cite id="real-time-chunking-2025" /> <Cite id="pi-real-time-chunking-blog-2025" />. On six π0.5 real-robot tasks, its aggregate throughput did not degrade at +0, +100 or +200 ms of injected delay, and it lit matches precisely at total delays above 300 ms <Cite id="real-time-chunking-2025" />.

VLASH rolls the robot state forward with the previous chunk and cuts reaction latency up to 11.8x against synchronous inference <Cite id="vlash-2025" />, and A2C2's small per-step correction head gains 23 percentage points of success over RTC <Cite id="a2c2-2025" />. FutureRTC predicts execution-time visual features and corrects rolled-forward proprioception while keeping the underlying policy unchanged <Cite id="futurertc-2026" />. Event-triggered inference sets the inference gap by scene change, averaging 95% real-world success <Cite id="event-triggered-vla-2026" />. SmolVLA's asynchronous stack decouples prediction from execution <Cite id="smolvla-2025" />, and on a local network its round trips stay under 100 ms while tasks finish about 2x faster <Cite id="lerobot-async-inference-2025" />.

## Training the tolerance in

Black et al. (2025) simulate the delay in training, which avoids inference-time inpainting's added latency and works better at higher delays <Cite id="training-time-rtc-2025" />. π0.7 trains with simulated delays of 0 to 12 timesteps, at most 240 ms on a 50 Hz robot <Cite id="pi07-2026" />, and Soft RTC's medium overlap window cuts high-delay action jerk by 9.6% against hard training-time RTC <Cite id="soft-rtc-2026" />.

Chronos Policy, from Changhao Wang, Jaden Clark and Shuran Song at Stanford (October 2026), tells a diffusion transformer when each observation was captured and when each action will run, and randomizes both timings in training. On a simulated conveyor pick-and-place with inference delays up to 200 ms, it kept 76.4% success where Diffusion Policy fell to 1.8%, over 450 episodes per method and condition. ChunkTrust (September 2026) infers how many actions to execute before replanning from the policy's own outputs while it runs. π0 integrated its flow with 10 Euler steps per chunk <Cite id="pi0-2024" />, π0.6 cut that to 5 <Cite id="pi06-model-card-2025" />, and π0.7's minimal variant takes 38 ms on one H100 with three cameras <Cite id="pi07-2026" />.

FASTER finds reaction time set by the time to first action and the execution horizon, and compresses the immediate reaction to a single denoising step <Cite id="faster-flow-vla-2026" />. For token-based VLAs, PD-VLA's parallel decoding recovers 2.52 times the execution frequency <Cite id="pd-vla-2025" />.

edits.before:
<span id="two-ways-to-use-imagined-experience" />
## A model can plan each step or train a policy in imagination

A planner rolls sampled action sequences through the model, executes the best first action and replans, so a new goal or cost needs no retraining, at the price of many rollouts per real step ([reward design and MPC](/rl-sim2real/reward-design-mpc/)). In 2016 Finn and Levine combined action-conditioned video prediction with MPC so a real robot could push novel objects <Cite id="deep-visual-foresight-2016" />. TD-MPC2 trained one 317M-parameter agent on 80 tasks <Cite id="tdmpc2-2023" />, and PointWorld, trained on about 2 million trajectories, plans with MPC at 0.1 s per inference on a real Franka without demonstrations <Cite id="pointworld-2026" />.

Dreamer instead trains a policy on trajectories imagined in a learned latent space <Cite id="dreamer-2019" />, and DreamerV3 covers more than 150 tasks with one configuration <Cite id="dreamerv3-2023" />. Dreamer 4 learns purely offline, a setting its authors tie to robotics, where interaction "can be unsafe and slow" <Cite id="dreamer4-2025" />. [Latent dynamics](/world-models/latent-dynamics/) covers these agents.

Stochastic Value Gradients provides an earlier route to differentiating through learned dynamics: it expresses randomness as external noise and uses real environment observations to limit compounded rollout error <Cite id="stochastic-value-gradients-2015" />.

<span id="uncertainty-aware-models" />
## Uncertainty estimates keep policies from exploiting model errors

A policy trained on a model "tends to exploit regions where insufficient data is available", which ME-TRPO counters with an ensemble <Cite id="me-trpo-2018" />. PETS, a probabilistic ensemble, matches model-free asymptotic performance with 8 and 125 times fewer samples than SAC and PPO on half-cheetah <Cite id="pets-2018" />.

MBPO keeps rollouts short and "branched from real data" <Cite id="mbpo-2019" />. In [offline RL](/rl-sim2real/offline-rl/), MOPO penalizes reward by model uncertainty <Cite id="mopo-2020" />. MOReL learns a pessimistic decision process from offline data and trains its policy within that process <Cite id="morel-2020" />.

MB-MPO meta-learns a policy that adapts to each member of a dynamics ensemble with one policy-gradient step, placing model disagreement inside the adaptation problem <Cite id="model-based-meta-policy-2018" />. CBOP weights model-based and model-free value estimates by their epistemic uncertainty and uses a lower bound on the posterior estimate for conservative offline learning <Cite id="bayesian-model-value-expansion-2022" />.

<span id="why-physical-robots-make-the-model-harder" />
## Robots see only part of the state, yet learn useful models in minutes to hours

A robot observation is partial: cameras miss forces, friction and compliance, and RGBD gave an 80% improvement in fabric-folding success over RGB <Cite id="visuospatial-foresight-2020" />. Data is narrow too: Hansen and Wang call world-model hallucination "inherently a data coverage issue" and adapt a model to unseen simulated environments with 50 trajectories <Cite id="wm-hallucination-2026" />.

Chenyuan Zhou, Yining Hong, Jiajun Wu and colleagues at Stanford and elsewhere (October 2026) condition a video world model on a 32-dimensional latent for hidden factors such as friction or mass, fitted at test time from one or two interactions while the model stays frozen <Cite id="t2z-2026" />. Averaged over four real-robot tasks, the adapted model's mean tracking error fell from 19.30 to 10.85 pixels against the same model without a latent <Cite id="t2z-2026" />. Actions it picked succeeded 70.80% of the time against 26.47% for the model without a latent, though the paper does not state trial counts <Cite id="t2z-2026" />.

PDDM learned contact-rich manipulation on a 24-DoF hand from 4 real hours <Cite id="pddm-2019" />. DayDreamer ran Dreamer online on 4 robots without simulators; a quadruped learned to stand up and walk in 1 hour <Cite id="daydreamer-2022" />. SSRL adds a learned force ensemble to known Lagrangian dynamics and learned Go1 gaits from a few minutes of data <Cite id="ssrl-2024" />.

## Model-based learning pays off when real interaction is expensive

It fits when interaction is expensive, goals change faster than dynamics and planning fits the latency budget; it fits less well when observations omit contact state or resets are cheap. ### Perception

Perception turns sensor streams into a model of the scene: which objects exist, where they are, how they move and what the road permits. Waymo's encoder fuses camera, lidar and radar inputs over time <Cite id="waymo-foundation-model-2025" />, and Waymo argues that no single sensor can replicate that redundant view <Cite id="waymo-ai-lessons-2026" />. BEVFormer, a camera-only bird's-eye-view detector, matched lidar-based baselines on the nuScenes test set <Cite id="bevformer-2022" />.

Point-cloud detectors make different choices about geometry. PointPillars organizes points into vertical columns for a 2D detector <Cite id="pointpillars-2018" />; PV-RCNN combines voxel convolutions with point-level features <Cite id="pv-rcnn-2019" />. CenterPoint detects object centres, estimates size, orientation and velocity, and links detections by nearest-centre matching <Cite id="centerpoint-2020" />.

<Image id="waymo-roof-sensor-suite-2025" />

nuScenes, 1,000 scenes of 20 seconds, was the first dataset with a full vehicle sensor suite: 6 cameras, 5 radars and 1 lidar <Cite id="nuscenes-2020" />. The Waymo Open Dataset added 1,150 scenes of synchronized lidar and camera data <Cite id="waymo-open-dataset-2020" />. By its own metric it was 15 times more diverse than the largest earlier camera-plus-lidar set <Cite id="waymo-open-dataset-2020" />. Box detectors struggle with general, out-of-vocabulary objects, so the Occ3D benchmark predicts the occupancy and semantics of the whole scene <Cite id="occ3d-2023" />.

Driving benchmarks separate the outputs they test. KITTI covers stereo, optical flow, odometry and 3D detection <Cite id="kitti-benchmark-2012" />; Cityscapes targets pixel-level and instance-level semantic labels <Cite id="cityscapes-2016" />. BDD100K combines multiple driving tasks with geographic and weather diversity <Cite id="bdd100k-2018" />. Argoverse couples tracking and forecasting data with detailed maps <Cite id="argoverse-2019" />, and Argoverse 2 separates annotated sensor, unlabeled lidar and motion-forecasting collections <Cite id="argoverse2-2023" />.

Every later stage inherits a perception error. At Tempe in 2018 the system first detected a pedestrian 5.6 seconds before impact <Cite id="ntsb-uber-2019" />. It classified her in turn as a vehicle, an unknown object and a bicyclist, and never predicted her path correctly <Cite id="ntsb-uber-2019" />.

### Prediction

Prediction estimates what every other agent will do over the next several seconds. The future is multi-modal: a pedestrian may cross or wait, and a predictor that averages the two forecasts a path through neither. The Waymo Open Motion Dataset made interactive forecasting a benchmark: over 100,000 scenes of 20 seconds at 10 Hz, more than 570 hours over 1,750 km of roads <Cite id="waymo-open-motion-2021" />.

Early predictors drew agent histories and map features into a top-down image for a convolutional network. VectorNet replaced that raster with a hierarchical graph network over vectorized polylines <Cite id="vectornet-2020" />. It matched or beat the raster with over 70 percent fewer parameters and an order of magnitude less computation <Cite id="vectornet-2020" />. MotionLM then cast multi-agent forecasting as language modeling over discrete motion tokens <Cite id="motionlm-2023" />.

A distribution over anchor paths preserves several candidate futures and their uncertainty <Cite id="multipath-2019" />. Road-topology graphs make lane connections part of the predictor <Cite id="lanegcn-2020" />; dynamics-aware recurrent models constrain forecasts to feasible agent motions <Cite id="trajectron-plus-plus-2020" />. Attention layers can combine road geometry, traffic signals and motion histories <Cite id="wayformer-2022" />, while learned intention queries separate broad motion choices from local trajectory refinement <Cite id="motion-transformer-2022" />.

### Planning

edits.before:
On nuPlan, the first closed-loop machine-learning planning benchmark <Cite id="nuplan-2021" />, an extremely simple planner built on rule-based priors won the 2023 challenge <Cite id="dauner-misconceptions-2023" />. Dauner and colleagues found learned planners limited in complex scenarios <Cite id="dauner-misconceptions-2023" />.

ChauffeurNet, Waymo's 2018 imitative planner, found standard behavior cloning on 30 million examples insufficient, even with perception preparing its inputs and a controller executing its outputs <Cite id="chauffeurnet-2018" />. It perturbed the expert's driving into collisions and off-road excursions and added losses that penalize them <Cite id="chauffeurnet-2018" />. Manipulation later rediscovered that fix for covariate shift, as [behavior cloning foundations](/manipulation/bc-foundations/) explains.

Closed-loop tests ask what happens after the planner acts. CARLA provides configurable sensors and environmental conditions for urban-driving simulation <Cite id="carla-2017" />. Bench2Drive tests separate interactive driving scenarios across locations and weather in CARLA <Cite id="bench2drive-2024" />. TrafficSim learns a joint policy for surrounding actors from human driving data, so their behaviour can be simulated together <Cite id="trafficsim-2021" />.

### Control

Control turns a planned trajectory into steering, brake and throttle commands, and holds the vehicle on it despite disturbances, tire nonlinearity and actuator delay. Paden's survey covers the feedback path-tracking families: pure pursuit, Lyapunov-based trajectory tracking and model-predictive control <Cite id="paden-2016" />. A learned planner outputs a trajectory, and a classical [controller](/classical/control/) tracks it.

### Modular versus end-to-end

Each interface between stages is a lossy summary, and an upstream error cannot be corrected downstream. A 2024 survey frames the trade: end-to-end systems optimize perception and planning features jointly, while modular designs are easier to interpret and debug <Cite id="e2e-ad-survey-2024" />. UniAD kept the task structure but trained it as one network, with stages linked by unified query interfaces <Cite id="uniad-2023" />. Waymo's EMMA, built on a multimodal large language model foundation like Gemini, maps raw camera data to driving outputs written as text <Cite id="emma-2024" />.

On NAVSIM, open-loop results on real data did not reflect closed-loop performance <Cite id="navsim-2024" />. Simple methods such as TransFuser matched large architectures such as UniAD <Cite id="navsim-2024" />. Waymo says its own foundation model has significant benefits over both pure end-to-end and modular approaches <Cite id="waymo-foundation-model-2025" />.

edits.before:
Every deployed level 4 system runs inside an <Term id="operational-design-domain">operational design domain</Term>, a defined geography, road set, speed range and weather envelope. Waymo's crash comparisons align the human benchmark to the same vehicle types, road types and locations <Cite id="waymo-crash-rates-2025" />.

On June 24, 2026, the UNECE World Forum for Harmonization of Vehicle Regulations adopted the first global regulations for fully autonomous driving systems <Cite id="un-ads-regulation-2026" />. Manufacturers must show that test environments, including virtual testing tools, meet strict credibility criteria, and that the system poses no unreasonable risk <Cite id="un-ads-regulation-2026" />. In the US, DOT and NHTSA announced an AV framework on April 24, 2025. On March 16, 2026, NHTSA proposed amending federal safety standards for automated vehicles without manual controls <Cite id="nhtsa-av-framework-2026" />.

In July 2026 NHTSA exempted Zoox's purpose-built robotaxi from parts of eight of those standards for commercial deployment <Cite id="nhtsa-zoox-exemption-2026" />. The exemption runs two years, for up to 2,500 vehicles in any 12-month period <Cite id="nhtsa-zoox-exemption-2026" />.

### The long tail

The technical obstruction is the <Term id="long-tail">long tail</Term>: scenarios that are individually rare and collectively decisive, such as an officer waving cars through a red light. No driving log holds enough of any one of them to learn from. Waymo's WOD-E2E benchmark collects 4,021 segments, about 12 hours, of scenarios that occur less than 0.03 percent of the time <Cite id="wod-e2e-2025" />.

Generative simulation is the industry's main answer. Waymo's World Model, built on Google DeepMind's Genie 3 and announced in February 2026, generates camera and lidar data controllable by driving actions, scene layout and language <Cite id="waymo-world-model-2026" />. Waymo built it to rehearse events "from a tornado to a casual encounter with an elephant" <Cite id="waymo-world-model-2026" />. The same post reported nearly 200 million fully autonomous miles on real roads and billions in virtual worlds <Cite id="waymo-world-model-2026" />.
