### The measurement problem

Kalra and Paddock's 2016 RAND study found that test driving alone would need hundreds of millions of miles, sometimes hundreds of billions, to show safety <Cite id="kalra-paddock-2016" />. Mobileye's Responsibility-Sensitive Safety defines safe longitudinal and lateral distances as a white-box, interpretable model <Cite id="rss-2017" />. Its authors warned that without such standards the field risked a "winter of autonomous driving" <Cite id="rss-2017" />. Koopman argues that "safe enough" also requires no risk hot spots, such as reckless driving or risk shifted onto vulnerable populations, plus standards conformance and accountability <Cite id="koopman-safe-enough-2026" />.

<AvSafetyMiles className="my-6" />

US companies must report crashes but not the miles they log, so crash rates are unknown for operators that do not volunteer mileage <Cite id="iihs-waymo-2026" />. NHTSA has also streamlined its Standing General Order on crash reporting <Cite id="nhtsa-av-framework-2026" />. California's DMV says its disengagement reports are not designed for comparison across companies, and deployment-permit operations need not report disengagements at all <Cite id="ca-dmv-av-miles-2026" />.

In September 2026, Chris Paxton argued that an automated system should be judged by its potential for catastrophic failure, which is much higher for a truck: it needs far longer to stop, and when one breaks down on a highway the law requires warning flares that a truck with no one aboard cannot set out <Cite id="paxton-autonomous-trucks-2026" />. He expected driverless trucks to spread over the following year mainly in China and the US Sun Belt, and put highways where ice forms years away <Cite id="paxton-autonomous-trucks-2026" />.

### The deployment record

Waymo's peer-reviewed 2025 study covered 56.7 million rider-only miles through January 2025 <Cite id="waymo-crash-rates-2025" />. Against human benchmarks on the same roads, it found statistically significant lower rates of any-injury-reported, airbag-deployment and suspected-serious-injury crashes <Cite id="waymo-crash-rates-2025" />. Vehicle-to-vehicle intersection crashes with any injury fell 96 percent, with no significant disbenefit in any of its 11 crash-type groups <Cite id="waymo-crash-rates-2025" />.

Waymo's own safety hub reports 271.3 million rider-only miles through June 2026 <Cite id="waymo-safety-hub-2026" />. Over the same distance it counts 95 percent fewer serious-injury-or-worse crashes and 82 percent fewer injury-causing crashes than human drivers <Cite id="waymo-safety-hub-2026" />. IIHS found that Waymo's driverless vehicles in San Francisco, Phoenix, Los Angeles and Austin had 68 percent fewer police-reportable crashes per mile than human drivers <Cite id="iihs-waymo-2026" />.

Tesla says it launched unsupervised rides in Miami, Orlando and Tampa in July 2026 and expanded its unsupervised area in Austin <Cite id="tesla-q2-2026-update" />. Baidu reported in August 2026 that Apollo Go had reached 28 cities and more than 240 million fully driverless kilometres <Cite id="baidu-q2-2026" />. Aurora began driverless customer deliveries between Dallas and Houston in May 2025 after closing its safety case <Cite id="aurora-driverless-launch-2025" />. By its count it drove nearly 440,000 driverless miles through June 2026 with zero collisions attributed to its system, and expected to end the year with 200 driverless trucks <Cite id="aurora-q2-2026" />.

On March 18, 2018, an Uber ATG test vehicle in Tempe, Arizona struck and killed a 49-year-old pedestrian crossing N. Mill Avenue at night, pushing a bicycle, where there was no crosswalk <Cite id="ntsb-uber-2019" />. The system judged a collision imminent 1.2 seconds before impact, and its design precluded emergency braking for crash mitigation alone, relying on the operator <Cite id="ntsb-uber-2019" />. The operator was streaming a television show, glancing down until about one second before the crash <Cite id="ntsb-uber-2019" />. Every layer failed at once, the correlated-safeguard problem the [reliability gap](/frontier/reliability-gap/) article examines.

On October 2, 2023, a driverless Cruise vehicle dragged a pedestrian about 20 feet before stopping. Under a September 2024 consent order, Cruise agreed to a \$1.5 million penalty for crash reports that omitted those details <Cite id="nhtsa-cruise-consent-2024" />. In December 2024 GM stopped funding Cruise's robotaxi work, citing the time and resources needed to scale it <Cite id="gm-cruise-refocus-2024" />.

## The relation to robot learning

The imitation toolkit was built on driving before it reached arms. DAgger, the canonical fix for covariate shift, was demonstrated on steering a car in a 3D racing game <Cite id="dagger-2011" />. It cuts the growth of mistakes over the horizon from quadratic to linear <Cite id="dagger-2011" />. On 500,000 hours of driving, Waymo found that forecasting and planning improve as a power law in compute, and closed-loop metrics improve too <Cite id="waymo-scaling-laws-2025" />.

RAD trains end-to-end policies by reinforcement learning in photorealistic 3D Gaussian splatting replicas, to address imitation's causal confusion and open-loop gap <Cite id="rad-2025" />. It reports a 3x lower collision rate <Cite id="rad-2025" />.

### The convergence is now explicit

EMMA is a vision-language model co-trained as a generalist on planning, detection and road-graph tasks, with its driving outputs written as text <Cite id="emma-2024" />. It is a <Term id="vision-language-action-model">vision-language-action model</Term> whose embodiment is a car. A late-2025 survey splits driving VLAs into end-to-end models, which perceive, reason and plan in one network, and dual-system models, where a slow VLM deliberates over fast, safety-critical execution <Cite id="vla-ad-survey-2026" />.

Waymo's foundation model uses such a "Think Fast and Think Slow" design, a sensor-fusion encoder for rapid reactions beside a driving VLM trained using Gemini <Cite id="waymo-foundation-model-2025" />. The split mirrors the end-to-end versus [hierarchical](/manipulation/hierarchical/) divide in manipulation and the [knowledge insulation](/manipulation/knowledge-insulation/) case for a separate fast path. NVIDIA reports that its Alpamayo-R1 driving VLA runs on the vehicle in real time at 99 ms latency <Cite id="alpamayo-r1-2025" />.

Shiva Sreeram, Daniela Rus and colleagues at MIT CSAIL and the University of Haifa (October 2026) asked six open video-language models which way the ego car moves in driving clips <Cite id="mind-temporal-gap-2026" />. On 200 simulated forward and 200 backward clips, every model answered forward every time, and the same biases appeared on 60 real videos <Cite id="mind-temporal-gap-2026" />. After LoRA finetuning on 80 percent of those clips, all six scored 100 percent on the held-out 80, and the authors conclude that the motion cues are learnable but not reliably exposed through prompting <Cite id="mind-temporal-gap-2026" />.

The Waymo Open Dataset set the pattern of shared perception benchmarks <Cite id="waymo-open-dataset-2020" />. Open X-Embodiment pools over a million real robot trajectories across 22 embodiments from 34 labs <Cite id="open-x-embodiment-2023" />. Driving data is counted in hundreds of thousands of hours, such as the 500,000 in Waymo's scaling study <Cite id="waymo-scaling-laws-2025" />, a contrast that [the data bottleneck](/data-hardware/data-bottleneck/) examines.

### What differs in kind

A car steers and accelerates through two channels governed by tire friction and well-studied vehicle models. A manipulator moves dozens of joints that make and break contact. The <Term id="mpc">model-predictive control</Term> that tracks a car's trajectory <Cite id="paden-2016" /> has no equally clean purchase on a robot wiping a table, the argument of [why RL won locomotion](/rl-sim2real/why-rl-locomotion/).

Evaluation differs too. Waymo says replaying recorded data in open-loop simulation is insufficient <Cite id="waymo-ai-lessons-2026" />, and nuPlan moved planning evaluation from open-loop L2 metrics to closed-loop simulation <Cite id="nuplan-2021" />. Manipulation still reports short-horizon success on small trial counts, the subject of the [evaluation crisis](/data-hardware/evaluation-crisis/).

Driving simulation covers rigid-body motion and appearance with no contact-rich phase, and Waymo says its World Model helps it scale its service safely <Cite id="waymo-world-model-2026" />. Robot learning attempts the same with Genie-class models whose range of actions is still constrained <Cite id="genie-3-2025" />.

### What to watch

One open question is whether dual-system driving VLAs settle into the shape of hierarchical manipulation systems <Cite id="vla-ad-survey-2026" />. Another is whether generative simulators extend from appearance into contact. A third is whether robotics adopts AV's safety-case machinery, from formal models like RSS <Cite id="rss-2017" /> to credibility rules for virtual testing <Cite id="un-ads-regulation-2026" />, before robots deploy at scale. [Drones](/adjacent/drones/) covers flight, where a policy trained in simulation has already beaten human champions.

### The measurement problem

Kalra and Paddock's 2016 RAND study found test driving alone would need hundreds of millions of miles, sometimes hundreds of billions, to show safety <Cite id="kalra-paddock-2016" />. Mobileye's Responsibility-Sensitive Safety defines safe longitudinal and lateral distances as a white-box, interpretable model <Cite id="rss-2017" />. Its authors warned that without such standards the field risked a "winter of autonomous driving" <Cite id="rss-2017" />. Koopman argues "safe enough" also requires no risk hot spots, such as reckless driving or risk shifted onto vulnerable populations, plus standards conformance and accountability <Cite id="koopman-safe-enough-2026" />.

<AvSafetyMiles className="my-6" />

US companies must report crashes but not the miles they log, so crash rates are unknown for operators that do not volunteer mileage <Cite id="iihs-waymo-2026" />. NHTSA has streamlined its Standing General Order on crash reporting <Cite id="nhtsa-av-framework-2026" />. California's DMV says its disengagement reports are not designed for cross-company comparison, and deployment-permit operations need not report disengagements <Cite id="ca-dmv-av-miles-2026" />.

In September 2026, Chris Paxton argued that an automated system should be judged by its potential for catastrophic failure, much higher for a truck: it needs far longer to stop, and when one breaks down on a highway the law requires warning flares that an unoccupied truck cannot set out <Cite id="paxton-autonomous-trucks-2026" />. He expected driverless trucks to spread over the following year mainly in China and the US Sun Belt, and put highways where ice forms years away <Cite id="paxton-autonomous-trucks-2026" />.

### The deployment record

Waymo's peer-reviewed 2025 study covered 56.7 million rider-only miles through January 2025 <Cite id="waymo-crash-rates-2025" />. Against human benchmarks on the same roads, it found statistically significant lower rates of any-injury-reported, airbag-deployment and suspected-serious-injury crashes <Cite id="waymo-crash-rates-2025" />. Vehicle-to-vehicle intersection crashes with any injury fell 96 percent, without significant disbenefit in any of its 11 crash-type groups <Cite id="waymo-crash-rates-2025" />.

Waymo's safety hub reports 271.3 million rider-only miles through June 2026 <Cite id="waymo-safety-hub-2026" />. Across that distance it counts 95 percent fewer serious-injury-or-worse crashes and 82 percent fewer injury-causing crashes than human drivers <Cite id="waymo-safety-hub-2026" />. IIHS found Waymo's driverless vehicles in San Francisco, Phoenix, Los Angeles and Austin had 68 percent fewer police-reportable crashes per mile than human drivers <Cite id="iihs-waymo-2026" />.

Tesla says it launched unsupervised rides in Miami, Orlando and Tampa in July 2026 and expanded its unsupervised area in Austin <Cite id="tesla-q2-2026-update" />. Baidu reported in August 2026 that Apollo Go had reached 28 cities and more than 240 million fully driverless kilometres <Cite id="baidu-q2-2026" />. Aurora began driverless customer deliveries between Dallas and Houston in May 2025 after closing its safety case <Cite id="aurora-driverless-launch-2025" />. By its count it drove nearly 440,000 driverless miles through June 2026 with zero collisions attributed to its system, and expected 200 driverless trucks by year-end <Cite id="aurora-q2-2026" />.

On March 18, 2018, an Uber ATG test vehicle in Tempe, Arizona struck and killed a 49-year-old pedestrian crossing N. Mill Avenue at night, pushing a bicycle, where there was no crosswalk <Cite id="ntsb-uber-2019" />. The system judged a collision imminent 1.2 seconds before impact, and its design precluded emergency braking for crash mitigation alone, relying on the operator <Cite id="ntsb-uber-2019" />. The operator was streaming a television show, glancing down until about one second before the crash <Cite id="ntsb-uber-2019" />. Every layer failed at once, the correlated-safeguard problem the [reliability gap](/frontier/reliability-gap/) article examines.

On October 2, 2023, a driverless Cruise vehicle dragged a pedestrian about 20 feet before stopping. Under a September 2024 consent order, Cruise agreed to a \$1.5 million penalty for crash reports that omitted those details <Cite id="nhtsa-cruise-consent-2024" />. In December 2024 GM stopped funding Cruise's robotaxi work, citing scaling time and resource needs <Cite id="gm-cruise-refocus-2024" />.

## The relation to robot learning

The imitation toolkit began with driving before reaching arms. DAgger, the canonical fix for covariate shift, was demonstrated steering a car in a 3D racing game <Cite id="dagger-2011" />. It cuts the growth of mistakes over the horizon from quadratic to linear <Cite id="dagger-2011" />. On 500,000 hours of driving, Waymo found forecasting and planning improve as a power law in compute, and closed-loop metrics improve too <Cite id="waymo-scaling-laws-2025" />.

RAD trains end-to-end policies by reinforcement learning in photorealistic 3D Gaussian splatting replicas, to address imitation's causal confusion and open-loop gap <Cite id="rad-2025" />. It reports a 3x lower collision rate <Cite id="rad-2025" />.

EMMA is a vision-language model co-trained as a generalist on planning, detection and road-graph tasks, with driving outputs written as text <Cite id="emma-2024" />. It is a <Term id="vision-language-action-model">vision-language-action model</Term> whose embodiment is a car. A late-2025 survey splits driving VLAs into end-to-end models, perceiving, reasoning and planning in one network, and dual-system models, where a slow VLM deliberates over fast, safety-critical execution <Cite id="vla-ad-survey-2026" />.

Waymo's foundation model uses such a "Think Fast and Think Slow" design, a sensor-fusion encoder for rapid reactions beside a driving VLM trained using Gemini <Cite id="waymo-foundation-model-2025" />. The split mirrors the end-to-end versus [hierarchical](/manipulation/hierarchical/) divide in manipulation and the [knowledge insulation](/manipulation/knowledge-insulation/) case for a separate fast path. NVIDIA reports its Alpamayo-R1 driving VLA runs onboard in real time at 99 ms latency <Cite id="alpamayo-r1-2025" />.

Open X-Embodiment pools over a million real robot trajectories across 22 embodiments from 34 labs <Cite id="open-x-embodiment-2023" />. A car steers and accelerates through two channels governed by tire friction and well-studied vehicle models. A manipulator moves dozens of joints making and breaking contact. The <Term id="mpc">model-predictive control</Term> that tracks a car's trajectory <Cite id="paden-2016" /> has no equally clean purchase on a robot wiping a table, the argument of [why RL won locomotion](/rl-sim2real/why-rl-locomotion/).

Robot learning attempts the same with Genie-class models whose action range remains constrained <Cite id="genie-3-2025" />.

It remains open whether dual-system driving VLAs settle into the shape of hierarchical manipulation systems <Cite id="vla-ad-survey-2026" />. import { ComparisonMatrix } from '@/components/interactive/comparison-matrix';

The comparison matrix is a table of major robot policies, from RT-1 (2022) to π0.7 (2026), compared on eight architectural axes: action representation, horizon, control frequency, backbone, conditioning, cross-embodiment, hierarchy and weights <Cite id="rt1-2022" /> <Cite id="pi07-2026" />. Each cell records what its named source discloses.

<Image id="octo-evaluation-setups-2024" />

Set the weights filter to Downloadable to compare the available checkpoints <Cite id="openpi-repo-2024" />.

<ComparisonMatrix className="my-6 wide-measure" />

## Use the matrix as a constraint solver

Remove models whose weights or training data the project cannot use (Gemini Robotics On-Device, for example, is reached through a trusted-tester SDK <Cite id="gemini-robotics-on-device-2025" />), then models whose action representation, latency, observations or adaptation-data needs do not fit the robot, and only then compare benchmark performance.

<Image id="roboarena-evaluation-2025" />

Compare the survivors under one trial protocol with the same cameras, action horizon and resets, and keep a behavior-cloning or action-chunking baseline. TRI's Large Behavior Model study used blind, randomized trials <Cite id="tri-lbm-2025" />, and RoboArena ranked seven generalist policies more accurately than centralized evaluation through over 600 double-blind pairwise real-robot episodes <Cite id="roboarena-2025" />. The [foundation-model guide](/manipulation/foundation-models/) explains what prior each family contributes, the [action-space guide](/manipulation/action-spaces/) whether its output fits, and the [evaluation crisis](/data-hardware/evaluation-crisis/) why protocols resist a shared leaderboard.

## The eight axes

Action representation is the output mechanism: continuous regression, discrete action tokens, or a generative head such as diffusion or <Term id="flow-matching">flow matching</Term>. Supervision and runtime generation can differ: π0.5 trains with FAST tokens but generates continuous actions with flow matching <Cite id="pi05-2025" />.

Horizon separates the planned chunk length $H$, the <Term id="predicted-horizon">predicted horizon</Term>, from the steps executed before re-planning, the <Term id="committed-horizon">committed horizon</Term>. Diffusion Policy's simulated CNN Push-T reference uses observation, prediction and execution horizons of 2, 16 and 8 <Cite id="diffusion-policy-2023" />; ACT's 100-step entry is its k=100 chunk-ablation reference <Cite id="act-aloha-2023" />; OFT+ predicts and executes 25 actions at 25 Hz on ALOHA <Cite id="openvla-oft-2025" />; and π0.7 predicts 50 with five denoising steps and executes 15 or 25 <Cite id="pi07-2026" />. [Real-time chunking](/manipulation/realtime-execution/) generates the next chunk while the current one executes <Cite id="real-time-chunking-2025" />.

Control frequency needs a named measurement setting. ACT's ALOHA setup runs at 50 Hz with <Term id="temporal-ensembling">temporal ensembling</Term> <Cite id="act-aloha-2023" />, RT-1 commands the Everyday Robots platform at 3 Hz <Cite id="rt1-2022" />, and RT-2's multi-TPU cloud service runs PaLI-X-55B at 1 to 3 Hz <Cite id="rt2-2023" />. OpenVLA reaches about 6 Hz on one RTX 4090, and its Franka fine-tuning setups use 5 Hz and 15 Hz controllers <Cite id="openvla-2024" />.

Gemini Robotics turns about 250 ms of end-to-end latency into a 50 Hz effective control frequency with multi-action chunks <Cite id="gemini-robotics-2025" />, GR00T N1 samples a 16-action chunk in 63.9 ms on an L40 <Cite id="gr00t-n1-2025" />, the π0.6 card reports 63 ms per chunk on one H100 <Cite id="pi06-model-card-2025" />, and Generalist says GEN-1.5 produces 100 Hz action trajectories <Cite id="gen-1-5-2026" />.

<ChunkBuffer className="my-6" />

Backbone, conditioning and cross-embodiment describe model components, inputs and the scope of robot-body transfer. Mixed-embodiment training, one checkpoint on several bodies and fine-tuning on a new body are different evidence; CrossFormer shows the strongest kind, with the same weights controlling very different robots after training on 900K trajectories from 20 embodiments <Cite id="crossformer-2024" />. Skild says S1 executes a task shown in one video <Cite id="skild-s1-2026" />, which adds demonstration video as a conditioning input.

Hierarchy distinguishes an internal high-level stage from a separately paired system. π0.5 predicts a semantic subtask before low-level actions <Cite id="pi05-2025" />, while in the N1.7 SONIC workflow a separate whole-body controller decodes the VLA's latent action tokens into joint commands <Cite id="isaac-gr00t-repo-2026" />. A separate high-level VLM gives π0 subtasks <Cite id="pi0-2024" />.

Weights records download availability, separately from license. openpi lists π0, π0-FAST and π0.5 checkpoints <Cite id="openpi-repo-2024" />; the N1.7 README separates Apache 2.0 code from weights under the NVIDIA Open Model License <Cite id="isaac-gr00t-repo-2026" />; and SmolVLA releases code, pretrained models and training data <Cite id="smolvla-2025" />.

## Row notes

RT-1's "limited" cross-embodiment label means Kuka IIWA data mixed with Everyday Robots data and evaluated on Everyday Robots <Cite id="rt1-2022" />. ACT trains a roughly 80M-parameter model from scratch for each task <Cite id="act-aloha-2023" />, and RT-2's action-only entry excludes its chain-of-thought variant <Cite id="rt2-2023" />.

<Image id="gemini-robotics-apollo-franka-2025" />

OpenVLA's 7B label names the language model, beside a 600M visual encoder <Cite id="openvla-2024" />. OFT's "limited" label means adapting the pretrained model to separate tasks and robot setups <Cite id="openvla-oft-2025" />, and GR00T N1.6 predicts state-relative action chunks for most embodiments <Cite id="gr00t-n1-6-2025" />. π*0.6 adds Recap post-training, which more than doubles throughput on some of the hardest tasks <Cite id="pistar06-2025" />.

Gemini Robotics 1.5's model card discloses continuous numerical action outputs but no action-head family, chunk length, command rate or parameter count; one checkpoint runs across ALOHA, bi-arm Franka and Apollo, and a separate GR-ER 1.5 orchestrator can pair with it <Cite id="gemini-robotics-15-2025" />. DeepMind's July 30, 2026 Gemini Robotics 2 announcement covers Apollo 2 and Franka Duo with one checkpoint but gives no backbone, output parameterization, chunk length, control frequency or parameter count <Cite id="gemini-robotics-2-2026" />. Skild's row rests on its January 14, 2026 Series C announcement, with no reproducible cross-embodiment evaluation or runtime details <Cite id="skild-series-c-2026" />.

## What the matrix can establish

ACT fixes its CVAE latent to the prior mean, zero, to decode deterministically <Cite id="act-aloha-2023" />, while π0 generates continuous action chunks with a flow-matching action expert <Cite id="pi0-2024" />. Generalist says GEN-1's base model trains on wearable human data without robot data and reaches 99% average success where earlier models reached 64%, with 1 hour of robot data per task <Cite id="generalist-gen1-2026" />. On March 16, 2026, NVIDIA previewed GR00T N2, based on DreamZero research <Cite id="nvidia-gtc-gr00t-n2-2026" />.

## Helix 02 and GO-2 disclosure limits

Figure's Helix 02 announcement gives S1 joint targets at 200 Hz and S0 actuator commands at 1 kHz, but no output-head training loss, chunk horizon or weight-release terms <Cite id="helix-02-2026" />. The first Helix post disclosed a 7 to 9 Hz onboard VLM and an 80M-parameter S1 at 200 Hz, trained end-to-end with a standard regression loss <Cite id="helix-2025" />, and Figure reports that Index human-video pretraining raised Helix 2.5's zero-shot success in 30 unseen homes from 9% to 56% <Cite id="helix-2-5-2026" />. AgiBot describes lower-frequency System 2 planning and higher-frequency System 1 action following, with no numerical rate, backbone, output encoding, chunk length or weight terms <Cite id="agibot-go2-2026" />; its predecessor GO-1 uses latent action representations trained on AgiBot World's more than 1 million trajectories across 217 tasks <Cite id="agibot-world-2025" />.

Compare major robot policies, RT-1 (2022) through π0.7 (2026), on eight architectural axes: action representation, horizon, control frequency, backbone, conditioning, cross-embodiment, hierarchy and weights <Cite id="rt1-2022" /> <Cite id="pi07-2026" />. Cells record named sources' disclosures.

<Image id="octo-evaluation-setups-2024" />

Filter weights to Downloadable to compare available checkpoints <Cite id="openpi-repo-2024" />.

<ComparisonMatrix className="my-6 wide-measure" />

## Use the matrix as a constraint solver

Remove models whose weights or training data the project cannot use (Gemini Robotics On-Device offers trusted-tester SDK access <Cite id="gemini-robotics-on-device-2025" />), then models whose action representation, latency, observations or adaptation-data needs mismatch the robot, before comparing benchmark performance.

<Image id="roboarena-evaluation-2025" />

Compare survivors with one protocol, identical cameras, action horizon and resets; keep a behavior-cloning or action-chunking baseline. TRI's Large Behavior Model study used blind, randomized trials <Cite id="tri-lbm-2025" />; RoboArena ranked seven generalist policies more accurately than centralized evaluation through over 600 double-blind pairwise real-robot episodes <Cite id="roboarena-2025" />. The [foundation-model guide](/manipulation/foundation-models/) explains family priors, the [action-space guide](/manipulation/action-spaces/) output compatibility, and the [evaluation crisis](/data-hardware/evaluation-crisis/) why protocols resist shared leaderboards.

## The eight axes

Action representation: continuous regression, discrete action tokens or generative heads, including diffusion or <Term id="flow-matching">flow matching</Term>. Supervision and runtime generation can differ: π0.5 trains with FAST tokens but generates continuous actions with flow matching <Cite id="pi05-2025" />.

Distinguish planned chunk length $H$, the <Term id="predicted-horizon">predicted horizon</Term>, from steps executed before re-planning, the <Term id="committed-horizon">committed horizon</Term>. Diffusion Policy's simulated CNN Push-T reference uses observation, prediction and execution horizons of 2, 16 and 8 <Cite id="diffusion-policy-2023" />; ACT's 100-step entry is its k=100 chunk-ablation reference <Cite id="act-aloha-2023" />; OFT+ predicts and executes 25 actions at 25 Hz on ALOHA <Cite id="openvla-oft-2025" />; π0.7 predicts 50 with five denoising steps, executing 15 or 25 <Cite id="pi07-2026" />. [Real-time chunking](/manipulation/realtime-execution/) generates the next chunk while the current one executes <Cite id="real-time-chunking-2025" />.

Control frequency: specify conditions. ACT's ALOHA runs at 50 Hz with <Term id="temporal-ensembling">temporal ensembling</Term> <Cite id="act-aloha-2023" />, RT-1 commands Everyday Robots' platform at 3 Hz <Cite id="rt1-2022" />, and RT-2's multi-TPU cloud service runs PaLI-X-55B at 1 to 3 Hz <Cite id="rt2-2023" />. OpenVLA reaches about 6 Hz on one RTX 4090; its Franka fine-tuning setups use 5 Hz and 15 Hz controllers <Cite id="openvla-2024" />.

Gemini Robotics turns about 250 ms end-to-end latency into effective 50 Hz control frequency with multi-action chunks <Cite id="gemini-robotics-2025" />, GR00T N1's 16-action chunk sampling takes 63.9 ms on an L40 <Cite id="gr00t-n1-2025" />, π0.6's card: 63 ms per chunk on one H100 <Cite id="pi06-model-card-2025" />; Generalist says GEN-1.5 produces 100 Hz action trajectories <Cite id="gen-1-5-2026" />.

<ChunkBuffer className="my-6" />

Backbone, conditioning and cross-embodiment: components, inputs and robot-body transfer scope. Mixed-embodiment training, one checkpoint across bodies and new-body fine-tuning are different evidence; CrossFormer gives the strongest evidence: identical weights control very different robots after 900K training trajectories from 20 embodiments <Cite id="crossformer-2024" />. Skild says S1 executes a task shown in one video <Cite id="skild-s1-2026" />: demonstration video conditioning.

Hierarchy: internal high-level stages versus separate systems. π0.5 predicts a semantic subtask before low-level actions <Cite id="pi05-2025" />; the N1.7 SONIC workflow's separate whole-body controller decodes VLA latent action tokens into joint commands <Cite id="isaac-gr00t-repo-2026" />. A separate high-level VLM gives π0 subtasks <Cite id="pi0-2024" />.

Weights separates download availability from license. openpi lists π0, π0-FAST and π0.5 checkpoints <Cite id="openpi-repo-2024" />; N1.7's README separates Apache 2.0 code and NVIDIA Open Model License weights <Cite id="isaac-gr00t-repo-2026" />; SmolVLA releases code, pretrained models and training data <Cite id="smolvla-2025" />.

## Row notes

RT-1's "limited" cross-embodiment training mixes Kuka IIWA and Everyday Robots data; evaluation uses Everyday Robots <Cite id="rt1-2022" />. ACT trains task-specific roughly 80M-parameter models from scratch <Cite id="act-aloha-2023" />; RT-2's action-only entry excludes its chain-of-thought variant <Cite id="rt2-2023" />.

<Image id="gemini-robotics-apollo-franka-2025" />

OpenVLA's 7B denotes its language model, beside a 600M visual encoder <Cite id="openvla-2024" />. OFT's "limited" means pretrained-model adaptation to separate tasks and robot setups <Cite id="openvla-oft-2025" />; GR00T N1.6 predicts state-relative action chunks for most embodiments <Cite id="gr00t-n1-6-2025" />. π*0.6's Recap post-training more than doubles throughput on some of the hardest tasks <Cite id="pistar06-2025" />.

Gemini Robotics 1.5's card discloses continuous numerical actions, omitting action-head family, chunk length, command rate or parameter count; one checkpoint spans ALOHA, bi-arm Franka and Apollo; separate GR-ER 1.5 orchestrators are optional <Cite id="gemini-robotics-15-2025" />. DeepMind's July 30, 2026 Gemini Robotics 2 announcement covers Apollo 2 and Franka Duo with one checkpoint but omits backbone, output parameterization, chunk length, control frequency or parameter count <Cite id="gemini-robotics-2-2026" />. Skild's row: its January 14, 2026 Series C announcement, without reproducible cross-embodiment evaluation or runtime details <Cite id="skild-series-c-2026" />.

## What the matrix can establish

ACT fixes CVAE latents to the prior mean, zero, to decode deterministically <Cite id="act-aloha-2023" />; π0's flow-matching expert generates continuous action chunks <Cite id="pi0-2024" />. Generalist says GEN-1's base trains on wearable human data without robot data and averages 99% success versus earlier models' 64%, with 1 hour of robot data per task <Cite id="generalist-gen1-2026" />. On March 16, 2026, NVIDIA previewed GR00T N2, based on DreamZero <Cite id="nvidia-gtc-gr00t-n2-2026" />.

## Helix 02 and GO-2 disclosure limits

Figure announced Helix 02's S1 joint targets at 200 Hz and S0 actuator commands at 1 kHz, but no output-head training loss, chunk horizon or weight-release terms <Cite id="helix-02-2026" />. Helix's first post disclosed a 7 to 9 Hz onboard VLM and 80M-parameter S1 at 200 Hz, trained end-to-end with standard regression loss <Cite id="helix-2025" />; Figure reports Index human-video pretraining raised Helix 2.5's zero-shot success in 30 unseen homes from 9% to 56% <Cite id="helix-2-5-2026" />. AgiBot describes lower-frequency System 2 planning and higher-frequency System 1 action following, without numerical rate, backbone, output encoding, chunk length or weight terms <Cite id="agibot-go2-2026" />; predecessor GO-1 uses latent action representations trained on AgiBot World's over 1 million trajectories across 217 tasks <Cite id="agibot-world-2025" />.

preserved: ## Agents trained inside a recurrent latent model reached human-level Atari

edits.before:
Ha and Schmidhuber trained an agent "entirely inside of its own hallucinated dream" and transferred it back to the real environment <Cite id="ha-world-models-2018" />. PlaNet planned from pixels with deterministic and stochastic latent transitions <Cite id="planet-2018" />. DreamerV3's Recurrent State-Space Model (RSSM) pairs a recurrent state that carries memory with a stochastic categorical representation, and learns to reconstruct inputs and predict reward and continuation <Cite id="dreamerv3-2023" />.

Dreamer's actor and critic are trained purely on imagined latent rollouts from real encoded states, backpropagating value gradients through the model <Cite id="dreamer-2019" />. DreamerV2, which added discrete latents, was the first agent to reach human-level performance on the 55-task Atari benchmark by learning inside a separately trained world model <Cite id="dreamerv2-2020" />.

IRIS learns inside a discrete-autoencoder and autoregressive-transformer world model, evaluated on the Atari 100k benchmark <Cite id="iris-world-model-2022" />. TransDreamer replaces recurrent dynamics with a Transformer State-Space Model shared with a transformer policy, targeting visual tasks that need long-range memory <Cite id="transdreamer-2022" />.

DreamerV3 was evaluated on more than 150 tasks across eight domains with fixed hyperparameters. It uses symlog transforms for vector observations, free bits with KL balancing and percentile-based return normalization <Cite id="dreamerv3-2023" />. In the 2025 Nature article its authors call it, to their knowledge, the first algorithm to collect diamonds in Minecraft from scratch without human data or adaptive curricula <Cite id="dreamerv3-nature-2025" />. Its MineRL-based task used abstract crafting actions, accelerated block breaking and sparse intermediate rewards for 12 milestones from log to diamond <Cite id="dreamerv3-2023" />.

DreamerV3 learned online; in 2025 Dreamer 4 became "the first agent to obtain diamonds in Minecraft purely from offline data", with a world model that runs in real time on a single GPU <Cite id="dreamer4-2025" />.

edits.before:
Dream-MPC refines policy-proposed action sequences by gradient ascent on predicted return, with an uncertainty penalty. Used in place of MPPI in pretrained TD-MPC2 and BMPC on 24 simulated tasks, over three seeds and ten episodes, the BMPC variant raises interquartile mean by 26.7% and mean by 20.5%. The TD-MPC2 variant beats its policy alone but does not consistently match MPPI <Cite id="dream-mpc-2026" />. BMPC learns its policy by imitating the MPC planner <Cite id="bmpc-2025" />, and HumanoidBench, one of the three task suites, poses whole-body humanoid tasks <Cite id="humanoidbench-2024" />.

TD-M(PC)² found that planner-generated data causes "persistent value overestimation" and fixed it with a policy constraint, gaining most on 61-DoF humanoids <Cite id="td-m-pc2-2025" />. Fast-WAM, a video world-action model, keeps video co-training but encodes the current frame once and runs action denoising on a chunk, with success similar to its imagine-then-execute variants on LIBERO and RoboTwin 2.0. On Galaxea R1 Lite towel folding it reports 190 ms inference latency against 810 ms for Fast-WAM-IDM on one RTX 5090D V2 32GB GPU <Cite id="fast-wam-2026" />.

## TD-MPC2's authors expect broad generalization to need far more tasks

TD-MPC2's authors expect broad generalization, such as transfer to new embodiments, "will likely require several orders of magnitude more tasks" <Cite id="tdmpc2-2023" />. In November 2025 the same group's Newt trained one language-conditioned world model jointly across 200 tasks <Cite id="newt-2025" />. In simulation, one world model trained on up to 90 insertion tasks reached 56% zero-shot success on unseen parts, against 7% for a model-free baseline <Cite id="insertion-world-models-2026" />. DayDreamer's authors report that long hardware training causes wear needing human intervention or repair <Cite id="daydreamer-2022" />.

<span id="pick-the-models-role-before-its-architecture" />
## Imagination tolerates slow models; online planning needs predictable latency

<Term id="cycle-time">Cycle time</Term> is the time required to produce a part or complete a process, measured for that operation <Cite id="lei-cycle-time-definition" />. <Term id="takt-time">Takt time</Term> is available production time divided by customer demand, and its purpose is to match production with demand <Cite id="lei-takt-time-definition" />. NASA distinguishes inherent availability, computed from <Term id="mean-time-between-failures">mean time between failures</Term> and mean time to repair without administrative, logistics or preventive-maintenance time, from operational availability, which includes them. Uptime is time in an operable state <Cite id="nasa-availability-prediction-analysis" />.

The calculator above reports capital cost per modeled pick: robot price times the integration multiple, divided by modeled lifetime picks over a fixed amortization period. It does not include running costs. The <Term id="payback-period">payback period</Term> is total system capital cost divided by monthly labour, reduced-damage and throughput value. EVST's guide estimates 12 to 24 months for multi-shift palletising cells and 24 to 36 months for single-shift or lower-throughput operations <Cite id="evst-cell-cost-2026" />.

## The jam rate is the lesson

A separate authored example has no measured intervention rate behind it. At 99 percent per-pick success, with every failure needing a ten-second clearing, overhead is (1 − 0.99) × 10 = 0.1 seconds per attempted pick. Amazon's stow system is designed to stow 80 percent of warehouse items at 300 units per hour. A no-stow turnaway, when a pod leaves with nothing stowed, consumes at least 12 seconds <Cite id="amazon-stow-2025" />.

The <Term id="intervention-rate">intervention rate</Term> and clearing cost together decide whether a cell ships. Physical Intelligence reports that training on deployment data, including expert corrections during autonomous runs, more than doubled throughput and roughly halved the failure rate on some of its hardest tasks <Cite id="pistar06-2025" />. Ken Goldberg proposes combining model-based engineering with model-free learning so robots can perform useful work, collect real-world data, and use those data to improve performance and learn adjacent skills. Goldberg does not claim that engineering removes the need for learning, and he expects model-free AI eventually to enable fully general-purpose robots <Cite id="goldberg-data-gap-2025" />.

[The Reliability Gap](/frontier/reliability-gap) tracks the demo-to-production gap and selected deployment examples; [Autonomous Vehicles](/adjacent/autonomous-vehicles) covers the same question for driverless cars. Morgan Stanley's 2026 note on the humanoid industry's "PR problem", as reported by CNBC, describes [investors](/market-map) looking for real-world return on investment over polished demonstrations <Cite id="morgan-stanley-pr-problem-2026" />. Figure says its livestreamed logistics run lasted 200 hours <Cite id="helix-2-5-2026" />, but it was one task at one site, with [no published success rate](/data-hardware/evaluation-crisis).

## The labour evidence, disagreement intact

Daron Acemoglu and Pascual Restrepo find that one more robot per thousand workers cuts the US employment-to-population ratio by about 0.2 percentage points and wages by 0.42 percent. Losses concentrate in commuting zones exposed to industrial automation <Cite id="acemoglu-restrepo-2020" />.

In Germany, robot-driven displacement in manufacturing was fully offset by new jobs in services, and the cost fell mostly on young workers entering the labour force <Cite id="dauth-robots-germany-2021" />. Spanish manufacturers that adopted robots raised output by 20 to 25 percent within four years and created net jobs at a rate of 10 percent <Cite id="koch-robots-firms-2021" />. French adopters also grew employment, at their competitors' expense, and the overall effect on industry employment was negative <Cite id="acemoglu-lelarge-restrepo-2020" />.

edits.before: The theses can coexist: π0.7 is an end-to-end vision-language-action model that also reasons hierarchically, takes optional subgoal-image prompts from a separate world model initialized from BAGEL, which the paper describes as lightweight, and distills experience from RL-trained π*0.6 specialists . ## Scaling has early laws, such as EgoScale's log-linear fit to validation loss The claim: keep the architecture general, scale data and parameters, and generalist robot intelligence follows, as it did for language. Rich Sutton's 2019 essay The Bitter Lesson frames it: general methods that leverage computation win in the long run . Brooks answered six days later, in a reply that paraphrases Sutton and describes itself, including its closing comment, as "seventy six words shorter than Sutton's post" . Bessemer's investor analysis argues that "scaling laws are emerging" and that capital is the moat ([VLA models](/manipulation/vla-models/)). EgoScale fit a log-linear scaling law (R² = 0.9983) from human-video pretraining hours to validation loss, which it reports correlates strongly with downstream robot performance . Its full recipe lifts average success by 54% over a no-pretraining baseline on a 22-DoF hand . Figure reports a human-to-humanoid transfer law on robot-action prediction, with Index pretraining lifting zero-shot success in 30 unseen homes from 9% to 56% . ## Motion Transfer across robot embodiments

Gemini Robotics 1.5 trains on ALOHA, bi-arm Franka and Apptronik Apollo data plus Internet text, images and video, with Motion Transfer, an architecture and training recipe that aligns embodiments. On tasks demonstrated only on another robot it helps, less so for Apollo, in ablations run interleaved on one work cell; one checkpoint drives all three robots, though the long-horizon agent adds bi-arm Franka post-training, and the report specifies an orchestrator over the <Term id="vision-language-action-model">VLA</Term> but not the alignment representation <Cite id="gemini-robotics-15-2025" />. DeepMind says tasks shown only to ALOHA 2 "just work" on Apollo and bi-arm Franka, and vice versa <Cite id="gemini-robotics-15-blog-2025" />.

DeepMind says On-Device 2, natively multi-embodiment with Motion Transfer, adapts to new bi-arm robots in a few hours, typically from fewer than 200 examples <Cite id="gemini-robotics-2-2026" />.

## Relative end-effector actions for robots and humans

GR00T N1 embedded state and action with embodiment-aware encoders <Cite id="gr00t-n1-2025" />; N1.6 moved most embodiments to state-relative action chunks, which NVIDIA found smoother and more accurate than absolute actions <Cite id="gr00t-n1-6-2025" />. N1.7 shares relative end-effector deltas between human and robot embodiments and calls this a key factor in cross-embodiment performance <Cite id="isaac-gr00t-repo-2026" />.

<HandMotionShare className="my-6" />

<Image id="egoscale-human-to-robot-2026" />

EgoScale uses relative wrist motion and <Term id="retargeting">retargets</Term> 21 human hand keypoints to the 22-DoF Sharpa hand, with embodiment-conditioned adapters for <Term id="proprioception">proprioception</Term> and hand actions around a shared backbone and action expert <Cite id="egoscale-2026" />. Morphometric Imitation (September 2026) retargets reconstructed hand-object interactions across [hand morphologies](/frontier/dexterity/), then refines them with residual RL; on a Sharpa hand its policies reached 89.3% zero-shot success in 300 real trials on 30 objects <Cite id="morphometric-imitation-2026" />.

## Closing the visual embodiment gap

Mirage masks out an unseen target robot and inpaints the source robot in real time <Cite id="mirage-2024" />. RoVi-Aug synthesizes training images with other robots and viewpoints and deploys zero-shot on an unseen robot, and co-training with it raises success by up to 30% <Cite id="rovi-aug-2024" />. Shadow replaces the robot image with a composite source-and-target segmentation mask during both training and evaluation <Cite id="shadow-2025" />.

## Latent actions as a shared interface

LAPA learns discrete latent actions between video frames, pretrains a VLA on them and fine-tunes on robot data; training only on human video still transfers positively <Cite id="lapa-2025" />. Latent Action Diffusion contrastively aligns actions from human hands, robotic hands and parallel-jaw grippers before policy co-training <Cite id="latent-action-diffusion-2025" />. LAC-WM (Stanford and Meta FAIR, October 2026) conditions a robot world model on a latent action space shared across embodiments; picking action chunks for a VLA on five unseen LIBERO tasks, it raised average success from 82.4% with an explicit-action world model to 92.0% <Cite id="lac-wm-2026" />.

## Human-to-robot transfer recipes

Simar Kareer's EgoMimic treated human and robot data equally and found an extra hour of hand data worth more than one of robot data <Cite id="egomimic-2024" />. TWIST combines reinforcement learning and behavior cloning to track human motion retargeted onto a humanoid <Cite id="twist-2025" />. On December 16, 2025, Kareer and Physical Intelligence colleagues co-fine-tuned π0.5 on human data, with 3D hand positions as actions, and the most relevant robot data. PI reports about 2× performance on four scenarios present only in human data, without trial counts, and transfer that improves as robot pretraining diversifies <Cite id="pi-human-to-robot-2025" />.

<Image id="phantom-human-video-robot-2025" />

EgoScale's Ruijie Zheng and coauthors instead pretrain on human video, mid-train on aligned human-robot data and post-train on task robot data, and find adding aligned mid-training best overall <Cite id="egoscale-2026" />. H-RDT pretrains on egocentric human video with hand poses, then adapts to robot data through modular action encoders and decoders <Cite id="h-rdt-2025" />. EgoBridge aligns human and robot policy latents with optimal transport and reports a 44% absolute success gain over human-augmented cross-embodiment baselines <Cite id="egobridge-2025" />. EgoLAP (Princeton, Toyota Research Institute and Physical Intelligence, October 2026) routes human and robot trajectories through a shared chain of language actions and reached 80.1% mean real-world task progress on bimanual YAM robots, 2.3 times the alternative action representations <Cite id="egolap-2026" />.

Phantom needs no robot data: it inpaints the human arm, overlays a rendered robot and deploys zero-shot, with success up to 92% <Cite id="phantom-2025" />. Masquerade robotizes in-the-wild human video and fine-tunes on 50 [robot demonstrations](/data-hardware/teleop-rigs/) per task, beating baselines by 5 to 6 times <Cite id="masquerade-2026" />. Figure reports that Index human-video pretraining, all else fixed, raised Helix 2.5's zero-shot success in 30 unseen homes from 9% to 56% <Cite id="helix-2-5-2026" />, and Generalist's GEN-1 base model pretrains on over half a million hours from wearable devices on humans, with no robot data <Cite id="generalist-gen1-2026" />.

## Scaling the number of embodiments

Across about 1,000 procedurally generated locomotion bodies, adding embodiments generalizes more broadly than adding data on fixed ones <Cite id="embodiment-scaling-2025" />. Skild reports training one model on 100,000 simulated robots and testing zero-shot on robots excluded from training <Cite id="skild-omni-bodied-2025" />. DreamZero adapted from AgiBot G1 to a YAM bimanual robot with 55 trajectories, about 30 minutes of play data, though its authors describe the result only qualitatively <Cite id="dreamzero-2026" />. GOTT shares a closed-loop contact-acquisition primitive across hand morphologies, followed by object-pose tracking <Cite id="gott-2026" />.

## Why chunking works

<Term id="behavior-cloning">Behavior cloning</Term> with per-step error ε on the expert's states can accumulate cost quadratic in episode length T, because each mistake carries the robot into states the expert never visited <Cite id="dagger-2011" />. <Term id="dagger">DAgger</Term> relabels the states the policy visits; its excess cost is linear in T only if u, the rise in expert cost-to-go after one action, does not grow with T <Cite id="dagger-2011" />:

$$
\underset{\text{behavior cloning}}{O(\varepsilon T^2)} \qquad \underset{\text{DAgger}}{O(u\,\varepsilon T)}
$$

<Term id="action-chunking">Action chunking</Term> shortens the horizon instead: k actions per inference cut it k-fold <Cite id="act-aloha-2023" />. With continuous actions, smooth deterministic imitators can suffer execution error exponentially larger in the horizon than their training error, part of why chunking and diffusion policies work <Cite id="simchowitz-continuous-il-2025" />, and chunking avoids that compounding through control-theoretic stability <Cite id="zhang-chunking-exploration-2025" />.

## ACT: chunking with a CVAE

Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT), introduced with the ALOHA bimanual [teleoperation hardware](/data-hardware/teleop-rigs/), wraps chunking in a <Term id="cvae">conditional variational autoencoder</Term>: training encodes each demonstrated action sequence as a latent style variable, and at test time the policy decodes a chunk from camera images and joint positions with that latent at zero. Dropping the CVAE objective barely changes scripted-data results and cuts human-data success from 35.3% to 2% <Cite id="act-aloha-2023" />.

<Image id="aloha-2-workcell-2024" />

### The chunk-size dial

In ACT's ablation, averaged over two simulated tasks with temporal ensembling off, success rises from 1% at k=1 to 44% at k=100 and dips at k=200 and k=400, near open-loop control; chunked BC-ConvMLP and VINN follow the same trend <Cite id="act-aloha-2023" />. A small k brings back <Term id="compounding-error">compounding error</Term>, and a large one reacts slowly to unexpected states <Cite id="bidirectional-decoding-2024" />. The best execution horizon is task-dependent: in flow-based VLAs success rises and then falls as it lengthens <Cite id="autohorizon-2026" />, and PACE, which picks it online, lifted real ALOHA and Franka success from 50.7% to 70.4% <Cite id="pace-2026" />. Mixture of Horizons processes several chunk lengths with one shared transformer and combines them through a learned gate <Cite id="moh-2025" />.

## Temporal ensembling and its limits

The pinned ACT reference implementation uses <Term id="temporal-ensembling">temporal ensembling</Term>: it queries the policy every timestep and averages, oldest to newest, the retained predictions for the current action. Weights are $w_i = \exp(-m \cdot i)$, where $i = 0$ is the earliest prediction and $m = 0.01$, so the oldest prediction weighs most <Cite id="act-reference-2023" />. The best decay rate varies by task <Cite id="bidirectional-decoding-2024" />.

For oldest-to-newest predictions `[0, 10, 20]` after selection, $m = 0.01$ gives normalized weights of about `[0.33667217, 0.33332222, 0.33000561]` and an average of `9.93333444`; the reference occupancy filter would discard a literal zero <Cite id="act-reference-2023" />.

In the table, `not disclosed` means the source omits the value, and weights means download availability. Physical Intelligence's openpi README lists base checkpoints for π0, π0-FAST and π0.5 <Cite id="openpi-repo-2024" />.

Octo's ALOHA fine-tuning example predicts 64 actions and executes 12 before replanning <Cite id="octo-2024" />, and RT-1 predicts one action per timestep; its paper announces open code <Cite id="rt1-2022" />. [π0](/manipulation/pi-line/) generates its chunks with conditional <Term id="flow-matching">flow matching</Term> <Cite id="pi0-2024" />, and π0.5 combines FAST tokens with flow matching <Cite id="pi05-2025" />, though openpi supports only its flow-matching head <Cite id="openpi-repo-2024" />.

The π0.6 model card, dated November 17, 2025, reports 63 ms per action chunk with five denoising steps and three cameras on one H100 <Cite id="pi06-model-card-2025" />. π0.7 predicts 50-step chunks and executes 15 or 25, at 20 Hz on UR5e and 50 Hz elsewhere; it distills experience from RL-trained π*0.6 <Cite id="pi07-2026" />. NVIDIA's GR00T N1.7 README lists a predicted horizon of 40 and downloadable weights, under Apache 2.0 in its overview and the NVIDIA Open Model License in its License section <Cite id="isaac-gr00t-repo-2026" />; GR00T N1 processed actions "in chunks as in Zhao et al. ## The autonomy stack on a flying robot

One camera and one low-cost IMU are the minimum sensor suite for metric six-DoF state estimation <Cite id="vins-mono-2018" />. <Term id="visual-inertial-odometry">Visual-inertial odometry</Term> fuses image features with IMU measurements into the pose and velocity the controller needs, without GPS or motion capture <Cite id="swift-drone-racing-2023" />. The fast inner loop often runs on a microcontroller stack such as PX4, which has substantially lower latency than a typical robotics Linux system <Cite id="px4-2015" />.

<Image id="dji-mavic-pro-in-flight" />

### Perception latency bounds the whole system

Falanga, Kim and Scaramuzza asked how fast a drone can fly given its perception latency and the acceleration its airframe can produce <Cite id="falanga-latency-2019" />. A drone at speed $v$ sees an obstacle at sensing range $s$, and its pipeline delays that information by latency $\tau$. Avoiding the obstacle at maximum lateral acceleration $u$ takes time proportional to the square root of obstacle size over $u$. If $s/v - \tau$ is shorter than the maneuver, no controller saves the drone <Cite id="falanga-latency-2019" />.

A 70 ms stereo pipeline, the upper bound the study took from a commercial camera's datasheet, supports about 19 m/s at 25 m/s² of lateral acceleration and 25 m/s at 50 m/s² <Cite id="falanga-latency-2019" />. An event camera reports per-pixel brightness changes without waiting for a frame. At 8 m of range its ceiling is 7 percent higher on the least agile airframe and 22 percent higher at 50 m/s², 31.03 against 25.40 m/s. The paper's own summary of 7 to 12 percent is for its most agile airframe, at 200 m/s², against the fastest stereo camera <Cite id="falanga-latency-2019" />.

Motion can also preserve the information the camera needs. PAMPC optimizes a point's visibility and motion in the image while respecting the quadrotor's dynamics and input limits <Cite id="pampc-2018" />.

In 2020 an event-camera quadrotor dodged fast-moving objects using only onboard sensing and computation <Cite id="falanga-event-avoidance-2020" />. Vision-language-action flight is far slower: RaceVLA averaged 1.04 m/s with a top speed of 2.02 m/s <Cite id="racevla-2025" />. On the CognitiveDrone benchmark RaceVLA succeeded 31.3 percent of the time, and CognitiveDrone-R1, which adds a reasoning module, 77.2 percent <Cite id="cognitivedrone-2025" />.

Jaewoo Lee, Guanya Shi and colleagues at Seoul National University, Carnegie Mellon and elsewhere (October 2026) let a coding agent that programs an aerial manipulator run diagnostic programs in simulation, such as a camera move or a test lift, before it declares a task done <Cite id="fly-by-code-2026" />. Over six simulated tasks and 60 trials per condition, the authors report 75 percent success against 31.7 percent with execution logs and final images <Cite id="fly-by-code-2026" />. Unmodified, the programs completed 4 of 5 real two-object pick-and-place trials and 3 of 5 cabinet trials <Cite id="fly-by-code-2026" />.

### End-to-end learning skips the interfaces

Real failures can supply supervision too. Learning to Fly by Crashing collected 11,500 crashes and combined the failed approaches with successful portions of the same trajectories to train a navigation policy <Cite id="learning-crash-2017" />.

Deep Drone Acrobatics trained a policy entirely in simulation by imitating an optimal controller with privileged information, and flew maneuvers at up to 3 g <Cite id="deep-drone-acrobatics-2020" />. In 2021 Loquercio and colleagues used the same recipe to map noisy depth images directly to collision-free trajectories <Cite id="high-speed-flight-2021" />. With realistic simulated sensor noise, the policy transferred to forests, snow, derailed trains and collapsed buildings with no additional training. The authors argue that separating sensing, mapping and planning "can be problematic for high-speed navigation in cluttered environments" because latency compounds and errors propagate <Cite id="high-speed-flight-2021" />.

Swift kept a modular front end: a visual-inertial estimator and a gate-detection network feed a Kalman filter, and a small two-layer RL network maps that state to collective thrust and body rates <Cite id="swift-drone-racing-2023" />. Later systems drop explicit state estimation. Geles and colleagues fly from pixels with the thrust and body-rate commands human pilots use <Cite id="geles-pixels-2024" />, and Dream to Fly learned racing from pixels with a world model where PPO and SAC struggled <Cite id="dream-to-fly-2025" />.

MonoRace keeps a state estimator, but its network skips inner-loop controllers and sends motor commands at 500 Hz <Cite id="monorace-2026" />. Training through differentiable physics produced a depth-to-control policy that flies forests at up to 20 m/s on a \$21 computer <Cite id="zhang-diff-physics-2025" />.

## Swarm robotics

## Impedance control: making contact a design variable

A stiff position-controlled arm driven into a surface 2 mm nearer than modeled turns that error into stored collision energy. Hogan's 1985 <Term id="impedance-control">impedance control</Term> instead commands the relationship between force and motion, so the arm presents a programmable mass-spring-damper: at a contact, a controller commands force or velocity, and the environment fixes the other <Cite id="hogan-1985" />.

Salisbury's earlier Cartesian stiffness controller programmed apparent stiffness along three translation and three rotation axes, transforming the Cartesian relation into joint-servo commands <Cite id="salisbury-1980" />.

<Term id="admittance-control">Admittance control</Term> is the dual: measure force with a wrist sensor and command motion. A backdrivable direct-drive arm realizes an impedance directly, while a stiff geared arm with a force-torque sensor runs admittance in software. ## The policy-to-controller contract

A learned action reaches the motors through a lower controller, so request type, rate, horizon, frame and saturation behavior belong to the interface. Peng and van de Panne showed that the action parameterization, from torques to target joint angles, affects learning, robustness and motion quality <Cite id="peng-action-space-2016" />, and the same Cartesian delta behaves differently in contact under a position controller and under an impedance controller.

The VICES study makes impedance itself part of the RL action: the policy selects end-effector motion and compliance, evaluated on tasks including door opening and surface wiping <Cite id="martin-martin-2019" />.

Deployed stacks are multi-rate: Berkeley Humanoid runs its RL policy at 50 Hz, its state estimator at 1 kHz and its PD controller at 25 kHz <Cite id="berkeley-humanoid-2024" />.

Model latency is part of the loop: a 3-billion-parameter VLA spends 46 ms on KV-cache prefill alone on an RTX 4090 <Cite id="real-time-chunking-2025" />. Deadline handling and hard bounds therefore sit outside the model, holding or stopping the robot when inference is late or an action is out of bounds. Data-driven controllers often lack well-understood guarantees, which motivates separate safety filters <Cite id="safety-filter-2023" />. The [action-space guide](/manipulation/action-spaces) covers interface choice.

Three queries separate the rungs: whether a cell is free for a planner, which way a surface faces for a contact solver, and what the scene looks like from a viewpoint the sensor never occupied. Cadena and colleagues judge representations by storage size, construction cost and usefulness for the task <Cite id="cadena-2016" />.

### Point clouds and occupancy grids

A <Term id="point-cloud">point cloud</Term> is an unordered set of 3D points, and PointNet requires invariance to the order in which they arrive <Cite id="pointnet-2017" />. A region without points is either empty or unobserved, and the store cannot say which. CUT3R maintains a recurrent state while processing an image sequence and predicts metric pointmaps in a shared frame, including inferred views that were not directly observed <Cite id="cut3r-2025" />.

Moravec and Elfes projected wide-angle sonar readings from different sensors and robot positions onto a 2D <Term id="occupancy-grid">occupancy grid</Term>. Each reading marked a probably empty beam interior and an uncertain reflecting point near the measured range, and overlapping readings refined these constraints. Zero represented unknown occupancy, and negative and positive values probably empty and probably occupied cells <Cite id="moravec-elfes-1985" />. OctoMap carries the three states into 3D in a compressed octree <Cite id="octomap-2013" />. Step through the figure below to see one mug stored four ways.

Curless and Levoy fuse range images into a cumulative weighted <Term id="signed-distance-field">signed distance function</Term> and recover the surface at its zero crossing, truncating distance ramps and weights near observed points. Their hole-filling construction marks empty space with negative $D_{min}$ and unseen space with positive $D_{max}$, both at zero weight <Cite id="curless-levoy-1996" />. KinectFusion uses the opposite sign: positive toward visible free space and negative on the non-visible side <Cite id="kinectfusion-2011" />.

KinectFusion fused 11-bit, 640×480 Kinect depth frames at 30 Hz, tracking each frame against the global model by coarse-to-fine ICP and mapping at the sensor rate on a commodity GPU. A large plane filling most of the view can cause drift or tracking failure. Its projective TSDF caps visible-space values at the truncation distance $\mu$, leaves non-visible points beyond $\mu$ unmeasured and is exact at the surface, so fusion yields an approximate pseudo-Euclidean distance. Normals come from numerical derivatives near the zero level set, and ray marching finds surfaces by trilinear interpolation <Cite id="kinectfusion-2011" />.

Voxel hashing stores dense surface data only near observed regions and streams blocks through a spatial hash table, avoiding a fixed dense volume over the entire scene <Cite id="voxel-hashing-2013" />.

<Image id="kinect-xbox-360-sensor" />

Trajectory optimizers need obstacle distances. Voxblox builds TSDFs faster than OctoMap builds its maps, then derives Euclidean signed distance fields (ESDFs) from them incrementally, more accurately than from occupancy <Cite id="voxblox-2016" />, and on GPUs nvblox reports up to 177x faster surface reconstruction and 31x faster distance-field computation <Cite id="nvblox-2023" />.

### Meshes, and then neural fields

A mesh adds connectivity, giving each face a normal and a renderable surface, but leaves holes where nothing was observed, and filling them invents geometry <Cite id="curless-levoy-1996" />.

NeRF fits a <Term id="neural-radiance-field">neural radiance field</Term> to a static scene from posed RGB photographs, intrinsics and scene bounds. Its MLP predicts density from position and colour from position and viewing direction, and differentiable volume rendering lets image error drive optimization <Cite id="nerf-2020" />. NeRF++ analyzes shape-radiance ambiguity and adapts the parameterization for 360-degree captures of unbounded scenes <Cite id="nerfpp-2020" />.

Instant NGP cut optimization cost with a multiresolution hash encoding, smaller networks and fully fused CUDA kernels, and rendered one scene at 1080p in 5 seconds over 128 samples and a large 360-degree scene at 10 frames per second on one RTX 3090 <Cite id="instant-ngp-2022" />. <Term id="gaussian-splatting">3D Gaussian splatting</Term> optimizes Gaussian positions, anisotropic covariances, opacities and spherical-harmonic appearance from calibrated photographs, then rasterizes by alpha-blending sorted splats. It reports real-time 1080p rendering, with results on an A6000 GPU <Cite id="3dgs-2023" />.

DUSt3R predicts dense pointmaps from a pair of RGB images without intrinsics or poses, in the first image's frame and at unknown scale, trained with geometric supervision from pretrained CroCo weights. For an image collection, it then optimizes the alignment of pairwise pointmaps in 3D <Cite id="dust3r-2024" />.

MASt3R adds matching descriptors to this 3D reconstruction approach and uses a fast reciprocal-matching procedure to obtain image correspondences <Cite id="mast3r-2024" />.

Feed-forward models now cover whole collections: VGGT infers cameras, point maps, depth maps and point tracks from one, a few or hundreds of views in under one second <Cite id="vggt-2025" />.

MapAnything accepts optional intrinsics, poses or depth alongside images and predicts metric geometry through separate depth, ray, camera and scale factors <Cite id="mapanything-2025" />. Pi3 avoids privileging one input view: its reconstruction is permutation-equivariant, with affine-invariant camera poses and scale-invariant local pointmaps <Cite id="pi3-2025" />.

Depth Anything 3 uses a depth-and-ray prediction target for arbitrary view collections, whether or not camera poses are supplied <Cite id="depth-anything-3-2025" />.

## A radiance field is geometry for rendering

The [world-models taxonomy](/world-models/taxonomy) treats a splat reconstruction as a learned renderer: appearance is learned and physics is not. In the original 3DGS, learned opacity is an image-space alpha-compositing weight with no free, occupied or unknown label, and the stored primitive is a volumetric Gaussian <Cite id="3dgs-2023" />. The paper names mesh reconstruction as an open direction <Cite id="3dgs-2023" />, and SuGaR then aligned Gaussians with surfaces and extracted meshes by Poisson reconstruction <Cite id="sugar-2023" />. 2D Gaussian Splatting instead uses oriented planar disks, ray-splat intersections and depth-distortion and normal regularizers to improve surface reconstruction <Cite id="2dgs-2024" />.

Simulators pair splats for appearance with separate physics: SplatSim renders with splats while PyBullet supplies physics <Cite id="splatsim-2024" />. Its authors report zero-shot real-world transfer of diffusion policies on four rigid-body tasks with a UR5 and Robotiq 2F-85 gripper, after manual robot segmentation and ICP alignment <Cite id="splatsim-2024" />. In RoboGSim's closed-loop evaluator, a policy acts on splat-rendered images while Isaac Sim handles inverse kinematics and physical interaction, from multi-view images, supplied MDH parameters and mesh assets <Cite id="robogsim-2024" />.

Other fields serve a planner directly. Dex-NeRF renders transparency-aware depth from learned density for a grasp planner, where a RealSense camera failed to compute depth for most transparent objects tested <Cite id="dex-nerf-2021" />. F3RM distills 2D foundation-model features into a 3D feature field so that language and a few demonstrations can guide grasping and placing <Cite id="f3rm-2023" />.

ParticleSplat, from Deepak Pathak (Carnegie Mellon) and colleagues (September 2026), encodes posed multi-view images into latent particles that decode to 3D Gaussians, trained with a novel-view synthesis objective. Object masks emerge without labels, moving a particle moves its object, and the representation improved downstream manipulation <Cite id="particlesplat-2026" />.

[State estimation](/classical/state-estimation) covers the inference machinery.

<LoopClosure className="my-6" />

<Term id="place-recognition">Place recognition</Term> asks whether the current image matches a stored place, and motion information can also inform that belief. Viewpoint, illumination and seasonal changes alter one place's appearance, and different places can look alike, which is perceptual aliasing <Cite id="lowry-2016-place-recognition" />. AnyLoc builds place descriptors by aggregating frozen self-supervised features, without training a network specifically for visual place recognition <Cite id="anyloc-2023" />.

Perceptual aliasing can create false-positive associations that corrupt back-end estimates, while false negatives discard useful measurements. Robust losses and loop-closure validation mitigate outliers, though failures remain that depend on initialization <Cite id="cadena-2016" />. Graduated non-convexity offers another route: it gradually sharpens a robust objective while using non-minimal solvers, avoiding a required initial guess in the tested estimation problems <Cite id="gnc-2019" />.

In the back end, Square Root SAM estimates the trajectory and landmark map jointly by MAP inference, which under Gaussian models with known data associations is sparse nonlinear least squares. It solves successive linearized systems by QR or Cholesky, and variable ordering controls fill-in <Cite id="dellaert-kaess-2006" />. iSAM2 adds incremental reordering and relinearization on a Bayes tree. Thresholded updates trade some accuracy for speed, and a large loop closure can cost as much as a batch solve <Cite id="kaess-2012" />.

Smoothing suits loop closure because relinearizing the past requires the past to stay in the graph. Cadena and colleagues contrast sparse landmark maps with dense models suited to obstacle avoidance, and cite octrees and voxel hashing as efficient volumetric storage. Two rooms can look identical to a 2D laser yet differ to a camera. Severe illumination changes defeat bag-of-words methods, and active range cameras work in dark, untextured scenes but face range and external-light limits <Cite id="cadena-2016" />.

The iMAP system learns a scene-specific MLP from scratch at room scale from a handheld RGB-D stream. It tracks at 10 Hz and maps at 2 Hz on a desktop CPU and GPU, retaining keyframes for replay <Cite id="imap-2021" />. NICE-SLAM uses hierarchical feature grids with pretrained geometry decoders, reconstructs a multi-room apartment and performs no loop closure <Cite id="nice-slam-2022" />. Navigation2, built on ROS 2, uses a layered costmap. Its global planner computes a shortest route to the goal, and a separate controller computes a local path and control signals, each a plugin in an asynchronous server <Cite id="nav2-2020" />.

Hydra stacks rungs in one real-time system, building a local ESDF, extracting a topological map of places from it and segmenting places into rooms <Cite id="hydra-2022" />.

ConceptFusion fuses pixel-aligned foundation-model features into a 3D map that can be queried through text, images, audio or geometry, without additional training <Cite id="conceptfusion-2023" />.

The mean moves through the true maps $g$ and $h$; only the covariance takes the linearized route <Cite id="thrun-2005" />. The Ames group moved from linearizing about a nominal reference trajectory to relinearizing about the *current estimated state*, which they hoped would bring "substantial advantages". An accidentally off-nominal simulation converged after initial overshoots, and the report names this modification the extended Kalman filter. It also discusses instability from round-off, inadequate statistical models and nonlinearities <Cite id="mcgee-schmidt-1985" />.

Linearization holds near the estimate, which is itself uncertain, so where the nonlinearity is strong over the region the covariance covers, $\Sigma$ stops describing the true error, and the filter grows overconfident and can diverge <Cite id="mcgee-schmidt-1985" /><Cite id="dellaert-kaess-2006" />. Julier and Uhlmann summarize 35 years of experience: the EKF is difficult to implement and tune, and reliable only for systems almost linear on the time scale of the updates <Cite id="julier-uhlmann-2004" />. Li and Mourikis proved that standard EKF visual-inertial odometry is inconsistent because of how its Jacobians are computed, so it underestimates its uncertainty <Cite id="li-mourikis-2013" />.

<LinearizationGap className="my-6" />

The unscented Kalman filter of Julier and Uhlmann keeps the Gaussian and pushes deterministically chosen sample points through the true nonlinearity <Cite id="julier-uhlmann-1997" />. Particle filters drop the Gaussian assumption and carry the belief as a set of particles <Cite id="thrun-2005" />.

Invariant filters on Lie groups remove the dependence on the estimate: in the contact-aided invariant EKF, neither the linearized error dynamics nor the linearized observation model depends on the current state estimate <Cite id="hartley-inekf-2019" />. EqVIO applies an equivariant filter to visual-inertial odometry, using the system's symmetries to reduce linearization error and improve consistency <Cite id="eqvio-2022" />.

Cadena and colleagues describe a classical SLAM period from 1986 to 2004, with EKF, Rao-Blackwellised particle-filter and maximum-likelihood approaches, and an algorithmic-analysis period from 2004 to 2015 <Cite id="cadena-2016" />. In Rao-Blackwellized grid mapping, each particle carries its own map <Cite id="grisetti-gmapping-2007" />.

Smith, Self and Cheeseman's stochastic map stores estimated spatial relationships together with their uncertainties and updates them incrementally as measurements arrive <Cite id="smith-1990" />.

The survey treats MAP estimation, often over factor graphs, as the de facto standard but notes EKF systems with state-of-the-art performance. The gap shrinks when EKF linearization is accurate, sliding windows are used and inconsistency is addressed, and graphs still face unbounded growth and information loss under sparsification <Cite id="cadena-2016" />. The MSCKF sliding-window filter keeps 3D feature positions out of the state and is optimal up to linearization errors <Cite id="msckf-2007" />, while OKVIS argues that nonlinear optimization offers superior accuracy and stays tractable through sparsity <Cite id="okvis-2014" />. [Scene representation and mapping](/classical/scene-representation) covers what a robot keeps from the estimate.

## Where this meets the learned stack

Learned components mostly enter classical estimators as measurements with uncertainty. TLIO regresses 3D displacement and its uncertainty from IMU data and fuses both into a stochastic cloning EKF <Cite id="tlio-2020" />, and MAC-VO learns a metrics-aware keypoint covariance and uses it to weight pose graph optimization <Cite id="mac-vo-2024" />.

Backprop KF makes the filter itself differentiable, representing its belief-parameter updates as a computation graph that can be trained from raw observations <Cite id="backprop-kf-2016" />.

AirIO preserves body-frame IMU measurements and encodes attitude, combining learned IMU correction with an uncertainty-aware EKF for aerial robots <Cite id="airio-2025" />.

## DROID: depth on one platform

DROID's distinction is scene and site diversity: 76,000 trajectories totaling 350 hours, across 564 scenes and 86 tasks, gathered by 50 operators at 13 institutions over 12 months <Cite id="droid-2024" />. Every trajectory came from one rig, a Franka Panda with two ZED 2 cameras and a ZED Mini wrist camera, [teleoperated](/data-hardware/teleop-rigs) through a Meta Quest 2. One platform gives one action space and one camera geometry, at the price of embodiment lock-in.

Single-platform collections can be larger. The Galaxea Open-World Dataset holds 500 hours across 50 scenes, all from one consistent robot embodiment <Cite id="galaxea-open-world-2025" />.

## RoboMIND: multi-embodiment under one protocol

RoboMIND's paper reports 107,000 successful trajectories totaling 305.5 interaction hours across 479 tasks and 96 object classes. The cohort mixes real-world and simulated demonstrations for four embodiments, a Franka Emika Panda, a UR5e, an AgileX dual-arm robot and a humanoid with dual dexterous hands, under one collection platform and standardized protocol. It also releases 5,000 real-world failure demonstrations with annotated causes and a digital twin of its tasks in Isaac Sim <Cite id="robomind-2024" />.

RoboMIND 2.0 (December 2025) reports over 310K dual-arm trajectories from six embodiments and 739 tasks, including 12K tactile-enhanced episodes and 20K mobile manipulation trajectories <Cite id="robomind-2-2025" />. The [public dataset card](https://huggingface.co/datasets/x-humanoid-robomind/RoboMIND) shows an Apache-2.0 tag but makes users accept access conditions before downloading, so check the terms before commercial use <Cite id="robomind-dataset-card" />.

## How to read dataset claims

Hours compare better than episodes. DROID averages about 17 seconds per trajectory and AgiBot World Beta about 11, so a large episode count can hide less interaction than a smaller set of long tasks ([the data bottleneck](/data-hardware/data-bottleneck)). The 2025 BEHAVIOR Challenge supplies 10,000 teleoperated demonstrations totaling 1,200+ hours <Cite id="behavior-challenge-2025" />, and the synthetic InternData-A1 holds over 630k trajectories and 7,433 hours <Cite id="interndata-a1-2025" />.

Modalities differ as much as size. RH20T records visual, force, audio and action data in over 110,000 contact-rich sequences <Cite id="rh20t-2023" />. Humanoid Everyday adds depth, LiDAR and tactile streams to 10.3k humanoid trajectories across 260 tasks, with a cloud evaluation platform <Cite id="humanoid-everyday-2025" />. Scaling work finds task diversity worth more than per-task demonstration count, and multi-embodiment pretraining optional given high-quality single-embodiment data <Cite id="diversity-scaling-2025" />.
